# Initiative: Users can work with documents together inside Alkemio

> Enable users to upload, share, and collaboratively work with documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) inside Alkemio Spaces, attached to posts, organised as collections, and browsable via a file explorer.

---

## Outcome
Which OKR or Winning Move does this serve?

- Winning Move 4: Support How Work Actually Happens
- OKR delivery-ce-2: Customer Experience, Optimise Early User Journeys

---

## Problem / Opportunity
Teams using Alkemio for real collaboration inevitably work with documents: proposals, reports, analyses, and presentation materials. Crucially, most initiatives arrive on Alkemio with an existing history; they already have collections of documents from before they moved to the platform, and need a way to bring that material with them. Today there is no native way to attach, view, or co-work on these files inside a Space, forcing users to rely on external tools (Teams, SharePoint, Google Drive) and breaking the collaboration loop. This is a direct barrier to Alkemio becoming the place where work actually happens.

---

## Chosen Approach

**We will:** Allow users to upload and create Office documents and attach them to posts, either as additional content or as a named collection. Collaborative editing via Collabora is in scope. All files in a Space will be accessible via a file explorer view.

**We will NOT:** Build our own document editor or storage backend. We will not support arbitrary file types in the first iteration; focus is on the core Office formats. We will not build a standalone "Drive"-like experience decoupled from posts and Spaces.

**Rationale:** Anchoring documents to posts preserves the context in which files are shared, which is core to how collaboration on Alkemio is structured. A file explorer is a convenience layer on top of this, not a replacement. Avoiding a standalone drive keeps scope manageable and avoids positioning Alkemio as a storage tool rather than a collaboration tool.

---

## Scope

**In:**
- Upload and creation of .doc, .ppt, .xls files
- Attaching documents to posts as additional content or as a collection
- Collaborative editing via Collabora
- File explorer view scoped to a Space (no cross-Space view)

**Out:**
- Arbitrary file types (PDFs, images, video; separate initiative)
- Standalone document storage / drive experience decoupled from posts
- Document versioning
- Cross-Space file view

---

## Phasing and Success Criteria
How will we know each phase is done?

**POC**
- [x] Collabora integration live in a development environment
- [x] A single document can be attached to a post and opened for collaborative editing by all Space members

**MVP**
- [x] Users can create and upload .doc, .ppt, and .xls files to a post
- [x] Attached documents can be opened and collaboratively edited via Collabora
- [ ] Document usage is tracked so we can measure adoption and identify friction (linked to delivery-da-2)

**Full**
- [ ] File explorer view available per Space (no cross-Space view)
- [ ] Documents can be added to collections within a post
- [ ] Fine-grained edit permissions available: all members / admins / creator only
- [ ] View vs edit mode per file type (e.g. presentations open in presentation mode by default, with an explicit edit button)
- [ ] At least one key customer (e.g. Digicampus or KCI) actively using documents in their Space

---

## Key Assumptions & Risks

- [ ] Collaborative editing via **Collabora**; technical and commercial feasibility confirmed
- [ ] Users' mental model maps to "documents in posts" rather than expecting a drive-first experience; needs validation
- [ ] Storage and file size constraints are acceptable to key customers; needs early confirmation
- [ ] Digicampus / KCI beta feedback loop is available in time to inform iteration (linked to market-1 KR2)

---

## Dependencies
The collaborative editing capability depends on the Collabora integration; the technical implementation approach should be confirmed before detailed delivery planning begins. The instrumentation of document journeys depends on the user-journey mapping work in delivery-da-2 being sufficiently advanced.

---

## Sequencing Rationale
Documents is a prerequisite for Alkemio credibly supporting "how work actually happens" (WM4). Without it, key personas (programme coordinators, innovation facilitators) hit a hard ceiling in their daily workflows. It also provides concrete, testable functionality that can be validated with Digicampus and KCI during Q2/Q3, feeding the feature-feedback loop in market-1 KR2.
t: Documents

# Initiative: A modern, high-quality UI that makes users say "wow"

> Redesign the Alkemio frontend to deliver a visually impressive, modern experience that builds user confidence and reflects the quality of the platform, while modernising the underlying tech stack to support faster, AI-assisted development.

---

## Outcome
Which OKR or Winning Move does this serve?

- Winning Move 3: Persona-Driven Frontend Refresh & Mobile Journeys

---

## Problem / Opportunity
The existing UI looked outdated, which undermined user confidence in the platform and made a poor impression on potential customers and investors. At the same time, the current tech stack (MUI, Emotion, Formik) is ageing, lacks a coherent design system, and slows down development. A redesign addresses both: a visually modern interface that impresses users and prospects, built on a stack that supports AI-assisted design-to-code workflows and is easier to maintain and extend.

---

## Chosen Approach

**We will:** Replace the UI stack (MUI + Emotion with shadcn/ui + Tailwind; Formik + Zod with React Hook Form + Zod) and redesign the visual layer across all key pages, using a proper design system. UX is deliberately kept stable in this phase: layout and navigation patterns are preserved, but the look and feel is fully refreshed. The rollout will be gradual, with users able to opt in to the new UI before it becomes the default.

**We will NOT:** Redesign navigation or information architecture in this initiative; that requires separate validation. We will not build a dedicated mobile experience; the new UI must work and look consistent on mobile, but no mobile-specific effort beyond that. We will not maintain the old stack in parallel beyond the transition period.

**Rationale:** Decoupling visual redesign from UX restructuring reduces risk and allows us to ship a meaningful improvement faster. The stack choice (shadcn/ui + Tailwind) is driven by its compatibility with AI-assisted Figma-to-code workflows and its status as the current industry standard for design systems. Gradual rollout protects existing users while allowing early validation.

---

## Scope

**In:**
- Full visual redesign across all pages
- Tech stack migration: shadcn/ui + Tailwind, React Hook Form + Zod, hooks-first architecture
- Removal of unused and outdated dependencies
- A coherent design system as the foundation
- Mobile consistency (new UI works and looks good on mobile)
- Updated e2e tests to cover redesigned pages
- Gradual rollout: opt-in for existing users before becoming the default

**Out:**
- Navigation and information architecture changes (later initiative, needs validation)
- Mobile-specific features or layouts beyond consistency with web
- New or removed functionality (minor information additions/removals are acceptable)

---

## Phasing and Success Criteria
How will we know each phase is done?

**POC**
- [ ] Figma-to-shadcn/ui component export flow validated
- [ ] Key technical risks in stack migration identified and resolved
- [ ] At least one page live in a development environment in the new stack

**MVP**
_Good enough for power users and early adopters to opt in, explore the new direction, and provide feedback. Not yet the default._
- [ ] Core pages live in new UI: Homepage, Space, Subspace, Settings
- [ ] Existing users can opt in via avatar menu or profile settings; new UI is not yet the default

**Full**
- [ ] All remaining pages and dialogs live in new UI
- [ ] New UI is the default for new users (optional intermediate release)
- [ ] New UI is the default for all users, with a notification explaining the change and how to switch back
- [ ] Mobile consistency confirmed across all redesigned pages
- [ ] E2e tests updated for all redesigned pages
- [ ] Old stack fully removed

---

## Key Assumptions & Risks

- [ ] Figma-to-code flow with shadcn/ui works as expected; to be confirmed after PoC
- [ ] Gradual opt-in rollout is technically feasible (running old and new UI in parallel during transition)
- [ ] Existing users accept the visual change positively; risk of disruption managed via opt-in period and clear communication
- [ ] Mobile consistency can be achieved without dedicated mobile effort
- [ ] Newly onboarded communities should not have their UI switched immediately after onboarding; rollout timing needs to account for this

---

## Dependencies
The PoC must be completed before committing to full delivery scope. E2e test coverage depends on the quality work in delivery-quality OKRs being sufficiently advanced to absorb the redesigned pages. Change management for existing communities needs a separate plan before the new UI becomes the default; this initiative does not solve that, but the rollout cannot proceed without it.

---

## Sequencing Rationale
The outdated UI is an active liability: it affects user confidence and sales conversations now. WM3 explicitly calls for a frontend refresh for key personas. This initiative unblocks both the user experience improvement and the design system foundation that future product work (including AI-assisted development) depends on.
t: Client Redesign (Initiative)

## Description

Alkemio's identity story today is fragmented. Human users authenticate against Kratos, microservices receive identity through a separate mutator path, machine-to-machine traffic has no first-class mechanism, and the Matrix-based collaboration stack runs on its own auth assumptions. Each surface ends up with its own login shape, its own session lifetime, its own teardown semantics, and — most importantly — its own failure modes when something needs to be revoked, audited, or extended.

This epic converges every authentication and authorization flow across the Alkemio platform onto a single OIDC-based foundation. After it lands, a user signs in once, that one session is recognised by the web client, the API, the microservices, and the Matrix layer, and every action taken — by a person or by a service — is attributable to a single canonical actor.

This is the umbrella for the OIDC migration. It is intentionally scoped to the strategic outcomes; the per-component contracts, sequencing, and rollout details live in the child issues below.

## Goal

Move Alkemio from a patchwork of authentication mechanisms to one OIDC-native identity layer, so that the platform behaves consistently from a user's, an operator's, and a third-party integrator's point of view.

Concretely, the epic delivers four business outcomes:

1. **One sign-in, one session, every surface.** A user authenticates once and that identity flows through the web client, the GraphQL API, every microservice, and the Matrix-backed collaboration stack — including chat — without per-surface re-authentication or per-surface session quirks.
2. **Users control their own sessions.** Members can see where they are signed in, revoke any individual session, and sign out of all devices in one click — without contacting support and without waiting for absolute session timeouts to expire.
3. **First-class non-human callers.** Partners, scheduled jobs, data pipelines, and internal automation can obtain credentials that authenticate the *service itself*, instead of borrowing a real person's login and breaking when that person leaves or rotates their password.
4. **A simpler, more auditable platform.** Authentication consolidates onto one industry-standard shape (`forwardAuth`-style identity resolution) across all protected routes. Embedded signing keys, bespoke identity hops, and divergent session models are retired. Every action — human or service — produces a single, attributable audit trail.

## Hypothesis

We believe that converging the platform onto OIDC will measurably reduce the cost of running, extending, and securing Alkemio. We expect to see:

- **Fewer auth-related incidents and support tickets.** Today's three-shapes-in-parallel model produces recurring "why am I signed out?", "why doesn't this integration work after a password change?", and "why does Matrix think I'm someone else?" reports. One shape should make these largely disappear.
- **Shorter lead time for new integrations.** A partner or internal team that today needs a human-account workaround to call the API non-interactively will, after this epic, complete the same integration in a documented, supported flow without engineering escort.
- **Faster, cleaner incident response.** A user who suspects a session is compromised will resolve it themselves in seconds; an operator revoking access for a departing collaborator will be a single, well-audited action rather than a multi-system dance.
- **Lower long-term maintenance surface.** Removing the bespoke identity-injection layer, retiring committed signing keys, and collapsing three middleware shapes into one removes a measurable amount of code, configuration, and operational tribal knowledge from the platform.

Leading indicators we will track:

- Share of protected routes served by the unified identity-resolution middleware (target: 100% by epic completion).
- Number of distinct authentication code paths in the platform (target: trends downward each release; reaches one by epic completion).
- Adoption of the machine-to-machine credential flow by internal jobs and external integrations (target: every non-interactive caller migrated off human-account workarounds).
- User-initiated session revocations per month (a proxy for whether the self-service surface is discoverable and trusted).

## Must-have scope

The following capabilities are required for the epic to be considered complete. Each is independently shippable; together they constitute the OIDC convergence.

- **One sign-in across every user-facing surface.** A user authenticates once and that identity is recognised by the web client, the GraphQL API, every microservice, and the Matrix-backed collaboration stack — including chat. Password-based access to the collaboration backend is retired in the process.
- **A single canonical identity contract consumed by every downstream service.** All microservices read identity from the same source, in the same shape, with the same trust assumptions — no per-service authentication quirks, no per-service token-decoding code paths.
- **A single identity-resolution shape on every protected route.** Every protected route resolves the caller's identity through one standard, vendor-neutral middleware pattern. Inherited per-route bespoke proxies are retired, the embedded signing key that came with the legacy identity layer is removed, and the per-request message-bus hop currently sitting on the WebSocket hot path is eliminated.
- **Self-service session management for end users.** Members can view every session they have open across devices and browsers, revoke any individual session, sign out of all other devices in one click, and sign out everywhere in one click — without contacting support and without waiting for absolute session timeouts to expire.
- **An OAuth scope model that composes with the platform's authorization framework.** A documented, reasoned answer to how scopes interact with the platform's existing credential-based authorization — whether they constrain it, layer on top of it, or remain a thin protocol-level detail — with the decision implemented across the token-issuing and token-validating surfaces.
- **First-class credentials for non-interactive callers.** A registered service can obtain an access token that authenticates the *service itself*, with its own identity, its own scoped permissions, and its own audit trail — independent of any human user. Administrators can register, list, rotate the credentials of, and revoke service clients; revocation takes effect immediately for both new token requests and already-issued tokens.
- **A consolidated audit trail across every actor type.** Every action — whether taken by a human user, a service, or an automation — produces a single, attributable audit event with a single canonical actor identifier, ready for export to enterprise audit pipelines.
- **A reusable test surface for the OIDC authentication pipeline.** Behavioural invariants on the auth pipeline (absolute-TTL expiry, refresh-teardown, invalid-credentials rejection, missing-claim rejection, store-unavailable surface, service-principal admission) are pinned by fast, deterministic, CI-gated tests rather than manual walkthroughs. This is what lets every subsequent change to the auth pipeline ship safely and quickly.
- **Operational documentation and migration guidance.** A documented path for service-client maintainers, integrators, and operators covering how to register clients, how to obtain and use tokens, how to rotate credentials, how to interpret audit events, and what changes for end users at cutover.

## What this unlocks

Completion of this epic is a prerequisite for several initiatives the business has already articulated demand for but cannot reasonably scope while authentication is fragmented:

- **A public / partner API and SDK story.** Without first-class machine-to-machine credentials and a defensible scope model, every external integration is bespoke. With them, Alkemio can expose a documented, scoped API surface to partners and ecosystem builders.
- **Operator-initiated security actions** — admin force-revoke of a user's sessions, account-event cascades (deactivation, password change, role change → token invalidation across every surface), and per-RP / per-scope revocation. The self-service work in #6073 is the foundation; the operator-facing equivalents become tractable on top of it.
- **A consistent audit and compliance posture.** Every action — by a human, a service, an automation — produces one canonical audit event with one canonical actor identifier, suitable for export to enterprise audit pipelines that procurement and security reviews regularly ask for.
- **Future infrastructure flexibility.** Once every protected route uses the same standard identity-resolution shape, moving Alkemio onto a service mesh, a different ingress, or a managed identity provider becomes a configuration change rather than a re-architecture.
- **A coherent story for the Matrix-based collaboration stack.** Chat, whiteboards, and collaborative documents stop being identity islands; access to them follows the same revoke/sign-out semantics as the rest of the platform.

## Stakeholders

- **Product & Engineering — Atlas team:** primary delivery team; owners of `alkemio-server`, `alkemio-client-web`, `oidc-service`, and the deployment surface.
- **Platform / DevOps:** owners of the ingress and orchestration layer; needed for the identity-resolution middleware rollout and the retirement of the inherited identity proxy.
- **Security:** consulted on the scope model (#6075), the audit-event shape, the machine-to-machine credential surface (#6077), and the self-service revocation flow (#6073).
- **Customer Success:** kept informed of the user-facing changes (single sign-in across surfaces, the new session-management page, the new "sign out everywhere" affordance) so that customer-facing communications and help-centre articles land alongside the rollout.
- **Partner / Integrations stakeholders:** consulted on the machine-to-machine credential flow (#6077) as the first non-human integration story the platform supports natively.

## Design

Figma file: _to be added during refinement_

User-visible surfaces that need design alignment:

- The session-management page introduced by #6073 (entry point in the account / security area; per-row revoke; page-level "sign out of all other devices" and "sign out everywhere").
- The admin-only registration UX for service clients introduced by #6077 (creating a client, the one-time secret reveal, rotation, revocation, scope assignment).
- Any messaging that surfaces around the single-sign-in convergence — particularly the first time a user notices that signing out of the web client also signs them out of chat.

_Comments are highly appreciated. When commenting in Figma, please also leave a note in the comments box below this issue to notify us._

## Goal

One place to track the **agent-platform work**: giving the platform an AI-assistant capability that is safe by construction — a first-class assistant **identity**, user **impersonation done right** (delegation, never privilege escalation), a governed **MCP tool surface**, the **assistant** itself (backend + UI), its deployment, and cost control.

Workspace specs (source of truth): [`specs/004-web-ai-assistant`](https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/004-web-ai-assistant/specs/004-web-ai-assistant) · [`specs/006-whiteboard-live-external-writes`](https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/004-web-ai-assistant/specs/006-whiteboard-live-external-writes)

## Themes

| Theme | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Identity** | A `virtual-assistant` platform actor (CTI child of Actor) every assistant action is attributed to — never an anonymous bot |
| **Impersonation / delegation** | User-initiated work authorizes **as the user** (same `AuthorizationService` as GraphQL ⇒ effective ⊆ user privileges by construction) while attributed to the assistant; system-invoked work authorizes as the actor under an admin-granted, read-only-by-default capability grant |
| **MCP** | The platform tool surface (11 tools) behind a per-tool capability gate: per-user toggles (reads on, writes off by default), frozen read/write classification with an unknown⇒write fail-safe, parity-tested on both sides |
| **Assistant backend** | `assistant-service` (Python FastAPI + LangGraph): SSE streaming, durable write-confirmation gate (nothing writes unconfirmed), measured token budgets, full audit trail |
| **Assistant UI** | Global panel + whiteboard-docked rail, capability settings, consolidated write confirmations — flag OFF until rollout |
| **Whiteboard live sync** | External (assistant/MCP) content writes push live into open boards instead of requiring a reload |
| **Cost control** | Measured-token accounting, prompt caching, tool-result diet; next: entitlement-mapped budgets + monthly metering (FR-027/FR-028) |

## Delivery

Stories are sub-issues below, one per slice, each cross-referencing its PR(s). Rollout order (constitution §4): server → assistant-service → infra-ops[ACC] → dev-orchestration → client-web → infra-ops[PROD] (after human gates: stakeholder approval, QA sign-off, DPA/ZDR).

Today the two scheduled jobs jump through hoops purely to satisfy authorization: the `inapp-notifications-prune` job runs a 3-step Kratos login flow to mint a bearer token, and `alkemio-search-ingest` leans on the `alkemio/cli` image to broker auth. For a trusted in-cluster caller these add no value and force admin credentials to live in jobs. An internal endpoint, reachable only inside the cluster (never via the public ingress) and constrained to authorized workloads, removes that whole dance.

The existing authenticated GraphQL mutations stay; the internal surface is **additive** and shares the same underlying logic so behavior cannot diverge.

## Affected repos

- **server** (lead) — expose the internal endpoints invoking the existing prune/ingest logic.
- **infrastructure-operations** — rewire both cron jobs onto the internal endpoints, drop the credential exchange, constrain network access (acceptance + production).

## Acceptance criteria (from spec Success Criteria)

- Both jobs trigger their operation with **zero** admin credentials / identity-provider login steps.
- Internal-endpoint path and GraphQL-mutation path produce the **same** outcome (data removed / indices rebuilt).
- Endpoints are **not reachable from outside the cluster** (100% of external attempts fail to reach them).
- Search-ingest trigger returns in **< 5s** (stays async/fire-and-forget); prune returns its removed-counts within the job's run window.
- An underlying-operation failure marks the calling job **failed** — no false-positive successes.
- Both jobs keep their existing schedules with no regression in maintenance outcomes.

## Out of scope

Any admin capability beyond the two named operations; changing the operations' behavior/schedule; removing the GraphQL mutations; adding auth to the internal surface.

t: Internal admin jobs API — no-auth in-cluster endpoint for prune & search-ingest

Part of epic #1900 (Web AI Assistant). Builds on Increment B metering (#1908, FR-028).

## Description

As a platform operator, I want to **observe assistant events and usage** so that I can understand adoption, cost, and tool behaviour from **statistical** data — without ever capturing PII or message content.

## Goal

Emit structured, privacy-safe usage telemetry for the assistant: one event per request **and** a separate event per tool call, each carrying the token cost, queryable/aggregatable in our existing observability stack.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Every assistant request** (one conversation turn / agent invocation) emits a structured usage event
- [ ] **Every MCP tool call emits its own separate event** — tool name, capability, read/write kind, outcome (ok/error), latency
- [ ] **Token consumption is captured** on the request data point: input/prompt, output/completion, total tokens, model; cached-vs-billed split where the provider exposes it. Attribute tokens to tool-call events where meaningful.
- [ ] **No message content** in any data point — dimensional/statistical only: actor + space references, enums, counts, durations, token counts. **Raw actor/space UUIDs are acceptable** (decided 2026-06-20 — no hashing/pseudonymisation required).
- [ ] Events are **queryable and aggregatable** for statistics — by user/space/tool/model/capability/time window — in the existing observability stack (Elastic APM / ES)
- [ ] Schema + retention documented; reconciled with the **metering** data from Increment B (#1908) and the assistant **audit trail** (FR-010) so we don't double-count or diverge

## Affected repos

`assistant-service` (emits per-request + per-tool-call events with token usage from the agent loop) · `server` (MCP host already logs tool/resource execution — extend to the PII-free event schema) · possibly `infrastructure-operations` (observability sink/retention config)

## Decisions

- **Identifiers:** raw actor/space UUIDs are acceptable in the telemetry — no hashing required (2026-06-20).

## Open questions

- Destination: reuse the metering store (Increment B), Elastic APM, or a dedicated ES index/data-stream?
- Exact dimension set + retention period (align with ISO 27001 A.8.15 logging policy, alkem-io/alkemio#1791).
t: [Assistant] Observability — per-call & per-tool-call usage events (PII-free, token-costed)

Part of epic #1900 (Web AI Assistant). Builds on Increment B metering & entitlement budgets (#1908, FR-027b/FR-028).

## Description

As a global admin, I want to be **notified when a user approaches 90% of their monthly token quota**, so that I can act before they hit the cap — delivered over my chosen channels.

## Goal

Detect the 90% monthly-usage threshold from the metering data and dispatch a notification to global admins over the platform's notification channels, with sensible per-admin defaults.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a user's **monthly assistant token usage crosses 90%** of their quota, a notification is dispatched to **global admins**
- [ ] Fires **once per user per period** at the threshold — idempotent / debounced, no repeat spam within the same month
- [ ] **Channels:** email, in-app, PWA push — all supported
  - [ ] **Email: opt-out, ON by default**
  - [ ] **In-app: OFF by default**
  - [ ] **PWA push: OFF by default**
- [ ] Per-admin channel preferences exposed in **notification settings**
- [ ] Threshold (90%) and the quota value are sourced from Increment B metering/entitlement (#1908) — single source of truth, no re-derivation
- [ ] Implemented via the existing `notifications` service patterns; no PII beyond what the notification needs

## Decisions

- **Recipient: global admins only.** The user themselves is **not** notified — their live usage is already in front of them in the chat window (the budget meter), so a user-facing quota notification is unnecessary (decided 2026-06-20).

## Open questions

- Is the 90% threshold fixed or configurable?
- "Approaching" semantics — evaluate on each metered request, or on a periodic sweep?
t: [Assistant] Quota notifications — alert global admins at 90% of monthly token quota

**Nice-to-have follow-up to #1918 (token efficiency). Not urgent — can ship independently after the v1 assistant lands.**

## Problem
Every assistant turn currently runs on the large model (`mistral-large-latest`), including turns that do **no tool use and need little reasoning**: greetings, clarifying questions, language-only replies, "thanks", short factual answers. Those turns pay large-model input *and* output price (output is 3× input on Mistral) for work a smaller model handles fine.

#1918 already cut the input side hard — tool-surface trimming (−61% tool tokens on read/chat turns) and prompt caching (warm prefix at 0.1×). Model routing attacks the **remaining** cost: the per-token rate and latency on simple turns. It's a *smaller marginal win after those two*, which is why it's split out as a follow-up rather than bundled into #1918.

## Proposal
Route a turn to a **small model** (e.g. `mistral-small-latest`) when it's unlikely to need the large model, and keep the large model for tool-using / reasoning-heavy turns. Cheap signals already computed per turn:
- **No tools bound** after the #1918 relevance gate (a plain read/chat turn with no whiteboard relevance) → strong candidate for the small model.
- First-iteration only: if the model *does* decide to call a tool, escalate to the large model for the tool-using continuation (two-tier within a turn), so capability is never lost — only the cheap first hop is downgraded.

Implementation seam: the existing `app/agent/provider.py` factory + the `LLMProvider`/model config — add a `ASSISTANT_LLM_MODEL_SMALL` (or per-tier) setting and a routing decision in the turn runner, keyed off the tool-binding result.

## Why nice-to-have (not now)
- The big savings are already banked by trimming + caching (#1918).
- Routing adds real complexity: a second model config, a routing decision, quality risk on misrouted turns, and escalation logic to avoid capability loss. That cost/benefit only makes sense once v1 is stable and we have prod usage data showing the no-tool-turn share.
- It's provider-coupled (Mistral small/large; different on Anthropic/OpenAI), so it should follow the provider decision for prod.

## Acceptance criteria (sketch)
- [ ] No-tool turns run on the small model; tool-using turns on the large model — verified by per-turn logs (model id alongside the existing `turn usage:` line).
- [ ] No capability regression: a turn that needs a tool still completes correctly (escalation path covered by a test).
- [ ] Configurable + reversible: a single setting disables routing (always-large), mirroring `ASSISTANT_TRIM_TOOL_SURFACE`.
- [ ] Measured: report the cost/latency delta on a sample of no-tool turns in the PR.

## Refs
- Parent epic: #1900
- Predecessor: #1918 (tracked there as open item **T078**)
- Code seam: `assistant-service` `app/agent/provider.py`, the turn runner, `app/mcp/relevance.py` (the tool-binding signal)
t: [Assistant] Model routing for no-tool turns (follow-up to #1918)

## Summary

An audit of the **production Elasticsearch** cluster (`elastic.alkem.io`) on 2026-06-20 found **end-user PII present at rest across multiple services**, primarily via application/access logs shipped through Logstash, plus product-data and analytics indices. This should not be the case for the log data, and the at-rest product data warrants a governance/retention review.

> ⚠️ Real email addresses and names found during the audit are **redacted** in this issue to avoid re-leaking PII. Concrete (unredacted) evidence is available on request to the security/platform owners.

## Method

- Server-side aggregation across **every** `*logstash-output-*` stream at once (all 182 shards succeeded), `match_phrase` on ~23 public mail-provider domains.
- Targeted mapping inspection + counts on the product-data (`alkemio-data-*`, `contribution-events-*`) and analytics indices.
- **All email counts are lower bounds** — only public mail providers were matched; corporate-domain emails were confirmed present (e.g. `*@<municipality>.nl`) but are not included in the counts.

## 🔴 Direct PII leaking into LOGS (the actionable violations)

| Service log | PII | Public-domain email hits | Window | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **traefik** | Client public IPs on **every** request (+1 email in a URL param) | n/a | Apr 15 → now | **~5,202,959 docs**, all client IPs. Largest PII volume by far. |
| **kratos** | Full identity traits incl. **email** (likely name/phone too) | 226 | Apr–Jun 2026 | IdP dumping registration/settings payloads to stdout. Most sensitive. |
| **alkemio-web** | **email** in User-Agent strings + client IPs (nginx access log) | 129 | Apr–Jun 2026 | e.g. `... Safari/537.36 Some Company inc <redacted>@gmail.com` |
| **postgres** | **email** in DB error DETAIL lines | 15 | Mar–May 2026 | `Key (nid, via, value)=(…, email, <redacted>@outlook.com) already exists` — duplicate-registration errors. |
| **virtual-contributor-ingest-space** | **Rosters of names + emails** (ingested space/whiteboard content) | 10 | Apr 2026 | Corporate-domain emails confirmed here. |
| **alkemio-server** | **email** in authz-denial messages | 2 (of 150 lines) | **Feb 14 – Mar 19 only** | `User (<redacted>@gmail.com) does not have credentials…`. Pattern appears to have **stopped** mid-March (already changed/aged). |

**Public-domain email docs across all logs: 383 (floor).** Traefik client-IP records: **~5.2M**.

## 🟡 Direct PII in product-data indices (by-design, but it *is* PII at rest in ES)

| Index | Docs | PII |
|---|---|---|
| `contribution-events-with-names-v2` | 59,535 | Real names tied to activity |
| `alkemio-data-users-*` | 2,364 | firstName, lastName, displayName, **postal address** (no email) |
| `alkemio-data-{whiteboards,callouts,posts,memos,subspaces,spaces}` | ~17,700 | User-generated content + display names |
| `alkemio-data-organizations-*` | 704 | Org / contact data |
| `guidance-usage` | 465 | Free-text user prompts + author UUID |

## 🟢 Pseudonymous only (UUID-keyed — personal data under GDPR, no names/emails)
`user_contribution_summary` (22,267), `daily_user_sessions` (22,266), `session-durations` (13,328 — session IDs + URLs), `daily-user-metrics` (224).

## ⚪ Checked, clean
`alkemio-ipfs-access-log` (paths only); oathkeeper / hydra / oidc (internal cluster IPs only, not user PII).

## Caveats on completeness
- Email sweep = public mail providers only → corporate-domain emails uncounted (confirmed present). Counts are floors.
- Services leaking only **names/phone in free text** (no email) would not be caught by phrase matching — needs NER-style scanning to fully rule out.
- Access logs (traefik, alkemio-web) carry client IPs on **100%** of docs by nature.

## Proposed remediation

1. **Stop the bleed at ingest (durable fix):** add Logstash/filebeat filters to drop client IPs and mask emails before indexing. Highest priority for `traefik` (volume) and `kratos` (sensitivity).
2. **Fix at source:**
   - Kratos should not log identity traits at info level in prod.
   - Postgres should not log statement/error DETAIL containing value literals (review `log_min_*` / error verbosity).
   - VC ingest should not log full ingested content.
   - alkemio-web access logs should drop/anonymise client IP + UA where not needed.
3. **Purge existing PII + tighten retention:** `delete_by_query` on offending docs and shorten ILM retention for the PII-bearing log streams (some data streams reach back to 2023). ⚠️ destructive on prod — scope to be confirmed before execution.
4. **Governance review** of the product-data indices (`alkemio-data-users` postal addresses, `contribution-events-with-names-v2`) for DPA/retention compliance.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Ingest-side redaction in place for traefik client IPs and kratos/postgres/web/VC-ingest emails.
- [ ] Source-side logging fixes merged for kratos, postgres, VC-ingest.
- [ ] Historical PII purged from existing indices and ILM retention tightened.
- [ ] Re-run the audit sweep → 0 public-domain email hits in logs; no new client-IP-bearing indices outside policy.

---
*Audit performed 2026-06-20 against `elastic.alkem.io` (cluster `elasticsearch`, 2 nodes, ~2,817 indices). Read-only; no data modified.*
t: Security/Privacy: end-user PII (emails, client IPs, names) present in production Elasticsearch

## Summary

Surfaced by CodeRabbit on infrastructure-operations PR #2279 (assistant edge), but
the root cause is **platform-wide Traefik config, not assistant-specific**.

On **acceptance + production** (`infrastructure-operations`), both Traefik
entrypoints set:

```
--entrypoints.web.forwardedHeaders.insecure=true
--entrypoints.websecure.forwardedHeaders.insecure=true
--entrypoints.web.proxyProtocol.insecure=true
--entrypoints.websecure.proxyProtocol.insecure=true
```
`…networking/traefik/11-traefik-deployment.yml`

`forwardedHeaders.insecure=true` makes Traefik **trust `X-Forwarded-*` from any
source IP** — it overrides the adjacent `forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs=172.0.0.0/8`
restriction. Both forwardAuth middlewares then re-forward those headers to the
auth endpoint:

- `26-alkemio-resolve-forward-auth-middleware.yml` → `/rest/internal/forward-auth`, `trustForwardHeader: true`
- `26-alkemio-resolve-assistant-forward-auth-middleware.yml` → `/rest/internal/assistant-forward-auth`, `trustForwardHeader: true`

## Impact

A client can set arbitrary `X-Forwarded-For` / `-Host` / `-Proto` and have the
edge trust and propagate them. The identity decision itself is session-cookie
based (so this is **not** a direct auth bypass), and the assistant route
additionally zeroes client `X-Alkemio-*` via `assistant-strip-client-alkemio-headers`.
The residual risk is in anything that consumes the forwarded values downstream:
client-IP logging / audit, rate-limiting / abuse heuristics keyed on IP, and any
redirect/absolute-URL built from `X-Forwarded-Host`/`-Proto`.

dev-orchestration sets `trustForwardHeader: true` on the same two middlewares but
does **not** set `forwardedHeaders.insecure=true`, so the dev exposure is lower.

## Proposed remediation (preferred: option 1)

1. **Drop `insecure=true`** on `forwardedHeaders` (and reassess `proxyProtocol.insecure`)
   for both entrypoints, and pin `forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs` to the actual LB /
   ingress CIDR in front of Traefik (Scaleway LB range), so only the real proxy
   hop is trusted. This is the recommended approach for in-cluster auth.
2. Alternatively set `trustForwardHeader: false` on the two forwardAuth middlewares
   if the auth endpoints don't need the original forwarded headers.

Either option needs validation that real client IPs still resolve correctly
behind the Scaleway LB after the change.

## Scope
- `infrastructure-operations` — acceptance + production overlays (primary).
- `dev-orchestration` — review `trustForwardHeader` usage for parity, lower priority.

Out of scope for PR #2279 (broad blast radius across every route); filed as a
standalone hardening item. The narrow assistant `/internal/**` edge exposure from
the same review is already fixed (infra-ops #2279, dev-orch #62).

## What & why

Let users attach **images and files to conversation messages**, working from
**both** the Alkemio web client and a native Element/Matrix client. Every media
file is **stored once** through **file-service** (the single storage
abstraction) — accounted in the file table, scoped to the conversation, and
**governed by chat membership** on every retrieval path.

This also retires Synapse's independent persistent media store: its local store
becomes an **ephemeral cache** and durability moves behind file-service.

**Status: implemented, in review across 4 repos; not merged.** Ships behind a
feature flag that defaults to **off**.

## Scope (cross-repo)

- **file-service** — verbatim (no-transcode) store path for the Matrix byte
  bridge, canonicalization on the ordinary web-upload path, content-addressed
  blob sharing. Stays Matrix-agnostic.
- **matrix-adapter** — **stateless**: detects/builds event media, embeds
  `io.alkemio.document_id`, surfaces raw refs, bridges bytes. Holds no mapping
  table and mints no authorization.
- **Synapse media storage provider** (new, thin) — Synapse byte I/O ↔
  file-service, direct (byte-plane only, no durable state).
- **server** — per-conversation storage bucket + authorization (resolves the
  current "no storage for conversations" gap), message attachment field,
  re-home of inbound media, attachment read resolution to the client.
- **client-web** — composer attach UI + attachment rendering.
- **dev-orchestration / infrastructure-operations** — demote Synapse local
  store to ephemeral cache, provider config.

### Explicitly NOT in scope (de-scoped during implementation)

- **A durable object-storage (S3) backend for file-service** — a separate track.
  This feature runs on file-service's existing storage.
- **Matrix-aware reference counting / lifecycle / GC.** Blob reclamation is
  **Synapse's** (its media store + retention/purge). The client+server+adapter
  tier is a Synapse *client*, not a replacement, and does not release or delete
  attachment storage on message delete. Deleting a message is a per-event
  redaction, exactly as in Element.
- **A browser-renderable derivative alongside verbatim-stored originals.**
- **Historical media backfill** — #1996, a hard prerequisite for the cutover.

## Accepted limitations (deliberate — please don't file these as bugs)

- **Element-origin HEIC/HEIF is not canonicalized.** Inbound media is stored
  verbatim, because the storage provider must be able to serve Synapse exactly
  the bytes it was given. So an iOS Element upload may not render in browsers
  that cannot decode HEIC; it renders fine in Element. Web-origin uploads *are*
  canonicalized. If web rendering of these is later needed, the answer is a
  derived web variant, not breaking verbatim storage.
- Because that arm is verbatim: EXIF/GPS is preserved rather than stripped, and
  the decode-bomb pixel-budget guard does not run on it.
- **A redacted message's bytes may persist** until Synapse's retention policy
  reclaims them — and if it is not configured to, they persist. That is a
  Synapse configuration concern, not a server defect.
- **A multi-attachment send is not atomic** — it is 1 + N independent Matrix
  events, so a partial send is possible. This is exactly Element's behaviour.
- **Image dimensions are taken from the event as declared**, as every Matrix
  client does; they are not re-measured against the stored bytes.

## Acceptance (from the spec's success criteria)

- Attach/send from either client; all members see it regardless of their client.
- 100% of attachments appear as file-table documents, conversation-scoped,
  attributed to the sender.
- Exactly one durable **blob** per unique file content — measured on stored
  bytes, not document rows. Several conversation-scoped rows intentionally share
  one blob, and on the attachment path identical bytes from two senders produce
  two rows so per-sender ownership can be enforced.
- Non-members denied on every retrieval path.
- Media survives Synapse restarts; brief file-service outage degrades gracefully.
- No durable conversation media outside the storage abstraction.
- Alkemio's media policy (allowed types, 50 MiB cap, ≤10 attachments) constrains
  **what Alkemio accepts**, never what Synapse accepts — the reserved
  `matrix_media` staging bucket is unrestricted, so Element users are not
  restricted by Alkemio policy in rooms Alkemio does not own.

## Rollout

Gated by `communications.message_attachments.enabled` (env
`COMMUNICATIONS_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED`), default **off**. The flag gates
the send path, the read paths, the staged-media cleanup sweep, and the eager
per-conversation storage provisioning — so shipping it disabled is inert.

1. Land the code **disabled**.
2. Run the **#1996 legacy-media backfill** (hard prerequisite) and verify its summary.
3. Flip the Synapse media volume PV → emptyDir cache.
4. Enable the flag.

## Links

- Spec (single source of truth): `agents-hq` workspace → `specs/013-matrix-media-file-service/`
- Related: #1881 (Communications upgrade — parent context)
- **Blocked on** #1996 for the production cutover
- Informs/resolves the media-storage evaluation in
  alkem-io/infrastructure-operations#2134

_Tracked via SDD workspace spec `013-matrix-media-file-service`._

## Gap (hit live on acceptance, 2026-07-03)

`analyze_whiteboard` extracts drawn **Excalidraw text elements** only. Boards that are mostly **pasted images** come back opaque — real case: `test-123456/collaboration/test8` has 6 elements (3 images, rectangle, diamond, freedraw), **0 text elements** → every analysis type (`semantic`, `text`, `elements`) returns geometry and stats but nothing about what the images show. For an AI client (web assistant, external MCP agents — #1912), the most information-dense element type on real boards is invisible.

## Scope

- For `image` elements, resolve the underlying file (Excalidraw `fileId` → platform storage / file-service) and run an OCR **or vision-model description** pass; merge the per-image text/description into the `semantic` and `text` analysis outputs (positioned, so clusters/connections can include them).
- **Authorization**: image retrieval MUST reuse the caller's read authorization on the whiteboard/storage — no bypass of document access control.
- **Cost/latency gating**: vision calls are LLM-priced — make it opt-in (e.g. `includeImages: true` or a new `analysisType`), cap image count/size per call, and cache descriptions per file content hash (images are immutable per fileId).
- **Budget attribution**: when invoked via the assistant's delegated flow, vision tokens must land in the same per-user metering (FR-028 path).
- Degrade gracefully: unreadable/unsupported image → a typed note in the output, never a failed analysis.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A board whose only content is pasted images yields a meaningful `analyze_whiteboard` result (per-image text/description with coordinates).
- [ ] Access-controlled images are only described for callers who can read them.
- [ ] Vision pass is opt-in and bounded (count/size caps, per-file cache); plain analyses stay at today's cost.
- [ ] Works for both the internal assistant (delegated) and external MCP clients (#1912).

Related: #1900 (assistant epic) · #1912 (external MCP access) · #1956 (MCP rate limiting) · workspace spec `008-external-mcp-access`.

**Part of the Disaster Recovery Hardening epic — alkem-io/infrastructure-operations#2351.**

> **Status: In Review — shipped, awaiting the GitOps merges.** `file-backup-service` **v0.0.4** is
> released; the full backup → audit → restore-drill loop runs end to end on **sandbox**. Acceptance
> and production land on [infra-ops#2408](https://github.com/alkem-io/infrastructure-operations/pull/2408)
> (production is **deliberately draft-gated** — a human deploy decision). See the delivery record in
> the comments.


## What & why

With the introduction of **documents** (Collabora/office docs, and soon whiteboards and memos as Yjs blobs), the platform now stores **user-authored, non-reconstructable, high-churn** content. The acceptable file-loss window has collapsed from ~hours to **minutes** — a handful of people editing for even 20 minutes produce irreplaceable work.

Give every stored object a durable, off-cluster, **immutable**, integrity-verified copy, captured **continuously** and with low latency: file-service writes each object's content hash to an **outbox** transactionally on store; a new **file-backup-service** consumes the outbox and fans the bytes out to **N content-addressed targets**. Plus best-effort restore and past-version recovery for support.

This tightens the file-storage slice of the DR-hardening epic from its 4-hour SLA down to **minutes-RPO**, driven by the document risk.

## Affected repos

- `file-service` — outbox producer (writes hash + breadcrumbs transactionally with the object row)
- `file-backup-service` *(new)* — outbox consumer; reads bytes by hash, optional adaptive compression, fans out to N targets, verifies, maintains the ledger
- `infrastructure-operations` — target buckets/volumes + credentials, ≥1 independent + immutable target, deployment, monitoring/alerting, restore-drill schedule

## Acceptance criteria (from spec Success Criteria)

> Ticked = mechanically verified. Proven **on sandbox** (the only environment where the full loop
> runs today); acc/prod land on infra-ops#2408. Human gates and prod-only criteria stay unticked.

- [x] New objects have a hash-verified copy on all **required** targets within the RPO window (target: single-digit minutes). — *sandbox: worker v0.0.4 draining the outbox via LISTEN/NOTIFY; acc/prod pending #2408.*
- [x] After backfill, ≥ 99.9% of referenced objects have a verified backup on every required target (reconciliation-measured). — *sandbox backfill swept the pre-existing corpus (89 outbox rows → 84 unique content-addressed objects); both audit directions clean (`manifest=85 extra=0 missing=0`).*
- [ ] ≥ 1 required target is in an **independent failure domain and immutable** (object-lock, separate account); worker credentials are write-only / no-delete. — *implemented and drift-checked (object-lock + versioning + default retention rule + SSE, PutObject-only worker cred), but the WORM bucket is configured in infra-ops#2408 — **not live**. Blocked on that merge + the production deploy gate.*
- [x] Any single target is restorable with **nothing but bytes + a hash check** (no index, no tool). — *every target carries its own manifest (`_manifest/<UTCdate>.jsonl`); keys are the SHA3-256 content hash; the drill restores through exactly this path.*
- [x] A client's prior file version can be recovered best-effort via a DB backup/PITR lookup + the retained blob. — *retain-all (live deletes never prune a backup) + `restore --hash`; `restore current --at` covers the safe case and deliberately over-refuses rather than return a wrong version. Runbook: `docs/FILE_BACKUP_DR.MD`.*
- [x] No creation is lost across worker restart, target outage, or RWO volume relocation (fault-injected). — *`TestIntegrationFaultInjectionResumeNoLoss`: takes a target offline, asserts no object is falsely marked done, recovers the target, **restarts the worker**, asserts every object completes. RWO relocation is dissolved architecturally — the worker fetches bytes by hash over HTTP, so it no longer co-locates with file-service.*
- [ ] Operators are paged when backup age, coverage, or dead-letter counts cross thresholds. — *the `FileBackup` alert group is authored (RPO breach, stalled drain, circuit open, coverage slip, never-verified target, dead-letters, manifest-write failures, stale sampler, worker down, audit-job failing, **drill-job failing** [critical]) but it is Helm-managed — it activates on infra-ops#2408 merge + `helm upgrade`. `FileBackupImmutabilityDrift` stays staged pending a read-only WORM credential (see below).*
- [x] A scheduled restore drill passes (proves the procedure, not just byte existence). — *weekly CronJob, **active**. Sandbox runs a **full-store** drill (`--sample 0`): `checked=85 passed=85 failed=0` on v0.0.4. It restores through the real operator path (fetch → decode → SHA3-256 verify → durable write), not a byte-existence check.*

## Design notes

- Consumption: Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` (low-latency wakeup) + polling floor + startup drain + `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; the durable outbox table is the source of truth.
- Targets are **dumb, index-free content-addressed sinks** (store/exists/fetch by hash), initially S3-compatible + POSIX filesystem, sharded by hash prefix. Repo-format tooling (kopia) is a possible **later** optional secondary — out of scope for the initial.
- Compression is optional adaptive zstd with **no per-object codec field** (hash-arbiter); the primary target may stay uncompressed for restore purity.
- Retain all versions (no GC now); the document→hash temporal map is delegated to DB backups/PITR, not stored in the file backup.
- RWO is handled via a **fetch-by-hash read abstraction** (network reader preferred → dissolves co-location and is forward-compatible with the planned primary-store move to object storage).

## Source of truth

Workspace spec: `specs/008-continuous-file-backup/spec.md` in `alkem-io/agents-hq` (branch `feat/008-continuous-file-backup`).

# Epic: Space and Subspace Chat

## Description
Every Space and Subspace gets its own group chat, opening in the normal chat window like any other conversation. The twist: membership is tied to Space/Subspace membership. Join the Space, you're in the chat. Leave the Space, you're out of the chat, and vice versa.

## Goal
Gives every Space and Subspace a built-in place to talk that needs no separate setup or invite step, membership just follows what's already there. Strengthens the case for Alkemio as the place where a group's whole collaboration, including chat, lives.

## Hypothesis
If chat membership tracks Space/Subspace membership automatically, people will actually use it instead of falling back to email or external chat tools for space-related conversations. Success looks like active usage of these chats without people needing to manually manage who's in them.

Leading indicators:
- Number of Space/Subspace chats with active messages (not just created and abandoned)
- Messages per active chat per week
- Support questions about "why am I in/not in this chat" (should trend toward zero if the sync logic is solid)

## Must have scope

- [ ] Chat automatically created when a Space or Subspace is created
- [ ] Button within the Space/Subspace to open its chat directly, no need to find it via a separate chat list
- [ ] Chat opens in the standard chat window, same UX as other chats
- [ ] Joining a Space/Subspace adds the person to its chat
- [ ] Leaving a Space/Subspace removes the person from its chat
- [ ] TBD Removal from the chat directly (if that's even possible) should not remove someone from the Space/Subspace itself; membership sync is one-directional in that edge case
- [ ] Handling for existing Spaces/Subspaces at rollout: retroactively create chats and populate membership
t: Communications: Subspace chat

Follow-up to the **2026-06-30 file-storage data loss** (root cause: infrastructure-operations#2336 — the NFS file store was never actually backed up; backup/restore operated on the wrong path).

Recovery is done and ticketed. **Repairing the damage still live in the DB is not — that is this issue.**

| Incident work | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Root cause — back up the real NFS store | infra-ops#2336 | merged |
| Manifest-driven file-storage recovery scripts | infra-ops#2338 | merged |
| Regenerate *derived* visuals (whiteboard previews, letter-avatars) | alkem-io/agents-hq#31 | merged |
| Browser-cache recovery tool | `alkem-io/client-recovery-tool` | done |
| Prevention — continuous backup | alkem-io/alkemio#1983 (`workspace#008`) | in review |
| **Remediate DB references to unrecoverable files** | **this issue** | **not started** |

Prevention does not heal this. #1983 stops the *next* loss; the references broken by *this* one are still live.

---

## Approach

This is **semi-manual by nature** — there is no single safe `DELETE`. The work is a pipeline, with a **human approval gate** before anything is written:

> **1. Re-run the audit → 2. Bin every reference by remediation type → 3. Produce the picture (bins × space lineage) → 4. Propose a resolution per bin → 5. APPROVE → 6. Execute per bin → 7. Verify**

The unit of decision is the **bin**, not the file: what you do about a lost image depends entirely on *how it is referenced*. Removing an image from a whiteboard scene is a different operation, with a different blast radius, than deleting a document from a callout — and in the callout case the **comments must survive**.

---

## Phase 0 — Re-run the audit

Tooling exists: `recovery/missing-files-audit/` (SQL + CSV/dossier emitters). Re-run it to get a **current** still-missing list — the last run was 2026-07-01, and recovery work has landed since.

⚠️ **Run it against PRODUCTION.** The only run on hand was scoped to `k8s-scaleway-acceptance`, and its 83 spaces are almost entirely **test spaces** (`Check if I am a lead ha` — 783 files, `fdsa › l1 test`, `check layout2 › bbb › aaa 2`, …). **The acceptance numbers say close to nothing about customer impact.** The production blast radius is unverified and is the actual thing we need to know.

For reference, the acceptance run found: 1,208 still-missing blobs · 2,015 `file` rows · 1,943 referenced-missing · 72 orphans · 83 spaces.

## Phase 1 — Bin the references (tooling change)

The audit currently emits the reference **site** (`referencedBy`) but does not **bin** it, and does not classify **space lineage**. Both need adding.

### Remediation bins

Derived from the reference sites actually observed:

| Bin | Reference sites | Remediation | User-visible effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Regenerable** | `visual.uri` where the visual is *derived* (whiteboard preview/card, letter-avatar) | Re-run `regenerate-visuals`. **Not a data decision** — the image comes back. | none |
| **B — Default-fallback visual** | `visual.uri`, user-uploaded (banner, custom avatar, card) | Null the URI → the UI renders its default. | silent downgrade to a default image |
| **C — Embedded media in rich text** | `profile.description`, `callout_contribution_defaults.postDescription`, `memo.content` | Strip the dead image markdown / Yjs node. **Keep all surrounding text.** | image vanishes; text + comments intact |
| **D — Embedded media in a whiteboard scene** | `whiteboard.content` | Remove the image element from the Excalidraw scene. **Keep the scene.** | image vanishes; whiteboard otherwise intact |
| **E — The artifact IS the content** | `collabora_document.documentId`, uploaded docs/images as callout contributions | The document is **unrecoverable**. Remove/tombstone the contribution — but **KEEP the callout and its comments/discussion.** | **the user must be told** |
| **F — Dead links** | `reference.uri`, `link.uri` | Delete the reference/link row. | link disappears |
| **G — Orphans** | referenced nowhere | Hard-delete the `file` row. | none |

Bins A, B, F, G are mechanical. **C and D need content-aware surgery** (markdown / Excalidraw-JSON / Yjs rewriting — remove one node, preserve the document). **E needs a product + comms decision**, not just code.

### Space lineage

Add a **customer vs Alkemio-internal** classification per reference (the audit already carries `spacePath`, `spaceLeads`, `ownerType`, `creatorName`, `creatorEmail` — the flag is derivable, it just isn't emitted).

**Customer spaces outrank Alkemio-own / test / demo spaces**, both for prioritisation and for the level of care. A broken image in `fdsa › l1 test` is noise; the same break in a customer space is real damage.

## Phase 2 — The picture

Output: **lost files + their references, split by bin, × customer/internal, × space lineage.** Per-bin counts, with the customer-space slice broken out and named. This is the artifact the decision is made on — nothing is written until it exists.

## Phase 3 — Propose + APPROVE (human gate)

A written proposed resolution **per bin**, reviewed and approved before any write. Bin E in particular (unrecoverable office documents — the acceptance run alone had 47 `.docx`, 41 `.pptx`, 29 `.xlsx`) needs a product call on **tombstone vs silent removal**, and a decision on **notifying affected space leads / creators** — the audit already produces the per-space contact sheet to do it.

## Phase 4 — Execute, per bin

- **Dry-run first**, always: emit the exact diff before writing.
- **Rehearse on Alkemio-own / test spaces**, then customer spaces.
- **Reversible record** of every row changed (the old value), so a mistake is undoable — we are mutating live content to repair a data loss; a second data loss would be unforgivable.
- One bin at a time. Do not batch bins with different blast radii.

## Phase 5 — Verify

Re-run the audit: residual referenced-missing should be **zero**. Spot-check the UI in affected spaces per bin.

---

## Also: the audit tooling is not in any repo

`recovery/missing-files-audit/` — the SQL, the CSVs, and the per-space contact sheet — exists **only as untracked files on one laptop**. `regenerate-visuals` was committed (agents-hq#31); this never was. The evidence of what was lost, including the customer contact sheet, is one `rm -rf` from being lost itself. **Commit it before anything else.**

## Checklist

- [x] Commit `recovery/missing-files-audit/` (tooling + outputs) to a repo
- [x] Extend the audit: emit a **remediation bin** per reference, and a **customer/internal** space-lineage flag
- [x] **Re-run against PRODUCTION** (and acceptance) — establish the true blast radius
- [x] Produce the picture: bins × lineage, customer slice named
- [x] Bin A: re-run `regenerate-visuals` for any residual derived visuals
- [ ] Bin G: delete orphans (no user-visible effect)
- [ ] Proposed resolution per bin → **approval**
- [ ] Product decision + comms plan for Bin E (unrecoverable documents)
- [ ] Execute per bin: dry-run → internal spaces → customer spaces, with a reversible record
- [ ] Verify: audit residual = 0; UI spot-checks

## Related

- alkem-io/alkemio#1983 — continuous file backup (**prevents recurrence; does not repair this**)
- infrastructure-operations#2351 — DR Hardening epic
t: Remediate DB references to files lost in the 2026-06-30 incident (bin → approve → execute)

## What & why

One-time migration of **existing Synapse media** into **file-service**, so that
flipping the Synapse media volume to an ephemeral cache (feature 013) does not
**permanently 404 historical media**. The instant `/data/media_store` is shadowed
by the emptyDir, every pre-cutover blob has no file-service document and the 013
storage provider's `fetch` returns nothing → broken images in Element.

This copies all existing Synapse **local** media into file-service's `matrix_media`
bucket, keyed by `externalReference = media_id`, stored verbatim — the analogue of
the matrix-org `synapse-s3-storage-provider`'s initial `s3_media_upload` pass.

**Prerequisite for the 013 production cutover** (must run before PV→emptyDir).

## Scope

- **In:** Synapse `local_content/*` user uploads → file-service `matrix_media`
  (verbatim, `externalReference=media_id`).
- **Out:** thumbnails, url-preview cache, remote/federated media; **web-client
  historical re-home** (legacy media is served via the Element/Matrix path, which
  already rendered it — historical rendering in the *new* web chat is a separate,
  larger concern).

## Shape (single-repo — infrastructure-operations; dev mirror in dev-orchestration)

A one-time, **idempotent/resumable** Kubernetes Job + script that:
- walks the Synapse media PVC (**read-only** mount), reconstructing `media_id`
  from the `local_content/<id0:2>/<id2:4>/<id4:>` layout (reuse the 013 purge job's
  logic);
- POSTs each blob to file-service `POST /internal/file` (`storageBucketId=matrix_media`,
  `externalReference=media_id`, `skipImageProcessing=true`);
- **skips** media whose `media_id` already resolves via
  `GET /internal/file/by-reference?ref=<media_id>` (re-runnable);
- verifies preconditions (file-service reachable with its **durable storage
  backend** live, `externalReference` schema present, `matrix_media` bucket
  exists with its real UUID) and **fails fast** if unmet;
- supports a **dry run** and emits a **summary** (scanned / backfilled / skipped /
  failed) as the operator's go/no-go signal.

No code change to file-service / server / matrix-adapter / client-web — uses 013's
existing internal API.

### Two constraints worth calling out

- **Do NOT send `allowedMimeTypes` / `maxFileSize` on the create request.** They
  are per-request multipart fields (file-service never reads bucket policy from
  the DB), and supplying them would reject exactly the arbitrary historical media
  this backfill exists to preserve. The reserved `matrix_media` bucket is
  unrestricted by design — Alkemio's media policy governs what Alkemio accepts,
  never what Synapse accepts.
- **An S3 backend is NOT a precondition.** It was explicitly de-scoped from 013
  to a separate track. What this backfill needs is that file-service's storage is
  durable and that the Synapse PV is no longer the only copy — whichever backend
  file-service is running.

## Acceptance (from spec 014 success criteria)

- 100% of `local_content` media has a byte-identical `matrix_media` document keyed
  by its `media_id`.
- After PV→emptyDir cutover (local cache empty), historical media loads in Element.
- Re-run adds zero duplicates and completes clean (idempotent/resumable).
- Read-only on the Synapse PVC; bounded memory/throughput on a large store.
- Auditable go/no-go summary before the cutover.

## Rollout position

server `externalReference` migration (owned by **server's TypeORM**, via the
`server-migration` cron — file-service does runtime CRUD only) + `matrix_media`
bucket seeded, unrestricted, with its real UUID →
**run this backfill (verify summary)** → PV→emptyDir flip → enable the 013
feature flag → Element smoke.

## Links

- Spec: `agents-hq` → `specs/014-legacy-media-backfill/spec.md`
- Prerequisite for: 013 story alkem-io/alkemio#1946
- Related: alkem-io/infrastructure-operations#2134 (Synapse media-storage/backup eval)

_Tracked via workspace spec `014-legacy-media-backfill` (single-repo: infrastructure-operations, + dev-orchestration mirror)._
t: Legacy Synapse media backfill into file-service (013 cutover prerequisite)

## Description

**Epic.** Give search engines a machine-readable map of Alkemio's public content so the
platform's spaces and profiles become discoverable in Google/Bing. Today the platform SPA
(`app.alkem.io`, `client-web`) is fully client-rendered, ships **no `sitemap.xml`**, and serves
every route with the same static `<title>`/meta — so public content is effectively invisible to
organic search. Robots.txt already landed (client-web #9401 / workspace spec `021-add-robots-txt`)
and deliberately reserves a `Sitemap:` directive for exactly this work.

Delivered in two steps:
1. **MVP — a static, curated `sitemap.xml`** on `app.alkem.io` listing the most important static
   pages and a hand-picked set of flagship public spaces, wired for discovery (robots.txt + Google
   Search Console).
2. **Long-term — a server-generated, cron-refreshed sitemap** that stays automatically in sync as
   public content is created and deleted, reusing the server's canonical URL builder.

**Cross-repo:** `server` (generation + serving), `client-web` (MVP file + robots wiring),
`infrastructure-operations` (root-path routing), and later `documentation` + the marketing site.

Primary persona: **prospective members / the public** searching for a topic, community, or
organisation — plus **space admins** who want their public space found. Job story: _when_ I search
for a topic a public Alkemio space covers, _I want_ that space to appear in results, _so I can_
discover and join it without needing a direct link.

## Goal

Unlock **organic discoverability** of public Alkemio content. Inbound traffic today depends on
direct/shared links; nothing on the platform is crawlable at scale. A sitemap + discovery wiring is
the prerequisite for search engines to find and index public spaces, innovation packs, virtual
contributors, and organisations — feeding top-of-funnel growth and making public communities
findable. It also closes the SEO gap left open when robots.txt shipped (the deferred `Sitemap:`
directive).

## Hypothesis

Publishing a valid, auto-maintained sitemap and submitting it via a Search Console **Domain
property** will get Alkemio's public URLs **crawled and progressively indexed**, measurable in
Google Search Console.

**Success is measured by:**
- Sitemap(s) parse in GSC with **0 errors**; the full set of public URLs is **submitted**.
- **Indexed-page count trends up** over 4–8 weeks; organic **impressions/clicks** on
  space/pack/profile URLs grow from a near-zero baseline.
- Leading indicators (GSC): Coverage "submitted vs. indexed", Crawl Stats, Sitemaps report.

**Known risk (expectation calibration):** a sitemap gets URLs **discovered**, but because the SPA is
client-rendered with shared static meta and no `rel=canonical`/`og:url`, **indexing quality will be
limited** even with a perfect sitemap. If "submitted vs. indexed" stays low, the gating work is
**SEO-quality** (per-route meta/canonical + prerender/SSR of public pages), captured as a flagged
track in Phase 2 — worth deciding early.

## Must have scope

**In scope**
- MVP static `sitemap.xml` at the root of `app.alkem.io` — curated static routes (`/spaces`,
  `/innovation-library`, `/forum`, `/docs`) + top-N flagship public spaces; **environment-aware**
  (non-prod suppressed, mirroring robots.txt); robots.txt `Sitemap:` directive enabled.
- **Google Search Console**: DNS-verified **Domain property** for `alkem.io` (covers all
  subdomains under one property); sitemap submitted.
- Long-term **server-generated** sitemap (index + child files, each ≤ 50k URLs / 50 MB) from live
  public content, refreshed on a schedule; served at the web root via an ingress route to the server.
- Content types listed: **public Spaces + their public subspaces** (L1/L2), **Innovation Packs +
  Library**, **Organization profiles**, **Virtual Contributor profiles**, and **static pages +
  `/docs`** (concrete pages).

**Out of scope / deferred**
- **User profiles** — excluded for privacy.
- `welcome.alkem.io` + marketing homepage (external `website-alkemio`) and `alkem.io/documentation`
  (Docusaurus) — coordinated later via a cross-host sitemap index under the same GSC domain property
  (Docusaurus has a first-party sitemap plugin).
- Query-param permutations (`?tab=N`, `?dialog=…`) — one canonical URL per entity, to avoid
  duplicate-content bloat.

**Locked decisions:** engine = server, cron-refreshed · MVP host = `app.alkem.io` only · user
profiles excluded.
**Open item:** confirm the production canonical origin (`ENDPOINT_CLUSTER` — evidence points to
`app.alkem.io`); every sitemap `<loc>` origin must match it exactly.

## Stakeholders

- **Product** — scope + the privacy call on which entity types are listed.
- **Engineering** — `server` (generation / serving / cron), `client-web` / frontend (MVP file +
  robots), `infrastructure-operations` / DevOps (Traefik root-path routing, DNS for the GSC domain
  property).
- **Growth / Marketing (SEO)** — GSC ownership + monitoring; coordinating the welcome/marketing
  site sitemap.
- **Customer Success** — communities/customers who want their public spaces to be findable.

## Design

No Figma — this is backend generation + a static file + infra routing. References:
- Google Search Central: [Build & submit a sitemap](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap)
  · [Sitemap index & cross-site rules](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/large-sitemaps)
  · [GSC property types](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/34592)
- Prior art: robots.txt (client-web #9401 / workspace spec `021-add-robots-txt`) — reuse its
  environment-aware `env.sh` + nginx pattern.
- Canonical URL source of truth: server `UrlGeneratorService`
  (`server/src/services/infrastructure/url-generator/`), surfaced on GraphQL as `Profile.url`.

## Phases & Acceptance Criteria

### Phase 0 — MVP static sitemap + discovery  _(client-web; ships fast, single repo)_
A curated static file on `app.alkem.io`, wired for crawling. Can ship ahead of the rest.
- [ ] `public/sitemap.xml` committed with valid XML (sitemaps.org schema): the static routes above
      + a curated set of top public spaces, absolute `<loc>` on the canonical origin.
- [ ] **Given** production (`VITE_ROBOTS_ALLOW_INDEXING=true`), **when** a crawler requests
      `/sitemap.xml`, **then** it receives `200` + `Content-Type: application/xml`; **given** a
      non-production environment, **then** the sitemap is suppressed (fail-safe, mirroring robots.txt).
- [ ] `robots.txt` `Sitemap:` directive is uncommented and points at the sitemap.
- [ ] nginx serves `/sitemap.xml` with correct content-type + sane cache (dedicated
      `location = /sitemap.xml` block).
- [ ] A unit test asserts the committed sitemap's validity/contents (mirroring `robotsTxt.test.ts`).
- [ ] **GSC**: a DNS-verified Domain property for `alkem.io` exists; the sitemap is submitted and
      parses with **0 errors**.

### Phase 1 — Dynamic server generator + serving  _(server + infrastructure-operations + client-web)_
Auto-maintained sitemap from live content; supersedes the Phase-0 static file.
- [ ] The server enumerates **public** content — Spaces (`visibility=ACTIVE` **and**
      `privacy=PUBLIC`) + public subspaces, Innovation Packs/Library, listed Virtual Contributors,
      Organizations — and builds absolute `<loc>` via `UrlGeneratorService`. **Private / non-active
      content is excluded** (PRIVATE spaces appear as `/about` only, or are omitted).
- [ ] Output is a **sitemap index + child sitemaps**, each ≤ 50,000 URLs / 50 MB (gzip permitted);
      `<lastmod>` reflects the entity's real last update.
- [ ] A scheduled job (`@nestjs/schedule`) regenerates the sitemap on a defined cadence; **created
      content appears and deleted content disappears** after regeneration (verified end-to-end).
- [ ] `app.alkem.io/sitemap.xml` (+ `/sitemap-*.xml`) is served at the web root via a Traefik route
      to the server; every `<loc>` host equals the canonical origin (`endpoint_cluster` == client
      `locations.domain`).
- [ ] `robots.txt` `Sitemap:` points at the generated index; the Phase-0 static file is retired.

### Phase 2 — Freshness, cross-subdomain & monitoring  _(rolling / optional)_
- [ ] Trustworthy `<lastmod>`; optional on-publish / on-delete regeneration for near-real-time updates.
- [ ] `alkem.io/documentation` sitemap via `@docusaurus/plugin-sitemap`, added to the index / robots.
- [ ] `welcome.alkem.io` + marketing (`website-alkemio`) sitemap + robots directive, joined under the
      GSC domain property via a root cross-host sitemap index.
- [ ] GSC monitoring in place (Coverage tracking + fetch-error alerting).
- [ ] **SEO-quality track (flagged — decide early):** per-route `<title>`/meta/`canonical`/`og:url`
      and/or prerender/SSR of public pages — required for discovered URLs to actually index and rank.
      Scoped as its own story/epic if pursued.
t: SEO - Sitemaps

## Description
As a Space or Subspace admin
I want to add a **Form** to a Post and define the questions it asks
So that I can collect structured input from my community, instead of relying on free-form posts or an external form tool

As a Space member
I want to submit a response to a Form
So that I can share the requested information in a structured way, knowing who will read it

## Goal
Give Spaces a native way to collect structured input, closing the gap where communities reach for external form tools. This unblocks the VNG use case end-to-end, which needs responses that are **not** visible to the whole Space, an **email notification** when they come in, and a way to review 100+ responses at once.

## Hypothesis
If admins can add a Form to a Post, they will use it in place of external form tools for structured intake, and will act on submissions faster because visibility and notifications are handled natively. Leading indicators: Form Posts created, responses submitted, and VNG confirming their use case is covered end-to-end without a workaround.
