Tracking issue for GDPR / legal review of self-service account deletion, opened alongside `workspace#054-delete-own-account` (client-web#10107).

Self-service account deletion is being shipped. The feature itself is sound, but adversarial review surfaced a set of **data-protection questions that engineering cannot answer on its own** — several of them are statements we make (or deliberately no longer make) to data subjects. Nothing here blocks the feature; all of it needs an owner.

The published help page has been deliberately written to **claim less** than we previously did, so nothing on it is knowingly false. That conservatism is what this issue is meant to resolve.

---

## 1. Backup retention posture is NOT established — highest priority

**We do not currently know what our backup retention actually is, and we have twice published a figure that was wrong.**

- The spec originally asserted "deleted data ages out of the restore window within 14 days". That was a **misreading**: `infrastructure-operations/.github/workflows/daily-backup-management.yml:129` reads `if age_days > 14: return False, "older_than_2_weeks"` under the comment *"Don't process backups older than 2 weeks"*. It declines to **thin** older backups — it does not delete them.
- A separate 30-day boundary exists at line 318 of the same workflow, governing the replication window.
- Neither figure has been confirmed by an infrastructure owner.

**Action taken:** every concrete timing has been withdrawn from the product documentation and from the spec (FR-024, US6-AS2, plan.md, research.md, T401). The page now says data can persist in backups and that we cannot state a fixed period, pointing users at support.

**Needed:** an authoritative statement of the real retention posture for (a) the primary database backup store, (b) the off-site archive, (c) the file backup store — then a decision on whether to publish it.

## 2. Deletions are not re-applied after a restore — the real Art. 17 exposure

Keeping a deleted user's data in a backup is defensible under the standard "beyond use" position. **Restoring that backup and silently resurrecting the account is not.**

There is currently **no step in any restore runbook** that says "re-apply any deletion executed after the snapshot timestamp". This is a process gap, not a code gap, and it is cheap to close. It belongs with the DR runbook work in `infrastructure-operations` spec 010.

## 3. What the file backup store actually is

`orchestration/overlays/production/.../file-backup-service/12-file-backup-service-config.yml` documents `alkemio-file-backup-prod-immutable` as provisioned with Object Lock COMPLIANCE, 30-day default retention, versioning enabled, and a worker credential with no delete permission (verified live 2026-07-28).

Separately, the **database** backup Object Lock posture (spec 010 T046/T047/T050) is **unbuilt**.

During review these two were conflated in both directions. We need one authoritative answer per store, because the difference determines whether an Art. 17 erasure request can be technically refused for file backups.

**Related:** an earlier draft of the help page told users that file copies "cannot be deleted on request at all". That is a public Art. 17 technical-impossibility refusal. It has been **removed** pending sign-off. If we want to say it, it needs DPO approval and a spec amendment; if we don't, no action.

## 4. Failed deletion clean-up is never automatically completed

The post-commit legs (session revocation, sign-in identity removal, file-bytes removal) are best-effort: each failure is caught, logged and written to an audit row. There is **no retry and no reconciler** (risk R-9).

The help page previously claimed we are "alerted and finish it automatically". That claim has been **removed**. It now says failures are recorded so the team can finish them, explicitly not automatically.

**Needed:** either an operational commitment (who watches those audit rows, and how often) or a reconciler story. Right now the honest position is "a human might notice".

## 5. Erasure is knowingly incomplete — chat identity

Account deletion does not touch the user's Matrix/Synapse identity: display name, avatar and room memberships survive indefinitely.

This is **not a regression** — the existing global-admin deletion path does nothing about Matrix either (`communication.adapter.ts` has `syncActor` and room/space operations but no deactivate/erase; `deleteUser` makes zero adapter calls). Every user ever deleted by an admin still has a live Synapse account.

`matrix-adapter` already implements `SynapseAdmin.DeactivateUser(ctx, userID, erase)`; it is only wired to bootstrap cleanup and has no RPC surface. A follow-up story is recorded (R-4).

**Needed:** a view on whether the current state is acceptable for a platform that tells users their account is deleted, and how long the follow-up may wait.

## 6. Files uploaded into other people's Spaces survive

Files a user uploaded into someone else's Space keep their rows, their bytes, and the departed user's `createdBy` uuid. Contributions are de-attributed in the UI ("Former member") but the identifier persists in the database.

The page now discloses this and offers support as the removal route. **Needed:** confirmation that "de-attributed but identifier retained" is an acceptable position, or a story to null the identifier.

## 7. Deleting an account does not cancel its subscription

Per an explicit product ruling, an active subscription does **not** block deletion. The deletion path makes **no billing-provider call at all** — it records the stored subscription reference into the audit row for finance reconciliation, and proceeds.

The page now states plainly that deletion does not cancel the subscription and that the user should cancel first, because afterwards they cannot reach it.

**Needed — two separate questions:**
- **Finance:** who reconciles those audit rows, so we do not keep billing a deleted account?
- **Legal:** Dutch fiscal law (Algemene wet inzake rijksbelastingen art. 52) requires roughly 7 years' retention of administrative and invoicing records, which likely **requires** retaining billing data through Art. 17(3)(b). Please confirm that retaining billing records while deleting the account is the correct posture, and that our privacy notice reflects it.

## 8. PII published to the external notification pipeline at the moment of erasure

The self-deletion path passes the departed user's display name and email to the external notification pipeline as part of the operator "user profile removed" notification — on the very path that erases them. Note this feature spent its entire BREAKING schema budget removing those same two fields from the **in-app** payload for exactly this reason, so the two halves are now inconsistent.

Tracked as `sec-server-20` (medium, accepted for this release). **Needed:** a view on whether operator notifications may carry the erased subject's PII, and for how long that pipeline retains it.

---

## Not GDPR, but found alongside and needing an owner

- **Production OAuth client secrets in cleartext.** Four `client_secret:` values (Microsoft, GitHub, LinkedIn, CleverBase) are committed in cleartext in `infrastructure-operations/orchestration/overlays/production/third-party/identity/ory/01-overlay-kratos-values.yml` (lines 38/48/58/67), with no SOPS or sealed-secret envelope. The repo is **private**, so the exposure is bounded to those with repo access rather than the public internet — but the values are in git history permanently, so **rotation at each provider is required; deleting the lines is not sufficient.** Pre-existing; unrelated to this feature.
- **`kratosService.getAuthenticatedAt` is a false control.** It takes `MAX(authenticated_at)` across **all** of an identity's active sessions and returns `undefined` on error (fails open), so it would pass a hijacked session the moment the legitimate user signs in elsewhere. Nothing in this feature depends on it — that was deliberate — but it should not be built on by anything else. Tracked as T-W3.
- **Unhandled promise rejection crashes the server** — filed separately as alkem-io/server#6404.

---

## Summary of what changed in the product documentation

| Previously claimed | Now |
|---|---|
| Failed clean-up is "finished automatically" | Recorded so the team can finish it — explicitly not automatic |
| "Uploaded files" removed immediately | Narrowed to your own profile/account; files in others' Spaces disclosed as retained |
| File backups "cannot be deleted on request at all" | Removed pending DPO sign-off |
| Backups pruned after 30 days / 14 days | No concrete period stated; points to support |
| "Billing is reconciled separately" | Deletion does not cancel your subscription and never contacts the provider |

Spec artifacts (`specs/054-delete-own-account/`) have been amended to match, and the withdrawal of the 14-day figure is recorded in the spec's Decision log with the evidence.
t: GDPR/Legal review: self-service account deletion — retention posture, restore re-application, and erasure completeness

## Description
Whiteboards on Alkemio are currently free-standing drawing surfaces. A whiteboard lives inside a callout but knows nothing about the Space or Subspace it sits in, and nothing in the domain model points back to what was drawn on it. Every whiteboard starts from an empty canvas, and any connection between a whiteboard and the entity it describes exists only in a user's head.

This epic is about making whiteboards first-class citizens of the domain model: seeded from the context they are created in, and referenced from that context in return.

Supersedes #478, which described the same intent against the old Hub/Challenge model and a now-defunct `ecosystemModel`. The data shape that issue named no longer exists under the unified Space/Subspace model and `whiteboard.entity.ts` — but the idea underneath it was never delivered and has no other home in the backlog.

## Goal
Whiteboards stop being a detached side artefact and become a working surface on the Space's actual content — lowering the cost of starting one, and making what happens on them recoverable afterwards.

## Hypothesis
Most whiteboards begin by manually re-typing context that the platform already holds (the Space name, its tagline, who is in the community, which callouts exist). If a whiteboard opens already seeded with that context, more get started and more get finished. And if the domain model holds a reference back to the whiteboard, the thinking done on it stays findable instead of being lost the moment the session ends.

## Must have scope
- [ ] Whiteboard can be seeded with data from its parent Space/Subspace — at minimum `displayName` and `tagline` from the profile
- [ ] Domain model holds a reference from the parent entity to the whiteboard (the modern equivalent of the original "store the link to the canvas as a reference on the challenge")
- [ ] Decide which entities can own such a reference: Space, Subspace, Callout, others?
- [ ] Seeded elements render as real Excalidraw elements, editable and deletable like any other

## Open questions
- Which domain data is actually worth seeding beyond name + tagline — community members, existing callouts, subspace structure?
- Is seeding a one-time snapshot at creation, or does it stay live if the underlying entity changes? (One-time is far cheaper and probably sufficient.)
- Does this belong to whiteboard templates rather than the whiteboard entity itself — i.e. a template that declares "insert the Space name here"?
- Relationship to `whiteboard-collaboration-service` and `excalidraw-yjs`: does seeding happen server-side at creation, or client-side on first open?

## Stakeholders
Product, Engineering (server + collaboration services)

## Design
Figma file:
_Comments are highly appreciated. When commenting in Figma, please also leave a note in the comments box below this issue to notify us_

## Additional context
Original epic: #478 (closed as obsolete, 25 Aug 2026)
Original initiative doc: https://hackmd.io/sv10h26kRXOo_0dINkp8Bw
t: Whiteboards: interaction with the domain model

## Description

Bring the Matrix/Synapse space hierarchy into line with the Forum reorganisation delivered in `workspace#060-forum-reorganisation` (issue #2052, merged).

Forum categories are mirrored into Matrix as one invisible space per category, parented under the Forum space, and every discussion room is anchored under its category's space. Feature 060 changed the category set and made posts movable between categories — **the Matrix side does not currently follow any of that**.

Space ids are derived deterministically server-side:

```
space id = uuidv5(`${forumId}:category:${categoryValue}`, FORUM_CATEGORY_NAMESPACE)
```

`matrix-adapter` has **no category awareness at all** — the entire mapping lives in `server`. Verified: the only `categor` match in the Go repo is an unrelated error-code comment, and `synapse-migrator` has none.

## Scope

Four items were raised. They differ enormously in cost, so they are separated here rather than treated as one lump.

### 1. Two new category spaces (`newsletter`, `tips-and-tricks`) — **no code needed**

`ForumService.createForumMatrixSpaces` runs **only at forum creation**, so the 060 migration added the two values to `forum.discussionCategories` without creating anything in Matrix.

They are created by either path already in place:
- **lazily**, by `ensureForumMatrixHierarchy` on the first discussion posted in that category, or
- **in bulk**, by the existing audited `adminCommunicationSyncSpaceHierarchy` mutation, which loops `forum.discussionCategories`, checks `getSpace` first and creates only what is missing (idempotent).

**Action: an operational runbook step, not development.** Run the sync mutation after the 060 migration. Already recorded in the 060 rollout notes. This item should not consume implementation effort.

### 2. Rename the Help space to "Q&A" — **server-only, small**

060 relabelled Help to "Q&A" in the client (all six locales) while deliberately keeping the stored value, slug and Matrix key as `help` (decision D-01). The Matrix space's **display name** is set once at creation from the raw category value and never updated, so the space is literally named `help`.

The primitive already exists end to end — **no adapter change and no library publish**:

| Layer | Available today |
|---|---|
| server | `CommunicationAdapter.updateSpace(...)` |
| AMQP | `communication.space.update` |
| adapter | `SpaceService.UpdateSpace(ctx, contextID, name, topic, avatarURL, joinRule, isPublic, customState)` |

**Open decision — do not implement before resolving.** Every category space is currently named with its raw kebab value (`platform-functionalities`, `challenge-centric`, …). Renaming only `help` makes it the sole exception. Options:

- **(a)** Rename all category spaces to human display labels. Problem: the server has no i18n layer; labels live in client-web's six locale files. Which language wins? English is the only defensible answer, and it hardcodes an English string server-side.
- **(b)** Rename only `help` → "Q&A", accepting one inconsistency to match what users are told the category is called.
- **(c)** Leave raw values and accept that Matrix space names are internal identifiers, not labels — consistent with them being invisible.

Whichever is chosen must also cover **newly created** spaces, or the next category reintroduces the divergence.

### 3. Re-parenting on recategorisation — **the expensive item; a fourth repo**

Feature 060 made posts movable between categories. `updateDiscussion` deliberately does **not** re-parent the room, because it cannot be done safely today (recorded as **A-07**, council-unanimous).

The adapter's hierarchy surface is **add-only** — verified in `internal/core/ports/matrix.go`:

```
GetSpaceChildren · AddSpaceChild · SetSpaceParent
```

There is no remove-child and no unset-parent, and `communication.hierarchy.set_parent` is the only hierarchy AMQP topic. Calling `SetParent` on a category change therefore yields **permanent dual parentage**: the room becomes a child of both the old and new category spaces, with two `m.space.parent` events, and the existing reconciler is add-only so it can never repair it. That is strictly worse than leaving it stale, which is why 060 does nothing.

Doing this properly requires, in order:

1. **matrix-adapter (Go)** — a remove-child / unset-parent operation. Matrix supports it (MSC1772): a child is removed by sending `m.space.child` with empty content for that `state_key`, and the reverse link by clearing `m.space.parent`. Needs the port method, the `SpaceService` implementation, and tests.
2. **A new AMQP topic** + request/response DTO + protocol table entry (`pkg/dto/commands.go`).
3. **`@alkemio/matrix-adapter-lib` publish**, and a server bump — server pins `0.8.16` **exactly**.
4. **server** — call remove-then-add on category change, with defined semantics for a partial failure (if the remove succeeds and the add fails, the room is orphaned from the hierarchy). Matrix calls here are currently swallow-and-log and are **not** on the mutation's critical path; that must stay true, so this needs an out-of-band or retryable design rather than a synchronous call inside `updateDiscussion`.
5. **infrastructure-operations** — adapter image bump for deploy.

### 4. Backfill and lifecycle reconciliation — **time-sensitive, and the item most likely to be missed**

Point 3 only fixes moves made *after* it ships. The 060 curation pass is **moving posts right now**, so every post moved before this lands will carry a stale Matrix parent. A forward-only hook does not fix them.

This item needs:
- a **reconciliation pass** that reads each discussion's category and repairs its room's parentage (which requires the remove primitive from item 3, so it is strictly downstream);
- a decision on **orphaned category spaces after retirement**. Retiring a category leaves its space in place — nothing prunes it, verified: the sync service has no delete path. The spaces are invisible and the retired category's rooms stay parented under them, which is what keeps tombstone posts coherent. `DeleteSpace` exists in both the adapter and the server adapter if cleanup is wanted. Because ids are deterministic, re-adding a category later reuses the same space.
- an **audit/report mode** worth having regardless: `ensureForumMatrixHierarchy` and the anchoring call are swallow-and-log, so hierarchy drift can already exist silently today with nothing surfacing it.

## Sizing note — read before prioritising

**None of this is user-visible today.** Every category space is created with `io.alkemio.visibility: {visible: false}`, and nothing in server reads the hierarchy back — `getSpaceChildren` has zero non-test callers. The value is Element-side coherence and not accumulating structural debt, not a user-facing defect.

Weigh that against the cost: item 3 drags `matrix-adapter` in as a fourth repo plus a library publish and an image bump. Items 1 and 2 are cheap and independent; item 3 is the real project and item 4 depends on it.

A defensible split is to do **1 (ops) and 2 (small server change)** immediately, and take **3 + 4** as their own delivery with the design questions below answered first.

## Decisions needed before implementation

1. Category-space naming: option (a), (b) or (c) from item 2 — and how new spaces get named.
2. Is re-parenting worth a fourth repo and a library publish, given nothing reads the hierarchy? An explicit yes/no, recorded.
3. Failure semantics for remove-then-add: accept a transient orphan and retry, or make it out-of-band?
4. Retired categories: prune the orphaned space, or leave it as the tombstone anchor?
5. Backfill: repair all historical drift, or only from a cut-off date?

## Evidence

Everything above was verified against the code on the merged 060 branch:
- `server/src/platform/forum/forum.service.ts` — `createForumMatrixSpaces`, `ensureForumMatrixHierarchy`, `getCategoryContextId`
- `server/src/platform-admin/domain/communication/admin.communication.space.sync.service.ts` — creates missing category spaces idempotently; has no prune path
- `server/src/services/adapters/communication-adapter/communication.adapter.ts` — `createSpace` / `updateSpace` / `deleteSpace` / `setParent` / `getSpaceState`
- `matrix-adapter/internal/core/ports/matrix.go` — add-only hierarchy surface
- `matrix-adapter/internal/core/service/space_service.go` — `SetParent`, `UpdateSpace`, `DeleteSpace`
- `matrix-adapter/pkg/dto/commands.go` — one hierarchy topic
- `agents-hq/specs/060-forum-reorganisation/` — decisions A-07 (no re-parenting), D-01 (Help relabelled in place), and the rollout note for the sync mutation

Source delivery: #2052 · server#6456 · client-web#10265 · test-suites#628 · agents-hq#137
t: Forum ↔ Matrix hierarchy sync: category spaces, rename, and room re-parenting

### Downtime & live sessions

*Deploy sequencing is not listed as a task: the pipeline is `validate-inert-artifacts → backup → migrate → deploy`, each gated on the previous, identical in the ACC and PROD workflows. Server and client deploy in the same final job, server first. Nothing to co-ordinate by hand.*

**Live memo and whiteboard collaboration sessions are NOT dropped by this release.**

- `collaboration-service` — the only service whose restart would sever every live session (`strategy: Recreate`, `replicas: 1`) — **stays at `v0.0.3` and is not redeployed**.

### Trust gateway (new service) — status 09.09 12:30 UTC

**What it is.** `alkemio/trust-gateway` is the Cleverbase signing gateway for memo signing: it holds the Cleverbase client credentials, runs the OAuth service/credential legs, calls `signatures/signHash`, embeds the signature and RFC 3161 timestamp, and answers `POST /v1/verify`. ### Release notes

**Memo signing arrives — sign a memo with your eIDAS identity through Cleverbase.** From a memo, Sign renders its current content into a timestamped PDF server-side, shows you exactly what will be signed, and submits it to Cleverbase; the signed PDF comes back with the signature embedded and is attached to the memo. Signing again adds a new, separately timestamped copy — earlier ones are never replaced. A memo is never itself "signed": it stays a living, editable document, and signatures attach to fixed PDFs capturing a point in time. Signed copies are visible to anyone who can read the memo.

⚠️ **Signing is not operational in this release** — the trust gateway is not deployed, so the Sign button will show an error. Do not announce the feature until the gateway is live.

Also in this release: admin role controls now explain themselves instead of failing after the fact; loading behaviour is calmer across the app (⚠️ the visible word "Loading" no longer appears on full-page loads — intentional, still announced to screen readers); whiteboard drafts older than 7 days are now cleaned up; build reproducibility restored.

## Description
alkem-io/alkemio#1985 shipped structured Classifications on the **Space** entity only. This Epic extends the same two-step interaction to **Posts**.

Primary persona: Space owners who want a consistent vocabulary and search ability across for example a knowledge base.

Two distinct pieces of work sit inside this:
1. **New host entity** — attaching the shipped Classification model to Posts. Largely reuse of the Space implementation; the host-entity attachment is the new work.
2. **Callouts-Set inheritance** — a new concept, with its own semantics (non-retroactive removal, per-Post override) and a configuration UX that has not been designed.

## Goal
Extend structured, aggregatable metadata from the Space level down to the content inside it, so that reporting and discovery work at the level where contributions actually live.

## Hypothesis
This will allow admins to structure their content better.

## Must have scope
- The same `+` control next to Tags on Post create and Post edit, with the identical two-step add-then-select flow
- Space owner can configure a **default classification set** at the Callouts-Set level
- Posts inherit the default set on creation; contributors can override or add to the inherited set on their own Post
- Removing a default classification from the Callouts-Set does **not** retroactively strip it from existing Posts
- Each Post classification is an independent snapshot — same copy-not-link rule as Spaces
- Post classifications render alongside Post Tags in all views (Post detail, Post cards in a callout)
- The picker offers the same template sources as the hosting Space (platform-wide + top-level Space's library)

## Product questions
- [ ] Posts already carry a **system-reserved `task` classification tagset** in production — Release 73 shipped the Kanban task board (alkem-io/server#6391) where a POSTS callout becomes a Tasks board via that reserved tagset, and alkem-io/server#6398 strips/replaces it when contributions move between callouts. User-authored and system-reserved classifications will sit on the same entity: how are they kept apart in the UI, and can a contributor see or edit the reserved one?
- [ ] **Filtering Posts by classification value is not tracked anywhere.** #2042 is scoped to Spaces only. As written this Epic delivers capture-and-display for Posts with no way to filter on it — the same gap the Space iteration shipped with. Does filtering come in scope here, or does #2042 widen?
- [ ] Where is the Callouts-Set default set configured — callout settings, Space settings, or the template that produced the callout?
- [ ] Does this replace the existing flow-state tagset behaviour for users, or coexist with it? (Open assumption carried over from #2077.)

## Stakeholders
Product Circle, plus design (Callouts-Set default configuration UX).

## Design
None yet — the Callouts-Set default configuration needs a design request. #1985's mockups (alkem-io/product#2161) cover the Space About flow only.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When a change in the URL or name ID (of a space) occurs, the existing links associated with the old URL fail. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A mapping between the new URL/name ID and the old URL/name ID. Anything referencing the old URL auto-resolves to the new URL, and 404s are avoided. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Create a workaround page for manual redirection.

b:
Raised from the architect review of alkem-io/matrix-adapter#71 (finding 5), deliberately deferred out of that PR to keep the safety fix small. It is not a correctness bug in the hierarchy contract — it is that the write budget does not mean what its name implies.

## What is wrong

**`maxOperations` is advisory, not enforced.** The server accumulates writes and compares *after* a whole call has completed, with `>` rather than `>=`:

```ts
cumulativeWrites += added + removed + pruned_unknown + parent_pointers_repaired;
if (cumulativeWrites > input.maxOperations) aborted = 'budget-exhausted';
```

So a call that is already over budget still runs to completion before anything stops, and the boundary itself is off by one. In the reviewer's reproduction `maxOperations=1` allowed three writes.

**The unit is wrong.** `parent_pointers_repaired.length` counts *children*, but one child's repair can perform several state writes (one clear per stale pointer, plus the set). Inferring state-event cost from a repaired-child count under-counts exactly where the budget matters most.

**The rate limiter is per-call.** It is constructed inside each `SetChildren`, so every call gets an immediate first write. It paces within a call but is not an aggregate limit across successive calls, across other adapter topics that write to Synapse, or across adapter replicas.

**Unknown outcomes are counted optimistically.** A call whose response is lost to a transport timeout may have performed writes that the server never counts.

## What it should do instead

- Send the *remaining* allowance in the request and enforce it in the adapter at the write site, alongside the adapter's own safety ceiling. Stop dispatching at the exhausted boundary rather than after the fact.
- Return explicit attempted/succeeded state-write counts and a budget-exhausted status; never infer state-event cost from repaired-child counts.
- Account for unknown RPC outcomes conservatively, or recover operation status, before claiming a strict per-pass budget.
- Share pacing at the bot/homeserver scope across calls and topics, coordinate the state-write and pointer/join budgets, and document how multiple adapter replicas share the allowance.

## Why it was deferred

The operation is operator-invoked and the hierarchy work per pass on the current forum is small, so an imprecise ceiling is a real but bounded problem: the adapter still paces within a call, and Synapse's own rate limiting remains the backstop (the `rate_limited: false` exemption was reverted under D-17 precisely so that backstop stays in place). The destructive-removal and completion-contract findings were the ones that could lose data, and those are fixed in #71.

Worth doing before this operation is run on anything larger than the forum, or before any non-operator-triggered caller is added.

## References

- Architect review: https://github.com/alkem-io/matrix-adapter/pull/71#issuecomment
- `internal/core/service/hierarchy_budget.go`
- `src/platform-admin/domain/communication/admin.communication.forum.hierarchy.reconcile.service.ts`
- workspace spec `061-forum-matrix-hierarchy-sync`
t: Forum hierarchy reconcile: enforce the write budget where the writes happen, with accurate units

b:
Make the web client send the real server error message and code into Sentry, not a generic wrapper.

Who: Marlise (error monitoring, probably low priority)

To what end: When a server call fails, the client often shows a generic message to the user (for example "Upload on visual failed!", or when you visit a page you do not have access to you see the about page with an apply button) and sends the raw error object to Sentry. In Sentry these become uninformative issues titled things like "Object captured as exception with keys: extensions, locations, message, path", so you cannot see why anything failed. If each captured error carried the server's message, its error code, and which operation it was, then error monitoring would show the cause, you could triage by cause, and you could count specific failure types (like the upload limit) straight from Sentry without a dedicated event for each one.
t: Send the real server error message into Sentry

## Description

As a developer, I want a view to have a complete and clear structure, like:

```
<HubProvider>
  <Layout>
    <Breadcrumbs paths={} />
    <Tabs currentTab={} />
    <Content>
       <Piece1 />
       <Piece2 />
    </Content>
  </Layout>
<HubProvider>
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] From within a page component, all the structure of what's on the page is clearly visible.
- [ ] A page component has no or very little outside logic except for the router and some top-level context providers.

## Additional Context

Benefits:
1. This gives a complete overview of which visual components a certain page incorporates.
2. This gives declarative access to components props (e.g. `<Tabs current={}>` or `<Breadcrumbs paths={} >`) without the need to leverage hooks for Breadcrumbs or guessing what is the currently active Tab (doing the Router work twice).
3. This gives a DI-way of specifying which layout a page has: the page specifies the type of layout and its structure, rather than being rendered within some fixed parent context (hence minimal privilege and single responsibility). Example: let’s say for Login or Privacy Policy page we want to leverage a completely different UI including the top elements.

Currently the contents of a single page are split across multiple components at different levels of hierarchy, e.g. Tabs are rendered from the Routing component.
t: Improve top-level views structure

b: The installed PWA shows a cropped logo on an unpredictable background, and iOS "Add to Home Screen" installs a screenshot of the page instead of an icon. Static assets and install metadata only — no application code, no dependency, no config change. Branch `115-pwa-assets-revamp`. ## Defects | # | Defect | Effect | |---|---|---| | 1 | `manifest.json` declares the 192×192 icon as `"sizes": "128x128"` | Browsers trust the declaration; the icon is rejected or rescaled | | 2 | The 512×512 icon is declared `"purpose": "any maskable"` but is full-bleed — **130,356 px of the logo fall outside Android's safe circle** | Android masks to a circle and shaves the mark | | 3 | Every install icon is transparent (**182,236 translucent px** in the 512×512) | Composited against the platform's backdrop; iOS uses black | | 4 | `` is commented out, and pointed at `logo192.png` — 225×137, not square | iOS installs a page screenshot | | 5 | `public/site.webmanifest` — empty `name`, added 2021, **never referenced by any file in any commit** | Contradicts the real manifest's `theme_color` | | 6 | `index.html` and `manifest.json` say `theme_color: #000000`; the dead manifest says `#ffffff` | Black status bar framing a white splash | Transparency (#3) is real but is **not** what crops the icon. A white background alone would leave #1 and #2 in place and ship a still-broken icon that merely looked different. fixing this ## Changes **`public/icons/`** — three files, all downscaled from one master: `icon-512.png`, `icon-192.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png` (180×180). Opaque, white-backed, square, declared sizes matching true dimensions, logo at a consistent 72.5% of the width across all three. **`manifest.json`** — four entries over the two icon files, each declared once `any` and once `maskable`. `theme_color` and `background_color` → `#ffffff`. Favicon entries dropped (icons under 192px are ignored by install prompts). **`index.html`** — `apple-touch-icon` link restored and repointed; `theme-color` → `#ffffff`; explicit `` for the 16×16 and 32×32 favicons so they aren't orphaned. **`service-worker.js`** — push `icon`/`badge` repointed off the deleted `android-chrome-192x192.png`. Reference update only; push assets belong to #023. **Deleted**, each verified unreferenced: `site.webmanifest`, `android-chrome-{192x192,512x512}.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png` (orphan), `logo192.png`. **Untouched:** `Dockerfile`, `env.sh`, `nginx.conf`, `vite.config.mjs`. The favicon family keeps its transparent artwork so it still reads on dark tab strips. ## Two notes for later **Maskable is declared, but backed by the same file as `any`.** Android crops every home-screen icon to the launcher's shape; without a `maskable` icon Chrome shrinks and letterboxes it. A maskable icon normally needs its own file, because a *square* mark inside the 80%-diameter safe circle spans only ~56% of the width and looks lost on platforms that never mask. The Alkemio mark is round — inside the circle it still spans ~78%, which is how a normal icon is framed. **If the mark ever becomes square, split the files.** Avoid the combined `"any maskable"` string. It let full-bleed artwork claim maskability without the claim being checked — that is how #2 shipped. **Replacing the artwork:** one square PNG, opaque white, 1024×1024 preferred, logo at ~80% of the width. Measure it against a centred circle of 80% diameter, **not** the square's edges — a master can look correctly padded and still overshoot (one did, by 150 px, invisible to the eye). Check at https://maskable.app/editor. Old icons are not kept for stale clients: nginx serves PNGs `immutable` for a year, so anyone holding the old files won't revalidate anyway, and the new `/icons/` paths are cache-busting by construction. ## Before merge - [ ] Install on Android Chrome — mask clips nothing; splash has no seam - [ ] Install on iOS Safari — a real icon, not a screenshot, not on black - [ ] Install on desktop Chrome - [ ] Lighthouse PWA audit: no icon/size/purpose findings
t: PWA assets: fix cropped, transparent install icon and missing iOS touch icon

## Description

When a space template is created out of an existing **subspace**, the resulting template may not contain all of the source subspace's callouts across all innovation flow states (phases).

Reported once by Simone: after creating a space template from a subspace and then using that template to create a subspace in another space, **all callouts from one phase were missing** in the new subspace. Callouts in the other phases came through as expected.

## Steps to reproduce

Not reliably reproducible yet - observed once. Rough path:

1. Take a subspace that has callouts distributed across several innovation flow states.
2. Create a space template from that subspace.
3. In a different space, create a subspace from that template.
4. Inspect the callouts in each flow state of the new subspace.

## Expected behaviour

The new subspace contains every callout from the source subspace, each in the flow state it had in the source.

## Actual behaviour

Callouts from at least one flow state are missing entirely from the created subspace.

## Open questions / where to look

- **Is the template itself incomplete, or is the loss at apply time?** Worth checking the stored template content (`templatesSet` → space template `contentSpace`) directly for the affected template. If the phase's callouts are absent there, the bug is in template *creation*; if they are present, the bug is in subspace *creation from template*.

- Does it correlate with a specific flow state (e.g. the last one, or one with no callouts visible on the default tab), or with callouts that are in a non-default state at the time the template is taken?

## Notes

Single anecdotal occurrence, no reproduction case captured. If anyone hits this again, please note the source subspace, the template, and the target space so the template content can be inspected before it's overwritten.

b: ## Summary In **global search**, a callout and the framing resource it wraps are returned as **two separate results** and rendered as **two cards in the same "Posts" section** — even though they are the same thing. For Collabora documents the two cards carry a **byte-identical `href`**, so both clicks land on the same callout view. Found while re-testing office-document content search (server#6196 / client-web#9950). The duplication is **not specific to documents** — it applies to whiteboards and memos too, since all three live in the `FRAMINGS` bucket. ## Reproduction Search `resilience` in *Entire platform* against a space with three document callouts named `doc-10-climate-resilience`, `ppt-10-climate-resilience`, `xls-10-climate-resilience`, plus `doc-01-renewable-energy` (which mentions "resilience" only in its body text). The sidebar reads **Posts 7**, and the section renders 7 cards for **4 actual resources**: | Card | Badge | Author | Date | |---|---|---|---| | `ppt-10-climate-resilience` | Post | Unknown | — | | `xls-10-climate-resilience` | Post | Unknown | — | | `doc-10-climate-resilience` | Post | Unknown | — | | `xls-10-climate-resilience` | Document | admin alkemio | 10 Jul 2026 | | `doc-10-climate-resilience` | Document | admin alkemio | 10 Jul 2026 | | `ppt-10-climate-resilience` | Document | admin alkemio | 10 Jul 2026 | | `doc-01-renewable-energy` | Document | admin alkemio | 10 Jul 2026 | The API confirms the overlap — the same `callout.id` and the same URL appear in both `calloutResults` and `framingResults`: ``` calloutResults: calloutId=b754905e… ppt-10-climate-resilience href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/ppt-10-climate-resilience calloutId=8f771d98… xls-10-climate-resilience href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/xls-10-climate-resilience calloutId=0066d4f8… doc-10-climate-resilience href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/doc-10-climate-resilience framingResults (COLLABORA_DOCUMENT): calloutId=8f771d98… xls-10-climate-resilience href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/xls-10-climate-resilience calloutId=0066d4f8… doc-10-climate-resilience href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/doc-10-climate-resilience calloutId=b754905e… ppt-10-climate-resilience href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/ppt-10-climate-resilience calloutId=7f82709c… doc-01-renewable-energy href=/adminspacepublic/collaboration/doc-01-renewable-energy hrefs present in BOTH buckets: ppt-10…, xls-10…, doc-10… ``` `doc-01-renewable-energy` appears **once**, because its callout title does not contain "resilience" — only its body text does. That is the tell: **the duplication is driven by the title match**, and a document-framed callout's title is the document's name by construction. ## Root cause The client merges two different API buckets into one section: ```ts // src/main/crdPages/search/CrdSearchOverlay.tsx:230 const mappedPosts = mapPostResults(calloutResults ?? [], framingResults ?? [], fallbackLabels); ``` and maps each to a card independently (`searchDataMapper.ts`): - **callout branch** → `title: callout.framing.profile.displayName`, `type: 'post'`, `href: callout.framing.profile.url` - **document branch** → `title: collaboraDocument.profile.displayName`, `type: 'collaboraDocument'`, `href: collaboraDocument.profile.url` Server-side, `collaboraDocument.profile.url` resolves to the **parent callout URL** — a document has no `nameID`, so there is no deeper route. The two hrefs are therefore the same string, and the two cards are the same destination. The server already has deduplication for exactly this. `buildFoldedCalloutResults` folds matching posts/whiteboards/memos/documents up to their containing callout, deduped by callout id (FR-017). But it only runs when `foldToCallouts` is true: ```ts // server: src/services/api/search/search.service.ts:71-73 const foldToCallouts = Boolean(searchData.searchInFlowStateFilter) || Boolean(searchData.foldCalloutResources); ``` and the only caller that opts in is flow-state search (`src/main/crdPages/space/hooks/useFlowStateSearch.ts:89`). **Global search never folds**, so both buckets come back populated and the client renders both. ## Also affects whiteboards and memos `memos`, `whiteboards` and `office-document` share the `FRAMINGS` category server-side, and `mapPostResults` maps all three into the same section alongside `calloutResults`. Any whiteboard- or memo-framed callout whose title matches will produce the same duplicate pair. One difference worth checking during the fix: whiteboards and memos resolve their profile URL through their own `nameID`, so their two cards may point at *different* URLs (callout page vs. deep link) rather than the identical URL documents produce. The duplicated **entity** is the problem in all three cases; the identical-`href` symptom is specific to documents. ## Secondary inconsistency The two cards for the same resource don't even look alike. The callout card shows author **"Unknown"** and **no date** (`callout.createdBy` is `null` and the mapper hardcodes `date: ''`), while the document card shows the real author and creation date. So the duplicate is not merely redundant — it is redundant *and* contradictory. ## Impact - Users see the same result twice and cannot tell the cards apart by destination. - The sidebar count is inflated (7 for 4 resources). - Interacts with pagination: duplicates consume slots in the 4-per-page budget. ## Possible fixes (needs a product/architecture call) 1. **Client-side dedupe.** When merging `calloutResults` and `framingResults`, drop the callout card when one of its framing resources is also present (match on `callout.id`), keeping the more specific resource card. Smallest change; lives entirely in `mapPostResults`. 2. **Server-side.** Omit a callout from `calloutResults` when its own framing resource matched and is being returned in `framingResults`. ## Summary

Users are landing on **`https://identity.alkem.io/home`**, a dead end that renders the 404 page when there is no session. `/home` is an apex-only route; `identity.alkem.io` is the Kratos identity host. Something is navigating to `/home` **relatively**, so it resolves against whichever origin the SPA happens to be on — and during auth/logout flows that is the identity subdomain.

Sentry: https://alkemio-bv.sentry.io/issues/117541389/events/ade56f0d1ea54e19af2e36cc6e3641f1/

> Note: the Sentry event itself was not readable while writing this ticket (auth required), so the exact triggering flow is not yet confirmed from telemetry. Everything below is derived from the code. The ranked hypotheses should be checked against the event's `referrer` / breadcrumbs.

## Why it 404s

`src/domain/platform/routes/NonIdentity.tsx:41-43`:

```ts
if (isIdentityOrigin) {
  return <CrdNotFoundView />;
}
```

`NonIdentity` wraps the `/home` route (`src/main/routing/TopLevelRoutes.tsx:77-86`). It bounces to the apex **only** when `isAuthenticated && !!platformOrigin`:

```ts
const shouldRedirectToNonIdentity = !isLoading && isIdentityOrigin && isAuthenticated && !!platformOrigin;
```

So on the identity origin **without a session**, it falls straight through to `CrdNotFoundView`. That is precisely the reported "no session → 404 page".

Both hosts serve the same SPA build (`identity.alkem.io/meta.json` and `alkem.io/meta.json` both report `0.156.2`), and both return HTTP 200 — the 404 is rendered client-side.

## How users get there — relative `/home` navigations

Three places navigate to `/home` without guaranteeing the apex origin:

1. **`src/core/auth/authentication/pages/LogoutPage.tsx:69`** — a bare relative literal:
   ```ts
   // outcome.kind === 'cleared'
   window.location.replace('/home');
   ```
2. `src/core/auth/authentication/hooks/useSignUpReturnRedirect.ts:62`
3. `src/core/auth/authentication/pages/LoginSuccessPage.tsx:34`

(2) and (3) share the fragile join `` `${platformOrigin ?? ''}${path}` ``. `usePlatformOrigin` (`src/domain/platform/routes/usePlatformOrigin.ts:11`) returns `locations && \`https://${locations.domain}\``, i.e. **`undefined` until the Configuration query resolves** — and the `?? ''` fallback silently degrades an intended absolute navigation into a same-origin relative one.

`resolveInternalReturnPath` (`src/core/utils/links.ts:52-71`) deliberately returns only a path and accepts the *current* origin as valid, precisely so the caller re-prefixes the apex. `src/core/utils/links.test.ts:63` even encodes this:
```ts
expect(resolveInternalReturnPath('https://identity.sandbox-alkem.io/home', undefined)).toBe('/home');
```
That `/home` then gets `''`-prefixed and replayed on whatever host is current.

## Most likely trigger (ranked)

1. **Logout, leg 2.** `useLogoutUrl` documents: *"Kratos's own `logout.after` config decides the landing page."* If that lands the SPA on `identity.alkem.io`, `LogoutPage` reaches `outcome.kind === 'cleared'` and runs the bare `window.location.replace('/home')` → `identity.alkem.io/home`. The session is gone by definition at that point → `NonIdentity` → 404. This matches the "no session" symptom exactly.
2. **Post-verification landing.** `useSignUpReturnUrl.ts:62-64` notes Kratos's verification email link "redirects straight to its configured landing page (`/home`)". Kratos runs on the identity host, so a relative `/home` there lands on `identity.alkem.io/home`. If the browser has no session yet → 404. (Fix may be server-side Kratos config rather than client-web.)
3. `useSignUpReturnRedirect` / `LoginSuccessPage` firing before `platformOrigin` resolves. Both require an authenticated session, so these are less consistent with the reported symptom, but the `?? ''` fallback is still a latent bug.

## Regression window

- `53193c458` — *Feat/003 alkemio OIDC idp (#9856)*, 2026-06-11 — introduced the bare `window.location.replace('/home')` in `LogoutPage`.
- `5db027ecb` — *fix the redirectUrl logic after sign in/sign up*, 2026-07-09 — introduced the `${platformOrigin ?? ''}` join and `resolveInternalReturnPath`.

Note `useRedirectToIdentityDomain.ts:1-5` already documents this **exact class of bug** from a previous incident:

> `/login` and `/logout` removed: … Bouncing to the identity subdomain caused LoginPage's relative `window.location.replace` (`/api/auth/oidc/login`) to 404 there.

## Suggested fix

Post-auth navigations to `/home` must be **absolute against the apex**, never relative:

- Replace the bare `'/home'` in `LogoutPage.tsx:69` with an apex-prefixed URL.
- Remove the `?? ''` fallbacks. When `platformOrigin` is `undefined`, either wait for the Configuration query to resolve or derive the apex from the base domain — never navigate relatively.
- Consider a single helper (e.g. `absoluteApexUrl(path)`) so the apex prefix cannot be forgotten at a fourth call site, and add a regression test asserting no post-auth redirect ever resolves to the identity origin.
- Separately, confirm Kratos's `logout.after` and verification `default_browser_return_url` point at the apex, not a host-relative `/home`.

## Repro

1. Ensure no session.
2. Visit `https://identity.alkem.io/home`.
3. Observe the client-rendered 404 (HTTP 200, `CrdNotFoundView`).

For the real flow, log out and follow the redirect chain with devtools "Preserve log", watching for a hop that stays on `identity.alkem.io`.
t: Users land on identity.alkem.io/home — relative /home redirect 404s on the identity subdomain

## Summary

The save-path (WOPI) outage indicator delivered in #10023 (FR-017 of workspace#015) **does not surface in practice**. When the wopi-service is down mid-edit, Collabora keeps the document editable and buffers changes into its own server-side session, but our disconnect indicator + top alert never appear — reproducing the ❌ hero101 reported on TC3.

Root cause is **two independent problems**; detection needs both halves working.

## 1. Client gate trusts Collabora's unreliable save-state (confirmed)

`useCollaboraSaveHealth` arms the `collaboraServiceAvailable` probe only while `saveStatus !== 'saved'`. But Collabora Online (COOL) emits `Doc_ModifiedStatus{Modified:false}` as soon as it buffers a change into its **own** session memory — i.e. it reports "saved" even though the storage write (PutFile → wopi → file-service) is failing.

Observed live (parent-page postMessage log, wopi pod stopped, actively editing):

- COOL held `Modified=false` for ~108s straight while every save was failing → our probe **disarmed** → indicator cleared.
- On **manual Ctrl+S** during the outage, COOL emitted `Doc_ModifiedStatus{Modified:false}` (falsely "saved"), then showed its **own** internal "Document cannot be saved, please check your permissions" modal via `_onError → showConfirmModal` — which **never crosses the postMessage boundary** (no `Action_Save_Resp`, no `Error`). So the probe is disarmed at the exact moment saves are failing, and there is **no hookable message** to react to instead.
- The COOL footer shows "Saved" while "Last saved: 16m ago" — its saved-chip reflects buffer state, not storage state.

Net: the `saveStatus !== 'saved'` gate is closed precisely when we need detection. And because there's no save-failure postMessage, a message-hook approach is off the table.

## 2. Server signal never observed returning `false` (unverified)

Across testing we **never captured `collaboraServiceAvailable` returning `false`** during a confirmed outage — only `true`, and un-correlated to the down-window (couldn't tell when they fired). On manual save it doesn't fire at all (probe disarmed, see #1).

So we cannot currently prove the server half works end-to-end. Two possibilities:
- The probes returning `true` were pre-outage baseline, and during the real down-window the probe was disarmed (#1) so it never asked — in which case fixing #1 is sufficient.
- The server's `/health` reachability check (`wopi.service.adapter.ts checkHealth`, hitting `storage.collabora.wopi_service_url` + `/health`) returns 2xx even when the pod is down (baseUrl routing / traefik), in which case there is a **second bug** to fix on the server/env side.

**Verification needed (one clean capture):** stop the wopi-service pod, type *continuously* to hold `Modified=true` so the probe keeps firing, and read the `CollaboraServiceAvailable` operation's boolean in the GraphQL Network tab. `false` → server signal OK, only #1 to fix. `true` → server/env bug to fix too.

## Proposed fix (client)

Stop trusting COOL's momentary `Modified` flag. Run the side-effect-free `collaboraServiceAvailable` probe on a **slow heartbeat** (~20–60s, existing backoff-while-healthy retained) for as long as the editor is open **and recently edited**, independent of the instantaneous save-state; **debounce** so the indicator stays steady through the outage rather than flapping with `Modified`. When down → show our indicator with our own clear wording (also mitigates the misleading COOL "permissions" text). Gate polling on `document.visibilityState` to avoid polling backgrounded tabs.

**Trade-off to weigh:** `/health` isn't free server-side (DB ping + NATS + up-to-2s Collabora probe). Bounded to actively-edited visible docs at one call per interval it's negligible for normal usage, non-zero at scale — pick the interval accordingly.

## Scope / boundary (documented, not bugs)

- **No hookable save-failure message** — COOL handles the failure internally; we can only ever overlay our own indicator, never intercept/replace COOL's modal.
- **"Healthy but this save rejected"** (expired token / lock / permission, `/health` green) stays undetectable by design — the only save-path-exact probe is the editor-URL query, which mints tokens, takes locks, and logs analytics per call (self-defeating). This is the accepted FR-017 boundary.

## Context

- PR: alkem-io/client-web#10023 (workspace#015)
- Server query: alkem-io/server#6264
- Related cosmetic bug: #9973 (lingering "Unsaved changes")
- Extended-outage data loss: tracked separately (see companion [wopi-service issue](https://github.com/alkem-io/wopi-service/issues/30)).
t: OfficeDocs: save-path (WOPI) outage indicator doesn't surface — COOL masks save-state; server signal unverified

**Describe the bug**

Changing your account password does not terminate any existing session — not the Kratos SSO session, and not the OIDC BFF `alkemio_session` that actually gates the API. After a password change, every session that existed beforehand, on every device, keeps full authenticated CRUD access.

This makes the password change actively misleading: the user receives a security-signal email telling them the change was observed, which implies the account has been secured, while an attacker's pre-existing session retains full access for up to the BFF absolute TTL (30 days).

Found while verifying the fix for #9965 — I was trying to use "change password on another device" to revoke a Kratos session server-side, and discovered it revokes nothing.

**To Reproduce**

1. Log in to Alkemio in browser A. Confirm you are logged in and CRUD controls work.
2. In browser B (separate profile/device), log in as the same user and change the account password.
3. Return to browser A and refresh.
4. You remain fully logged in with working CRUD. `ory_kratos_session` is still present and valid; `alkemio_session` is untouched.

**Expected behavior**

Changing the password should terminate the user's other active sessions — both the Kratos SSO sessions and the BFF `alkemio_session` records — so that the password change actually locks out anyone holding a pre-existing session. The session driving the change itself may be preserved (re-issued) so the user is not signed out of the device they are working on.

**Additional context**

There are two independent gaps, both required for the expected behaviour:

1. **Kratos side** — the self-service settings flow has no session-revocation hook. In `.build/ory/kratos/kratos.yml`, `selfservice.flows.settings.after.password.hooks` contains only the `web_hook` to `kratos-webhooks`. `revoke_active_sessions` appears zero times across both `alkem-io/server` and `alkem-io/infrastructure-operations`.

2. **BFF side** — the `USER_PASSWORD_CHANGED` pipeline is observe-only. `PasswordChangedConsumer` → `UserPasswordChangeObserverService.handleObservedPasswordChange` performs `auditService.record(...)` + `publishSecuritySignal(...)` and nothing else. No Redis session tombstone, no Hydra token revocation. This is the gap explicitly deferred in client-web#10053: *"Server-side revocation propagation: Kratos session revocation (password change / logout-all / admin) should tombstone the actor's BFF sessions in Redis — today a revoked identity keeps API access until the BFF session dies."*

Note that since the OIDC BFF migration the BFF session is the sole authority for both API access and (after client-web#10053) the login indicator. So revoking only the Kratos session would not be sufficient — the BFF tombstone is the part that actually removes access.

**Related**

- alkem-io/client-web#9965 / #10053 — the login-indicator investigation this surfaced from. #10053 fixed the indicator divergence and explicitly deferred revocation propagation.
- alkem-io/server#6073 — *OIDC: session management UI — per-session revoke + sign out of all devices*. Not a duplicate: that story covers **user-initiated** revocation from a UI, and explicitly lists *"Account-event cascade (deactivate / password-changed / admin-force-revoke) and the associated webhook → Hydra / Synapse fan-out"* as out of scope. This issue is that deferred cascade, now with an observed reproduction. The per-user Redis session index proposed in #6073 is the natural mechanism for both.

**Areas that will be affected**

_To be added during refinement._ Likely: Kratos settings-flow config (`server/.build/ory/kratos/kratos.yml` + the infra Kratos values), the `kratos-events` consumer/observer path in `server`, the OIDC BFF Redis session store, and Hydra token revocation.
t: BUG: Password change does not revoke existing sessions (Kratos or BFF) — pre-existing sessions keep full access

A `accepted_cookies` consent cookie holding **valid JSON that is not an array** (e.g. `true`, `42`, `{"a":1}`) crashes the app into its error boundary. The entire site is replaced by *"Looks like something went wrong: `s.includes is not a function`"* and there is no user-discoverable way out — clearing site data is the only recovery.

Found while investigating an unrelated nightly E2E failure. Reproduced on **acc** (`test-alkem.io`) on 2026-08-07.

## Cause

`src/core/analytics/apm/useApmInit.ts`, in `useGetOrSetApmCookie`:

```ts
const cookieId = cookies[APM_CLIENT_TRACK_COOKIE];
if (cookieId) {
  return cookieId;                       // early return — see precondition below
}
const acceptedCookies: string = cookies[ALKEMIO_COOKIE_NAME];
if (!acceptedCookies || !acceptedCookies.includes(AlkemioCookieTypes.analysis)) {
```

The annotation `const acceptedCookies: string` does not match runtime. `react-cookie` JSON-parses cookie values, so this is a `string[]` in practice — the cookie is written as `JSON.stringify(['technical','analysis'])`. Arrays and strings both implement `.includes`, which is why the wrong type has never surfaced. A boolean, number or plain object does not, and the `TypeError` escapes into the error boundary.

Note the throw produces **no uncaught `pageerror`** — the boundary catches it. Monitoring keyed on uncaught errors will not see this.

## Reproduction

1. Open a **new incognito window**. The profile must have no `apm` cookie for the domain.
2. Go to `https://test-alkem.io/home`. The consent banner appears — **do not accept**.
3. In the DevTools console:
   ```js
   document.cookie = 'accepted_cookies=true; domain=.test-alkem.io; path=/'
   ```
4. Reload.

The app is replaced by the error screen. Recovery: Application → Clear site data, or expire the cookie manually.

**Precondition:** the browser must hold no `apm` tracking cookie — `useGetOrSetApmCookie` early-returns on it before reading the consent value. So anyone who has accepted analysis cookies is immune, and the exposed population is visitors who declined analysis or never consented.

## Likelihood — low, but the blast radius is total

- No shipped build produces a crashing shape: every writer since #2267 (2022) uses `JSON.stringify` of an array.
- Corruption and truncation are **safe** — an unparseable value comes back from react-cookie as the raw string, and strings have `.includes`.
- Only valid-JSON-wrong-type triggers it, which random damage essentially never produces.

**One vector I could not verify:** `useAlkemioCookies.ts` notes that `welcome.alkem.io` writes this same cookie at the shared apex domain, and that consent given there is already read by the platform. If that codebase ever writes a non-array value, every platform visitor without an `apm` cookie would hit this. Worth a check by someone with access to that source.

## Suggested fix

Guard the shape at the read, and correct the type:

```ts
const acceptedCookies: unknown = cookies[ALKEMIO_COOKIE_NAME];
if (!Array.isArray(acceptedCookies) || !acceptedCookies.includes(AlkemioCookieTypes.analysis)) {
  return undefined;
}
```

Worth auditing other `useCookies` readers for the same mistyped-as-`string` assumption.

## Test coverage

A regression guard is committed as `test.fixme` in the QA repo — `client-web/src/functional-e2e/language-offer/us3b-review-fixes.spec.ts`, test `corr-client-2b` (alkem-io/test-suites@0e4b9dbd). It is skipped so it does not red the nightly; un-`fixme` it once the read is shape-guarded and it becomes a live regression test.

The sibling case (an *unparseable* cookie) is already covered and passing as `corr-client-2`.
t: Wrong-shape accepted_cookies value crashes the app: s.includes is not a function

## Bug

When a whiteboard collaboration connection drops, we show the **"Whiteboard disconnected"** modal with a loading spinner and a **Reconnect** button. If the user **switches networks** (e.g. WiFi → mobile) while one or more whiteboard tabs are open, the loading gets stuck and the **Reconnect button stays permanently disabled**, leaving the user with no way to recover except manually reloading the tab.

## Root cause

The modal's Reconnect button is enabled purely off the browser's online status:

- [`CrdWhiteboardDialog.tsx:335`](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/blob/develop/src/main/crdPages/whiteboard/CrdWhiteboardDialog.tsx#L335) wires `canReconnect={isOnline}`.
- [`WhiteboardDisconnectedDialog.tsx:73`](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/blob/develop/src/crd/components/whiteboard/WhiteboardDisconnectedDialog.tsx#L73) disables the button when `!canReconnect || reconnecting`.
- The auto-reconnect countdown (`useAutoReconnect`) is **paused while offline or connecting**, so the timer never fires either.

On a network switch, `navigator.onLine` (via `useOnlineStatus`) can stay stale for several seconds to tens of seconds. During that window `isOnline` is `false`, so the Reconnect button is disabled **and** the auto-reconnect countdown is paused — the modal appears frozen with no user-actionable escape.

## Requested change

Add a **"Reload page"** button to the "Whiteboard disconnected" modal as a guaranteed escape hatch:

- It calls `window.location.reload()` (full page reload), independent of `isOnline` / `canReconnect` state.

## Summary

Whiteboard collaboration: the "Whiteboard disconnected" modal could get stuck with a disabled **Reconnect** button and a paused countdown — most reproducibly **after a network switch** (e.g. WiFi → mobile) with a whiteboard tab open — leaving the user no way to recover except manually reloading the tab. This adds a **"Reload page"** escape hatch to that modal.

Fixes #10131. Delivered in PR #10136.

## What changed (user-facing)

- The "Whiteboard disconnected" modal now offers a **"Reload page"** button (full page reload) in addition to **Reconnect**.
- It appears:
  - **immediately** once a reconnect **attempt fails** (`connect_error`) — e.g. the server/network is unreachable after a switch; and
  - **after ~6s** if the modal is otherwise stuck (offline / reconnect disabled), so it stays off the normal fast-reconnect path.
- The button is **always clickable**, independent of the browser's online status (which can stay stale for seconds-to-tens-of-seconds after a network change).
- Normal fast auto-reconnect and the countdown behaviour are unchanged; a brief transient drop that self-heals does **not** show the button (avoids nudging users into a reload that would discard unsynced strokes).
- New i18n key `disconnected.reloadPage` added across all 6 locales (en, nl, es, de, fr, bg).

## Root cause

- The Reconnect button was gated on `navigator.onLine` (`canReconnect={isOnline}`), which lags a real network switch, and the auto-reconnect countdown (`useAutoReconnect`) is paused while offline/connecting.
- While **online**, the countdown cycles `connecting`, so the dialog's own "stuck" timer kept resetting and the reload button would otherwise never surface — fixed by threading the connection-failure reason (`connect_error` vs transient `disconnect`) from `Portal` → `Collab` → `useCollab` → the wrapper, and passing it to the dialog as `hasError`.

## Scope

- **client-web only.** No `whiteboard-collaboration-service` change required.
- Files: `Portal.ts`, `Collab.ts`, `useCollab.ts`, `CollaborativeExcalidrawWrapper.tsx`, `CrdWhiteboardDialog.tsx`, `WhiteboardDisconnectedDialog.tsx`, whiteboard i18n locales; tests: `WhiteboardDisconnectedDialog.test.tsx`, `portalCloseConnection.spec.ts`.

## Verification

- Unit/integration tests green (dialog visibility/timeout/error/callback; `connect_error → error`, `disconnect → non-error`, intentional close silent).
- Manual repro: with a whiteboard open, drop the collab connection and switch networks — the modal now provides a working "Reload page" action.

## Release note (suggested)

> **Whiteboards:** Fixed the disconnected-whiteboard modal getting stuck after a network change; added a "Reload page" recovery button.
t: Whiteboard: "Reload page" recovery button for stuck disconnected modal (fix for #10131)

## What this is

The code side of alkem-io/alkemio#2075: a new `src/core/matrix/` module in client-web that logs the browser into Synapse silently, keeps that session alive, and cleans up on logout. Behind a flag that is off by default. It renders nothing yet; later tasks build the chat screen on top of it.

Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801. Status: built (PR alkem-io/client-web#10215), proven live on sandbox.

## What it does

- Loads the Matrix SDK only when the flag is on and a user opens chat (flag off = nothing loads, bundle unchanged).
- Runs the silent SSO login in a hidden frame and exchanges the one-time token for a Matrix session.
- Stores the tokens in a per-user IndexedDB namespace; refreshes the access token every 15 minutes; recovers without a prompt while the Alkemio login is valid; fails closed otherwise.
- On logout or user switch: stops the client, tells Synapse (3-second limit), wipes the namespace, tells the other tabs.
- Elects one tab to run the sync stream; other tabs mirror its state and take over if it closes.
- Exposes a diagnostics handle (`window.__alkemioMatrix`) with state and a redacted last error, never a token.

## Done when

- [x] A signed-in user gets a Matrix session with no second prompt.
- [x] Exactly one sync stream per user per browser, however many tabs are open.
- [x] After logout or user switch nothing of the previous user is reachable.
- [x] Expired or revoked sessions recover silently or show a recoverable error, never a wrong identity.
- [x] With the flag off nothing changes; turning it off again needs no migration.
- [x] Unit tests cover the state machine and the "no tokens in logs" rule (173 tests, both flag states).

## Depends on

alkem-io/alkemio#2075 (the contract) and the Synapse config change in alkem-io/dev-orchestration#83 (token lifetimes, SSO whitelist).

## Not in this task

Showing conversations from Matrix (#10158), sending (#10159), per-user rollout groups, production environments.

## Read more

Spec: https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/053-matrix-browser-session/specs/053-matrix-browser-session

## What this is

Make the chat screen read from Synapse instead of the Alkemio server: the list of conversations, the full message history, live updates, unread counts and read receipts. Rolled out in three steps per environment: off, shadow (sync silently, show nothing, compare), render (show it).

Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801 (gates 5 and 6). Builds on the session foundation (#10157).

## In plain terms

Matrix's sync stream already gives a client everything a chat screen needs. Once a user is on "render", that stream is their only source of messages; the server's old message feed is switched off for them so nothing arrives twice. Membership and room creation still go through the server.

## What changes

- First, a measurement on sandbox: push a few thousand small state events into one room and record initial-sync time and size (this decides the storage choice and is a datapoint the wider platform is waiting for).
- A per-environment switch `VITE_APP_MATRIX_READ_STAGE` = off | shadow | render, on top of the existing user allowlist. Rollback is flip plus reload; no migration.
- Shadow mode: sync for the cohort, compare rooms, timelines and unread state against the GraphQL path, publish the diff as gate evidence.
- Map each conversation to its room via the `#t_<id>` alias plus the server's new readiness and repair API; verify the "missing room" case (alkem-io/alkemio#2015) on this path.
- Render mode: room list, timeline, scroll back to the oldest message (beyond today's 1,000 cap), reconnect catch-up, unread and highlight counts, read receipts; replies, edits, deletions, reactions and mentions rendered from Matrix events; media events arrive via sync but bytes still resolve through the server.
- A persisted IndexedDB sync store (default) so reloads are instant.
- For the render cohort, stop consuming the GraphQL message feed; keep only control-plane events.
- A transport header on remaining GraphQL calls so the rollout counters can tell migrated reads apart.

## Done when

- [ ] History and new events match Element on agreed fixtures, once each, in order.
- [ ] Scrolling reaches the oldest accessible message.
- [ ] Unread counts and receipts agree between Alkemio web and Element.
- [ ] Offline, reconnect and multi-tab produce no missing or duplicate events.
- [ ] Each Matrix event has exactly one source in the browser; GraphQL carries only control-plane events.
- [ ] Media events render through the existing #1946 path without trusting a forged document id.
- [ ] alkem-io/alkemio#2015 is verified on the new path.

## Depends on

#10157 built and applied; shadow needs nothing else. Render needs: the security sign-off on alkem-io/alkemio#2075, alkem-io/matrix-adapter#69 landed, alkem-io/server#6378's readiness API accepted, the wave-0 measurement recorded.

## Open product questions

Typing indicators and presence (currently not rendered, not sent). Who owns the "resolve attachment by room and event" server surface (until then, attachments show as placeholders for the cohort).

## Read more

Spec: https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/065-matrix-direct-reads/specs/065-matrix-direct-reads

## What this is

Let the browser send messages straight to Synapse: send, reply, edit, react, delete your own message, mark as read. Show each message as "pending" until Synapse confirms it, never as sent when it was not. Attachments keep their current route through the server for now.

Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801 (gate 7). Builds on the read path (#10158); may only spread to more users once alkem-io/server#6379 proves notifications still fire.

## In plain terms

Sending becomes a two-step dance the user does not notice: the bubble appears at once as pending, the browser sends with a transaction id (so a retry can never post twice), Synapse answers with the real event id, and the same event comes back through sync and replaces the pending copy.

## What changes

- The migrated set, declared: send, reply (Matrix "in reply to", not threads), edit, delete own, react, read marker. Everything else stays on GraphQL and is listed.
- A per-room send queue (one failed room must not block others); pending, sent, failed and retrying states follow what Synapse actually said; nothing is blindly resent after a session renewal.
- Three checks that exist only in the old server path (consent at send time, closed callouts, assistant-sender rule) each get a ruling: move to the client, enforce in Synapse via alkem-io/matrix-adapter#69, or accept as no longer enforced.
- Attachments unchanged: upload still goes through the server; the browser never emits a media event carrying the trusted document id.
- Never from the browser: create room, invite, kick, change settings. The code is checked for their absence.
- Element interoperability both ways, including `m.mentions` so highlights work in Element and in web.
- A per-environment switch `VITE_APP_MATRIX_WRITE_STAGE` = off | direct on top of the read stage; when on, zero GraphQL message mutations for the migrated set; each operation declares its transport for the rollout counters.
- A 403 from Synapse (removed member) ends the attempt, no retry loop.

## Done when

- [ ] Each operation round-trips web → Element and Element → web without losing meaning.
- [ ] Pending, sent, failed and retrying reflect the real outcome.
- [ ] Reconnect and retry never create duplicates.
- [ ] Removed members cannot write after the measured window.
- [ ] Zero GraphQL message mutations for migrated operations; attachment operations counted separately.
- [ ] Attachments still work exactly as #1946 built them, including its documented limitations.

## Open product questions

A mention picker (none exists today), rich formatting for Element readers, what happens when consent is withdrawn after a chat exists, deleting attachments.

## Read more

Spec: https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/067-matrix-direct-writes/specs/067-matrix-direct-writes
t: Move conversation message operations to matrix-js-sdk

## Summary
The committed generated Apollo artifacts under `src/core/apollo/generated/` (`graphql-schema.ts`, `apollo-hooks.ts`, `apollo-helpers.ts`) have drifted behind the current server GraphQL schema. Running codegen against an up-to-date schema regenerates ~1100 lines of changes unrelated to any single feature — the client's generated types no longer fully reflect the server contract.

## Evidence
Running codegen against the current server worktree schema:

```
pnpm exec graphql-codegen --config codegen.yml --schema ../server/schema.graphql
```

produces ~1100 insertions across the 3 generated files (new types such as `AssistantCapability`, `CalloutContributorsMapView`, `ContributorLocation`, `CalloutSelectionSettings`, …) that are not part of the feature currently in flight.

## Impact
- A feature branch adding a new GraphQL operation can only safely include its own operation's generated slice, because a full regeneration would bundle the entire unrelated drift.
- Type-checking against the server contract is incomplete until the generated types are re-synced.

## Repro
1. Have an up-to-date server schema (`server$ pnpm run schema:print`) or point at a develop server `/graphql`.
2. `pnpm exec graphql-codegen --config codegen.yml` (or `--config` a copy whose `schema:` is the schema file path — the CLI `--schema` flag does not override the config's `schema`).
3. Observe the ~1100-line diff under `src/core/apollo/generated/`.

## Proposed disposition
A dedicated codegen-sync PR against `develop`: regenerate all three files against the current server schema, review the diff, and land it as its own change. Until then, feature branches include ONLY their own operation's generated slice.

_Source-of-truth tracking issue for the 006 collab-content-unification client work: the whiteboard AssetAdapter branch deliberately includes only its own `WhiteboardAssetDocument` operation's generated slice (not the full schema sync) to avoid bundling unrelated drift._
t: Generated Apollo types are stale vs the server schema (codegen drift)
