## Description

As a subspace admin I want to be able to customize the side panel (left panel) of my subspace, the same way this is now possible for an L0 Space.

Follow-up to #10092 (*Space Sidepanel*), which explicitly scoped customization to L0 and left L1/L2 out ("L1 and L2 not affected, may come later"). Now that the L0 side panel is configurable, the demand for the same on subspace level is significant — subspaces are where most day-to-day collaboration actually happens, and the current fixed set of widgets does not fit the way people use them.

**Jeroen is working on a design; this issue is opened to capture the need and start refinement. The design will be attached / linked here once available.**

## Problem

The current subspace side panel ([`SubspaceSidebar`](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/blob/develop/src/crd/components/space/SubspaceSidebar.tsx)) has a fixed composition that admins cannot change:

- a hard-coded set of **quick actions** (Community, Events, Activity, Index) that many subspaces do not want at all;
- **no events list** — only a quick-action icon that opens a dialog, where L0 has a proper Upcoming Events widget;
- **no search and no tag filtering for posts**, which is the most requested item: subspaces accumulate a lot of posts and there is currently no way to find them from the panel.

## Proposed direction

### 1. One panel for the whole subspace — explicitly *not* per phase

The subspace side panel is **one single panel**, the same on every innovation flow phase. This is a deliberate design choice and **must stay that way**: the flow phases are content tabs, the panel does not reconfigure itself when switching phase.

This is a deliberate difference from L0 in #10092, where the panel is configurable *per tab*. For subspaces the configuration is **per subspace**, applied to the whole subspace.

### 2. Configurable widgets

Admins can enable/disable and order the available widgets, reusing the widget model and settings UI from #10092 where possible. At minimum:

| ID | Name | Notes |
|----|------|-------|
| `intent` | Intention & Leads | The info block with subspace description + leads |
| `about` | About this Subspace | About button |
| `createPost` | Add Post | Create post button |
| `search` | **Search & tags for posts** | **New — the main driver for this issue** |
| `events` | Upcoming Events | Real events list widget (as on L0), not just a quick-action icon |
| `updates` | Latest Update | Community updates |
| `subspaceLinks` | Subspaces | Nested subspaces list |
| `virtualContributors` | Virtual Contributors | |
| `index` | Post Index | |
| `quickActions` | Quick Actions | Should be removable |

### 3. Search and tags for posts

The highest-value item. Search within the subspace's posts from the panel, with tag chips to filter. Should align with the existing sidebar search behaviour (see #10267 for the tag-chip overflow refinement) rather than introducing a second pattern.

### 4. Identical for L1 and L2

The side panel settings, the available widgets and the settings UI are **exactly the same for L1 and L2** — no differences between levels.

### 5. Part of the (sub)space template

The side panel configuration must be **captured in the (sub)space template** and round-trip like the other layout settings: creating a subspace from a template applies the template's side panel configuration, and saving a subspace as a template stores it.

### 6. Visibility rules unchanged

As in #10092: existing permission-based visibility rules still apply. A widget that is invisible today for a given role stays invisible; the setting only controls whether/where it appears when the user is allowed to see it.

## Open questions for refinement

- Defaults for existing subspaces: keep them visually identical to today, or ship an improved default (e.g. search on, quick actions off)?
- The #10092 migration already writes side panel settings to subspaces and subspace templates but keeps them hidden and inactive — can that data model be reused as-is, or does the per-tab → per-subspace difference require a different shape?
- How does a subspace template's side panel configuration behave when that template is used to create an **L0** space (which is per-tab)?

## Areas that will be affected

- [ ] Subspace settings > Layout: component to enable/disable/sort side panel widgets (identical for L1 and L2)
- [ ] `src/crd/components/space/SubspaceSidebar.tsx` — widget-driven instead of fixed composition
- [ ] New search + tags widget for subspace posts
- [ ] Events widget reused from the L0 side panel
- [ ] Server: settings model for L1/L2 side panel + migration/defaults
- [ ] (Sub)space template round-trip of the side panel settings

## Related

- #10092 — Space Sidepanel (L0), parent epic alkem-io/alkemio#2000
- #10267 — Sidebar search: keep selected tag chips visible ahead of the +N overflow
- #10255 — BUG: Subspace's own sidebar card disappears when the subspace has no description
t: Subspace Sidepanel: customizable left panel for subspaces (incl. search & tags for posts)

## Context

CodeRabbit review of hotfix PR #10310 found three reachable defects in memo-signing return code already merged to `develop` via #10305 (`ac5e1bcb2d012f2971e718f54681b5354924782c`). They must be fixed on `develop` first; after human merge, the exact develop fix can be cherry-picked with `-x` onto #10310 for develop/master parity.

## Root causes

1. `UrlResolverProvider` deliberately skips resolution for paths such as `/user/me`, returning `providerPresent: true`, `loading: false`, `resolutionComplete: false`. `MemoSigningReturnDialogConnector` therefore never settles after consuming the callback token. A blanket `resolutionComplete: true` for the empty/cold state is unsafe because it reintroduces the late-callout Radix modal-order regression.
2. A non-network Apollo/GraphQL error on the returned signing-attempt query maps the signing stage to `undefined` after the single-use token and storage record are consumed, so the user receives no error dialog.
3. Tailwind preflight strips native list semantics from the signing journey `ol` and signed-success `ul`; they lack the explicit `role="list"` required by the CRD convention.

## Acceptance criteria

- Distinguish deliberately skipped URL resolution (terminal/complete) from a cold or in-flight callout resolution (pending). Prove both real paths; preserve the existing modal-order protection.
- Map every returned-attempt query error, including non-network GraphQL errors, to the existing return-error dialog.
- Add `role="list"` to the changed `ol` and success `ul`, with the repository-standard Biome suppression where needed.
- Add discriminating regressions before the product fix using the replay-evidence model; normal hooks and CI must be green on the signed PR head.
- One narrow client-web PR targeting `develop`; no server/schema/provider/PDF change.
- Keep the discriminated-origin prop-type and test-local-cast review nits out of scope unless a concrete runtime defect is proven. The docstring warning is tooling-only.
- Do not merge, deploy, mark Done, or modify the production hotfix in this issue. After the develop PR is human-merged, cherry-pick that merge/fix with `-x` onto #10310 and re-gate the hotfix separately.

Related: #10305, #10310.
t: Fix memo signing return settlement, error feedback, and list semantics

Found during QA of the Release 75.1 patch (alkem-io/alkemio#2126) while verifying the new 1 MB editor-content budget from alkem-io/server#6505. ## Reproduction (ACC, client-web v0.165.1 / server v0.166.0) 1. ## Summary

In **Organization → Settings → Community**, the "Load more" button under **Available users** does nothing and throws an uncaught error in the console. The list never expands past the first page.

Found on ACC (client-web v0.165.1) during Release 75.1 QA. **The same code is on `master` (v0.164.1), so PROD is affected too.** Not a 75.1 regression.

## Reproduction

1. Sign in as an org admin/owner of an organization with more than one page of available users (default page size `AVAILABLE_USERS_PAGE_SIZE`).
2. Open `/organization/<nameId>/settings/community`.
3. Under **Available users**, click **Load more**.

**Actual:** nothing is appended; console shows:

```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
    --> starting at object with constructor 'HTMLButtonElement'
    |     property '__reactFiber$…' -> object with constructor 't5'
    --- property 'stateNode' closes the circle
    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
    at Object.assign.reset (vendor-apollo…)
    at t.getObservableFromLink
    …
    at e.fetchMore
    at v (useRoleSetAvailableUsers…)
```

**Expected:** the next page of available users is appended and the button disappears when `hasNextPage` is false.

## Root cause

`useRoleSetAvailableUsersOnPlatform` / `…OnRoleSet` expose

```ts
const fetchMore = async (itemsNumber = AVAILABLE_USERS_PAGE_SIZE) => {
  await fetchMoreRaw({ variables: { first: itemsNumber, after: pageInfo?.endCursor, … } });
};
```

and the org settings hooks hand that function **directly** to the view as the click handler:

- `src/main/crdPages/topLevelPages/organizationPages/settings/community/useOrgAssociates.ts:104` — `onLoadMore: availableResponse.fetchMore`
- `src/main/crdPages/topLevelPages/organizationPages/settings/authorization/useOrgRoleAssignment.ts:113` — same, for the admin and owner blocks on the **Authorization** tab (very likely broken the same way; please verify)

`RoleMembersEditor` renders `<Button onClick={onLoadMore}>` (`src/crd/components/admin/roles/RoleMembersEditor.tsx:159`), so React passes the `MouseEvent` as `itemsNumber`. Apollo then gets `variables.first = <MouseEvent>` and fails while serialising the variables for the request/cache key — hence the circular-structure error on `HTMLButtonElement`.

## Fix

Wrap the call so the event is never forwarded, e.g. in both hooks:

```ts
onLoadMore: () => availableResponse.fetchMore(),
```

Optionally harden the shared hooks so a non-number argument falls back to the page size:

```ts
const fetchMore = async (itemsNumber?: number) => {
  const first = typeof itemsNumber === 'number' ? itemsNumber : AVAILABLE_USERS_PAGE_SIZE;
  …
};
```

Also worth a look for the same pattern: `DashboardUnauthenticated.tsx:39` and `SpaceExplorerPage.tsx:68` pass `fetchMore` straight as `onLoadMore`; they are only safe if their list component calls `onLoadMore()` without arguments.

## Test

A unit test on `useOrgAssociates` / `useOrgRoleAssignment` that invokes `onLoadMore(new MouseEvent('click'))` and asserts `fetchMore` was called with `variables.first === AVAILABLE_USERS_PAGE_SIZE` would have caught this and prevents the regression.

## Environment

- ACC, client-web v0.165.1 (also present in `master` → PROD v0.164.1)
- Found by @Comoque1 during Release 75.1 QA (alkem-io/alkemio#2126); unrelated to that release's scope.
t: Org settings › Community: "Load more" under Available users throws "Converting circular structure to JSON" and never loads (click event passed to fetchMore)

## Designed and developed by @rtharakan 

## Description

As a collaborator editing a whiteboard together with others in a live session
I want a chat panel next to the canvas where we can exchange short messages
So that we can coordinate during the session without leaving the whiteboard or switching to another tool.

**Phase 1 is ephemeral by design.** Messages exist only for the participants currently connected to the live collaboration session. Nothing is written to the board's content, to storage, or to any database, and nothing chat-related ever appears in the board after a reload. Persistent history and "X joined the session" presence notices are deliberate follow-ups, not part of this story.

Who can chat: exactly the audience that already shares the live session — the same people who see each other's cursors, emoji reactions and the countdown timer, including guests on a public whiteboard link. No new permission surface is introduced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Should let a participant in a live whiteboard session open a chat panel from the toolbar, type a message and send it; every other connected participant sees it appear in real time, attributed to the sender by name and avatar initials, without reloading.
- [ ] Should render the sender's own messages right-aligned and unattributed, and others' messages left-aligned with name, initials and a timestamp, following the platform's existing chat bubble conventions.
- [ ] Should keep the Send control disabled and ignore Enter when the composer is empty or whitespace-only.
- [ ] Should cap a message at 500 characters in the composer, with no silent loss beyond the cap.
- [ ] Should start with the panel closed; when a message arrives while it is closed, the toolbar toggle shows an unread-count badge that clears when the panel is opened, and the canvas is never obscured or interrupted.
- [ ] Should show an empty panel when the whiteboard is reloaded or reopened after everyone has left — no chat history survives the session through any path.
- [ ] Should never include chat content in an exported `.excalidraw` file, a duplicated board, a saved template, or the whiteboard's serialised scene.
- [ ] Should render message bodies as plain inert text only (no markup, no rich text), since messages from other peers are untrusted input.
- [ ] Should not add any chat affordance to the single-user (non-collaborative) whiteboard editor.
- [ ] Should match the Alkemio design system and brand, reusing the existing chat components rather than introducing a new look.

## Additional Context

Scope decisions recorded during specification:

- **Ephemeral only** in this phase. A later phase may add persisted history if longer retention, moderation or export is needed.
- **Plain text only**; emoji typed as unicode characters work as ordinary text.
- **No rate limiting** in this phase, matching the posture of cursors and emoji reactions today. An oversized message from a misbehaving peer is truncated on receipt, not rejected.
- **Presence notices** ("Priya joined the session") are deferred to a follow-up.

Workspace spec: `agents-hq` `specs/063-whiteboard-chat` (branch `feat/063-whiteboard-chat`).

## Areas that will be affected

- `client-web` only: the collaborative whiteboard editor's side rail and the live-session awareness channel.
- No change to the collaboration service, file service, server, or the Excalidraw fork.
t: Whiteboard session chat: live side-chat for collaborators on the same board

**Describe the bug**
On a whiteboard, with an element selected, pressing <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Delete</kbd> (macOS; <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Delete</kbd>/<kbd>Backspace</kbd> elsewhere) does **not** delete the selected element. Instead it opens Excalidraw's **"Clear canvas"** confirmation — *"This will clear the whole canvas. Are you sure?"* — offering to wipe the entire board.

On macOS, Cmd+Delete is the platform convention for "delete the selected item" (Finder, most editors). A user pressing it with a selection active is one reflexive **Confirm** away from clearing a whole shared whiteboard — and because our boards are collaborative (Yjs-synced), the wipe propagates to every collaborator, not just the local session.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open any whiteboard.
2. Select a single element.
3. Press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Delete</kbd>.
4. The "Clear canvas" confirmation dialog appears instead of the element being deleted.

**Expected behavior**
Cmd+Delete with a selection deletes the selected element(s) (same as plain Delete/Backspace), or at minimum does nothing. A destructive whole-board wipe should never sit behind a gesture users reach for to delete a selection; clearing the canvas should stay an explicit menu action.

**Screenshots**
The "Clear canvas — This will clear the whole canvas. Are you sure?" dialog shown over a board with one element selected (selection handles visible behind the dialog).

**Additional context**
Root cause traced — the behavior is **inherited from upstream Excalidraw**, not our code:

- Whiteboards embed `@excalidraw-yjs/excalidraw` 0.5.2 (a fork of `excalidraw/excalidraw`, commit `864353be`).
- Upstream registers `CtrlOrCmd+Delete` as the documented "Clear canvas" shortcut, and its App keydown handler opens the confirm dialog on `CTRL_OR_CMD` + `Backspace`/`Delete` **unconditionally — selection state is ignored** (in the bundle: `event[CTRL_OR_CMD] && (key === BACKSPACE || key === DELETE) → activeConfirmDialog = "clearCanvas"`).
- Our wrapper (`src/domain/common/whiteboard/excalidraw/ExcalidrawWrapper.tsx`) only customizes `UIOptions.canvasActions.export`; it doesn't touch this.
- ⚠️ `UIOptions.canvasActions.clearCanvas: false` alone would **not** fix it: that predicate is only consulted by the menu item (`isActionEnabled`). The keydown path sets the confirm-dialog state directly, and the dialog's Confirm runs `executeAction` without re-checking the predicate. Verified in the 0.5.2 bundle.
- The `clearCanvas` action marks **every** element `isDeleted` and clears all files — on a shared board this syncs out to all collaborators.

Suggested fix direction: intercept <kbd>Ctrl/Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Backspace</kbd>/<kbd>Delete</kbd> at capture phase before it reaches Excalidraw (precedent: the Escape handling in `src/domain/common/whiteboard/excalidraw/excalidrawEscape.ts`) and, when a selection exists, delete the selection via the API instead — leaving clear-canvas reachable only through the menu. Alternatively patch the shortcut out in the `@excalidraw-yjs` fork.

**Areas that will be affected**
_Optional, to be added by developer if relevant_
t: BUG: Cmd+Delete with a selection offers to clear the whole whiteboard instead of deleting the element

b: ## Description As a platform user who receives in-app notifications I want a notification to be marked as read automatically when I view the content that triggered it directly on the platform (by navigating to it myself, not by clicking the item in the in-app notifications dialog) So that my notifications list and unread counters reflect what I have actually already seen, and I don't have to open the dialog just to clear items I am already up to date on ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Should mark an unread in-app notification as read when the user opens the page / item that triggered it (e.g. the post, comment thread, callout, whiteboard, calendar event, space, community application…) by any route other than the notifications dialog — direct navigation, a link, a bookmark, search, etc. - [ ] Should mark as read all unread notifications that point to the same viewed content (e.g. several comment notifications on the same post), not only the latest one - [ ] Should update the unread indicators without a page reload — the counter on the notifications bell, the unread state of the item in the dialog, and the browser-tab badge - [ ] Should only mark a notification as read when the triggering content was actually displayed to the user — not when the user merely visits a parent page (e.g. the space home) where the content is not shown - [ ] Should leave notifications for content the user has not viewed untouched (still unread) - [ ] Should keep the existing behaviour unchanged: clicking a notification in the dialog still marks it as read, and "mark all as read" still works - [ ] Should not resurrect or alter notifications that are already read or archived - [ ] Should apply across the user's sessions — a notification marked as read this way shows as read in other tabs / devices as well ## Additional Context Current behaviour: an in-app notification is only marked as read from inside the notifications dialog (clicking the item, or "mark all as read"). If the user reaches the same content on their own, the notification stays unread and keeps inflating the bell counter and the browser-tab badge, even though the user has already seen it. Open questions for refinement: - Which notification types are in scope for the first increment (all types that carry a link to viewable content, or a subset such as comments / posts / mentions)? - What counts as "seen" for content inside long pages or collapsed threads — page open, or the item actually scrolled into view? - Should chat / conversation message notifications be included, or are they already covered by the messaging read receipts? Related: #10327 (unread tab badge not syncing across tabs) — same unread-state surface. ## Areas that will be affected _To be added during the refinement_ Pointers from a code read, unverified: today the client only exposes `updateNotificationState(ID, state)` and `markNotificationsAsRead(filter: { types })` (`src/main/inAppNotifications/`). Matching "the notifications that point to the content I am viewing" probably needs either a client-side match of unread notifications against the current route/entity, or a server-side filter by triggering entity — likely a `server` slice as well.
t: Mark in-app notifications as read when the triggering content is viewed directly on the platform

## Description

The shared markdown preview renderer (`src/crd/components/common/InlineMarkdown.tsx`, default `sanitize` mode) interprets author-supplied raw HTML and passes inline `style` attributes through `src/crd/lib/rehypeSanitizeStyles.ts`. That allow-list permits `position`, `top`, `left` and `z-index` **without constraining their values**, so a contributor can paste an HTML block into any markdown field rendered by this component and place a full-viewport fixed overlay across the whole application for anyone who opens that page.

Reproduced against the unchanged default mode — the surviving style attribute:

```
position: fixed; top: 0px; left: 0px; width: 100%; height: 100%; z-index: 99999;
```

`DANGEROUS_VALUE_PATTERN` only screens `url(`, `expression(`, `javascript:`, `@import`, `-moz-binding` and `behavior:`; nothing checks positioning values.

This is **pre-existing** and affects every consumer of the default mode (about ten today). It was found during the security review of the expanded subspace cards work (client-web#10033, `workspace#076-expanded-subspace-cards`), which deliberately kept the wider renderer out of scope: the new card-safe mode used by the expanded cards does not interpret raw HTML at all, so that surface is unaffected. Nothing in #10033 makes this newly reachable.

## Suggested fix

Remove `position` and `z-index` (and the offset properties that only matter with them: `top`, `left`, `right`, `bottom`) from `SAFE_CSS_PROPERTIES` in `rehypeSanitizeStyles.ts`, or constrain `position` to `static | relative`. Add a characterisation test that a fixed full-viewport block loses its positioning in default mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A raw HTML block with `style="position:fixed;…;z-index:99999"` renders in default mode without `position`/`z-index` surviving
- [ ] Existing default-mode consumers render unchanged for ordinary content (characterisation tests)
- [ ] No change to the card-safe mode

## Control mapping (from the review)

SOC 2 CC6.1 / PI1.2 · ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.28 (secure coding). Severity: medium.
t: Markdown renderer's default mode allows author-supplied fixed-position overlays (position/z-index pass the style allow-list)

Deferred from #10316 by operator ruling (workspace spec
`specs/077-richer-contributor-cards`, R8). The "…" menu on contributor cards
shipped with *View Profile* and *Message* only. This story adds the third item
the design shows — **Remove from Space**, visible to space admins only.

It looks like a menu item; it is a destructive, multi-service action. The 077
architect council (three seats, code-verified) found the following — treat
each as an acceptance criterion, not a suggestion:

1. **The role set must come from the server, resolved from the post's own
   community** (`callout → community → roleSet`, the resolution
   `ContributorCollectionService.resolveContext()` already performs). It must
   **never** come from the client's `useSpace()`: `SpaceContext` hard-codes
   `spaceId = levelZeroSpaceId` and `level: L0`
   (`src/domain/space/context/SpaceContext.tsx`), so from a post in a subspace
   it yields the **parent's** role set — non-empty, wrong, and it type-checks.
   The removal would strip the person from the parent space. The connector
   receives only a `calloutId` today (`LazyCalloutItem`,
   `CalloutDetailDialogConnector`). Expect one additive nullable server field
   (e.g. `CalloutFraming.contributorsRoleSetID`).
2. **Removal is a cascade, not a record delete.** For a space role set and the
   MEMBER role, `RoleSetService.removeActorFromRole` removes the person from
   the space's chat rooms (Matrix), revokes their credentials in **every
   descendant space** (`revokeSpaceTreeCredentials`), and purges their in-app
   notifications across the tree, then re-applies their authorization.
3. **One role per call.** `removeActorFromRole` revokes exactly one role
   credential, while the card list is the union LEAD ∪ ADMIN ∪ MEMBER
   (`getRankedIdsForType`). Removing MEMBER from a lead leaves the lead
   credential *and the card on screen*; for an admin who is not a member it is
   a silent no-op — while the descendant cascade fires anyway. **Revoke every
   role the contributor holds in that role set, or disable the action for that
   card.** One failing test per combination: member only; lead + member; admin
   only; lead + admin + member.
4. **Self-card guard.** A space admin genuinely holds GRANT, and the server
   additionally extends the policy per request for self-removal
   (`extendAuthorizationPolicyForSelfRemoval`, on an unsaved policy clone — so
   a client privilege read never sees it). "Remove from Space" on your own card
   is a mislabelled "Leave space" wired to the full cascade: never show it.
   **Still contested — decide in this story:** a server-computed per-item
   capability, false on self and without GRANT (systems-architect + operator
   seats: "the client cannot be the only guard"), versus the shipped client
   chain `useRoleSetManager({roleSetId}).myPrivileges` →
   `ROLE_SET_GRANT_PRIVILEGES` → `useActionPermission` pointed at the
   server-supplied role set plus a client-side self check (simplifier seat: the
   server re-authorizes every call, so the flag buys UI accuracy, not safety).
   `SpacePermissions.canUpdate` is the wrong privilege either way
   (UPDATE ≠ GRANT).
5. **Confirmation copy must name the cascade** — access to this space and
   every subspace, removal from its chat rooms, notifications cleared — via
   `ConfirmationDialog` `variant="destructive"` (CRD Golden Rule 9). A generic
   "Are you sure?" is a defect here.
6. **After success refetch BOTH queries** — `ContributorCollectionByType`
   (cards) and `ContributorCollectionConfig` (the per-type counts live there).
   No optimistic update, no cache surgery. Show a pending state (the mutation
   is slow) and render policy-limit rejections (`validatePolicyLimits = true`
   can legitimately refuse, e.g. minimum leads).
7. **Acceptance walk that must exist**: from a Contributors post in an **L1
   subspace**, remove a member → the L1 credential is gone, the parent-space
   membership and sibling-subspace credentials survive.

Note: 077 made `ContributorCollectionItem` a per-post cache record
(`keyFields: false`) — cards of different posts no longer share state.

  leaving an L0 space cascade-deletes the rows of its subspaces. When several
  rows exist for one person and space, use the earliest.
- 077 exposes it on contributor cards at **month precision** (first of the
  month, UTC) as a deliberate data-minimisation choice for a publicly readable
  list. An admin-only settings table may justify day precision — decide here,
  and record the privacy classification.
- **Data trust**: whether historic `createdDate` values survived the
  out-of-repo MySQL→Postgres copy (baseline migration `1764590884532`) was
  checked for 077 by the operator on acceptance data (gate G-1 of that spec) —
  **record that result here before building**. If the dates are
  import-stamped, this column would show the same wrong day for every
  long-standing member.
- Any client formatting of a UTC-truncated date must use the UTC year/month
  (077 decision D-UTC), or viewers west of UTC see the previous month/day.

As a developer I want to be able to easily replace one UserCard component by another without re-mapping properties to a new format, especially given that the data is mostly the same.
The solution would be that all UserCards, such as: ContributorCard, UserCard and LeadUserCard - all take User properties in the same format.
I propose that for that format we use prop names as they are defined in the GraphQL schema; for the long paths, we just skip/join fragments (such as user.profile.avatar.uri becomes user.avatarUri).

Please note that this change would not be trivial since a lot of utils rely on those types (such as mapping functions doing remapping without explicitly specifying the target type), so an automatic refactoring is only possible to some extent.
t: Unify User properties for various User Cards

## Description

As Alkemio organization I want the users to have readable display names,
As an Alkemio developer I want Mentions system to work properly and detect user mentions in messages and other user inputs.


Markdown links are in the form: `[link text](link url)`
We want user mentions to be links to the user profile: `[@User Display Name](https?://alkemio_domain/user/user-nameId)`

We need to make sure that user names don't have characters that can break the markdown link syntax.
A user called `C@rlos` or `[[John Doe]]` or `Jane (old account)` could generate wrong markdown that may endup in not detecting properly the mention or even breaking the comment rendering.

Obviously we should not whitelist only latin alphabet characters: 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/421046/what-are-all-of-the-allowable-characters-for-peoples-names
The way to go is to blacklist characters that can break HTML or markdown, such as `[](){}#"<>` `\` `*` ([maybe more](https://wilsonmar.github.io/markdown-text-for-github-from-html/))

## In the production database
- [ ] Client to replace non-latin characters with appropriate latin characters when generating the mentions links

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Strip markdown characters from suggestions in mentions

## Additional Context
Server already has capability to replace non-latin characters for the generation of nameIDs:  replaceSpecialCharacters in the server + see the associated package.
t: Handle usernames with Markdown-special characters on mentions

- [ ] Select the smallest device that is still sort of commonly used, check whether it has a predefined frame in figma, if not, create a frame for the library.

  - Most commonly used screensizes for phones in Europe 2022 and 2023 | In order of most common (Based upon Statcounter)

Fortunately, we now have lookup queries so we can create ContributionItems from IDs and use lookups in ContributionDetailsContainer.

- [ ] ContributionDetailsContainer should fetch journeys via lookup queries
- [ ] ContributionItems should always contain UUIDs not nameIDs (refactor src/domain/community/user/userContributions/useUserContributions.ts)

## Additional Context
Screen shots / UX designs / data that are relevant.
t: Convert ContributionDetailsContainer to using lookup

## Description

People who can't use a mouse or trackpad, often (if not always) navigate by using their keyboard. You can experience this yourself by using the tab-key and your arrow-keys. You might notice that although the order on most pages of the platform is correct, you often can't actually see where you are. Some browsers indicate this better than other browsers do, but there are many buttons/links that do not have any indication that they're ''highlighted''.
Moreover, you might also notice that you can't access some of the content, for example the info icons and some of the tooltips. 

### Examples of clear indications of where you are:
[Private Zenhub Image](https://api.zenhub.com/attachedFiles/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMUVRQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--0e047de5229913b309d08fd9a524a45f57c19e14/image.png)
[Private Zenhub Image](https://api.zenhub.com/attachedFiles/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMUlRQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--abead04e0c7446c2289d52807d8215fd4b0e1f82/image.png)
And here you can also find nice examples, try tabbing through this website: https://www.accessibility.nl/kennis/zo-zet-je-skiplinks-voor-een-optimale-navigatie

### Examples of no or vague indications where you are:
I see nothing while I'm actually focusing on the Challenges button:
[Private Zenhub Image](https://api.zenhub.com/attachedFiles/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMVVRQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--127b813e8fa14cc5c92b77e639dd54d654430d9b/image.png)


Quite difficult to see that my focus is currently on German (Landing page)
[Private Zenhub Image](https://api.zenhub.com/attachedFiles/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMzhRQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--ef2b76abc0fc64ce4c2b7c8a19a77c0ec7435a9e/image.png)


When using the keyboard, it should be clear where you are on the page. Would be great if we can also style it a bit, so it aligns nicely with the rest of the content (while of course still standing out to be clearly visible)

- [ ] Innovation flow tab - All buttons have an unclear focus area

### Opportunity settings

- [ ] Context tab - All markdown icons have an unclear focus area
- [ ] Innovation flow tab - All buttons have an unclear focus area

As a user invited to a subspace but not a member of the parent space yet, I want to see this invitation on space level as well, since accepting this will give me direct access to the Space. - [ ] When there are invitations to multiple subspaces, open the first invitation that was sent (see comments)

## Description

As a developer
I want readable code

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Should be maybe just created from scratch, it's hard to tell how it works by looking at the code
- [ ] The references API should be consistent. `CreateProfileInput` has the property `referencesData` renamed to `references`.
- [ ] Users should be able to create references with the same name (confirm with product team)
- [ ] Users should not be able to submit references without url (confirm with product team)
- [ ] On delete references cache is updated (open edit dialog > delete a reference > close dialog > open it again, doesn't show the old deleted reference).

## Additional Context
- It has multiple notes and todos from multiple devs who saw this code since it was created in 2021.
- For the communityGuidelines template library I ( @ccanos ) had to create `FormikReferencesSegment`, there was already a `ProfileReferencesSegment`. Then they use `ReferencesSegment` which is a FieldArray with a weird API (push and remove callbacks) which makes things quite difficult. We need to refactor these.
- At the moment, when we are editing an entity, we do have a profile where we can upload references, when we are creating a new entity, that profile (and it's storageBucket) still doesn't exist, so any upload to a reference while creating an entity ends up in the space's StorageBucket or failing.
- Another problem we have at the moment is, if you create 3 references for example, they'll have names 1, 2 and 3. You delete the 2nd, so you have 1 and 3. Then you can't create another one (you get an error), because the name "New reference (3)" is already taken. We think should allow references with the same name.


## Areas that will be affected 
 
_To be added during the refinement_
t: Client: refactor ReferenceSegment

## Description
As a security-conscious product owner, I want to prevent users from using special characters/symbols in their usernames and other fields, So that we can mitigate the risk of malicious scripts being executed through user inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Should restrict the use of special characters/symbols in usernames.
- [ ] TBD Should restrict the use of special characters/symbols in other specified fields?
- [ ] Should allow only the following special characters in usernames and other fields:
- Periods: .
- Underscores: _
- Dashes: -
- Single quote: '
- Back tick: `
- [ ] Should display a user-friendly error message when a user attempts to use restricted characters.
- Error: Invalid Characters. Please use only letters, numbers, periods (.), underscores (_), and dashes (-).
- [ ] Should ensure that existing usernames and fields are sanitized to remove any restricted special characters/symbols
- [ ] Client should prevent using the symbols
- [ ] **Server needs to validate it as well.**

## Additional Context
At least the following symbols should be restricted:

- Ampersand: &
- Equals sign: =
- Apostrophe: ’
- Plus sign: +
- Comma: ,
- Brackets: <, >
- Percent: %
- double quotes: "
- exclamation: !
- Emojis (otherwise mentions are not working :( ) --> Or can we only prevent this in the first couple of characters?

## Areas that will be affected 
 
_To be added during the refinement_
t: Restrict Special Characters/Symbols in User Names (& Other Fields?)

b: **Describe the bug** Looks like the client is not pushing the correct files object until around 10 seconds after inserting the image into the whiteboard. If the whiteboard is closed before the file has been pushed to the server, the image will be lost, a grey image will be shown when the wb is open again. - Not sure if it's always 10 seconds - Not sure if it's always with the first image uploaded or with all the images. **Technical info** See the network log (With firefox you can watch and filter the `SCENE_UPDATE` messages sent by the client: Green arrows are messages with the file added. Red arrows are incomplete messages. - First of all the file is uploaded to the storage bucket - Then we have that first message, which surprisingly has the file and the correct url, but doesn't include the image element - Then another SCENE_UPDATE message without any change, we can ignore that. - Then (the red arrow), we have a message with the element, but it doesn't contain the file - (if the whiteboard dialog is closed here, the resulting whiteboard will not contain the image) - After 12 seconds, we have another message that has the element and the image, that message is good and now we can close the dialog without any problem. We need to dig into Collab and see if we can make the messages more consistent, either the red arrow should contain the file, or either the green arrow should be sent quicker... But another solution may be easier in the server: if the first message with green arrow, that contains the file but it is not used by any element, is not ignored. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Go to a newly created single whiteboard callout. Edit it. 2. Insert an image in the whiteboard 3. Close quickly the whiteboard 4. Open the whiteboard again. 5. See that the whiteboard is not showing the image **Expected behavior** An image can be added and the whiteboard can be closed quicker (or the whiteboard cannot be closed until all the images are properly pushed).
t: BUG: Images take around 10 seconds to be pushed to the server

## Description

As an Alkemio developer I want a stable build of @alkemio/excalidraw fork package
As an Alkemio user I want mermaid-to-excalidraw feature to work

## Context
When we build our excalidraw-fork a build error is thrown. We are ignoring it because it's just a typescript error and the npm package is built correctly, but the problem lays on the fact that:
`@alkemio/excalidraw-fork` is based on `@excalidraw/excalidraw` version 0.17.1 commit `530617be90df8d41f93c7c885d3097565c4c7f6d`

This version has a dependency `@excalidraw/mermaid-to-excalidraw` version 0.3.0 which in turn is dependent on `@excalidraw/excalidraw` version `0.17.1-7381-cdf6d3e` which is older than our excalidraw version and still doesn't have `index` in the `Element`s
That dependency loop ends up in Typescript complaining about an `Element` in Excalidraw not being equal to an `Element` returned by `mermaid-to-excalidraw`.
Also mermaid to excalidraw window crashes when the user clicks on the menu item, so that's already not working.

Tried changing `mermaid-to-excalidraw` to currently latest version `1.1.0` and the problem still persists. So further investigation is still needed. We may even need to fork `mermaid-to-excalidraw` or just remove the dependency and the code related to it.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `yarn build:esm` doesn't throw any errors on Excalidraw fork
- [ ] mermaid to excalidraw dialog doesn't crash the dialog, or is just not available.

## Additional Context

Screen shots / UX designs / data that are relevant.

## Areas that will be affected 
 
_To be added during the refinement_
t: Upgrade / fix / remove mermaid-to-excalidraw dependency of Excalidraw package

## Context
- The useUrlResolver hook in src/main/urlResolver/useUrlResolver.ts needs improvements in its readability and maintainability.
- Also there is a useRouteResolver that could be removed because they share common functionality.
- JourneyTypeName needs to disappear and we should be able to work just with spaceLevel.
- No nameIds should be used for url building. 
- NameId parsing should only happen inside urlResolver hook.
- In general we need to review any usage of NameId and remove it if possible.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Improve readability of useUrlResolver hook
2. Extract the subspace resolution into a dedicated helper function to improve code organization and reusability.
3. Refactor the loading state management to replace multiple `loading = loading || otherLoading` assignments with a more elegant solution.
4. Try a generic approach of calling all the queries with the variables and the skip and a function to return the desired id, and that it sets the loading variable, so it's easier to add new resolvers and not miss anything
5. Implement whiteboards url resolver
6. Replace space url resolver and remove `useRouteResolver` 

## Related PR Discussion
//pull/7515#discussion_r1930709587
t: Finish implementation of useUrlResolver

## Description

As an Alkemio developer I want clean and consistent code

## Context
Zoom to fit functionality was not exposed by excalidraw to the outside API when we started to use their package. After multiple attempts of them implementing it, we ended up forking Excalidraw's package.
We exposed `zoomToFit: boolean` flag in `appState`, to perform that action when loading the whiteboard content, but also we exposed through the external API the function `zoomToFit()`, that the client is also calling after loading the content.

After our upgrade to React version 18 we detected a problem (a loading spinner infinitely staying there in the whiteboards).
That was caused by some error inside Excalidraw's initialization, caused by the `zoomToFit` flag in the `appState`.
The good thing is that we don't really need that `zoomToFit` flag, because we are calling the API function anyway, so we can just remove it.
Also they have finally implemented and exposed something we can use, `scrollToContent` so there is no need to expose the function `zoomToFit()` either, and our fork can become again more similar to theirs (we still have some other functionalities that forces us to keep the fork but of course, the more similar the better).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] zoomToFit flag is not exposed through AppState
- [ ] Try to replace zoomToFit calls with scrollToContent 
     - [ ] If the behavior is good, also remove the exposed API function zoomToFit,
     - [ ] If not, just keep the calls to zoomToFit. Just removing the flag from the AppState is good enough

## Estimation
Estimated to 3 because removing the flag is pretty trivial, but requires building and publishing another Excalidraw package. So probably this could be tackled at the same time next time we upgrade Excalidraw.

## Additional Context

Screen shots / UX designs / data that are relevant.

## Areas that will be affected

_To be added during the refinement_
t: Remove zoomToFit flag on Excalidraw AppState

## Background

The `CardsLayout` component in `src/core/ui/card/cardsLayout/CardsLayout.tsx` is currently marked as deprecated with the comment:
> @deprecated - doesn't add any functionality except items.map but adds complexity and reduces flexibility

Despite this deprecation notice, a recent change has added a special case for `globalSearch` that embeds a 'Load more' button directly within the component.

## Problem

As discussed in PR #7810 in [a discussion](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/pull/7810#discussion_r1998107511), there are concerns about this approach:

1. It adds a special case to a component that's already marked for deprecation
2. It further increases complexity in a component that should be simplified
3. It mixes layout and functionality concerns

## Discussion points

- @hero101 suggested either:
  - Passing a component that handles the 'fetch more' functionality
  - Adding a special card at the end of the items array

- @bobbykolev proposed keeping `CardsLayout` unmodified and using a structure like:
  

- @reactoholic noted that placing the 'Fetch more' button outside of `CardsLayout` breaks the UI in certain situations depending on viewport width

## Proposed solutions

1. Create a new, more flexible layout component that can accommodate the 'Fetch more' functionality without special cases
2. Extend the existing `CardsLayout` to accept a footer component that would handle the 'Fetch more' functionality
3. Investigate ways to properly position the 'Fetch more' button outside of `CardsLayout` without breaking the UI

## Action items

- [ ] Decide on the preferred approach
- [ ] Implement the refactoring
- [ ] Update any components currently using the special `globalSearch` case
- [ ] Consider next steps for the deprecated `CardsLayout` component

Refs: #7810
t: Refactor CardsLayout component to better handle 'Fetch more' functionality

## Description

As an Alkemio user I want consistent urls.

## Context
During the routing refactors we have come to a conclusion that the path of the url should be the entity.
We have the service urlResolver to return the ids of the entities whenever we want.

Following this url for entity agreement we have urls like:
`/user/admin` for users,
`/innovation-packs/ip1` for innovation packs
`/space1/challenges/subspace11` for a subspace
`/space1` for a space

But the settings of some entities, are after the `/settings` path,
So in the case of spaces we have things like:
`/space1/settings/community`
`/space1/challenges/subspace11/settings/about`

That was causing that the urlResolver was querying the server for every tab change in the settings area, going to the server to request the same entity (because it was the `settings/....` part of the same entity.
That was solved with line `UrlResolverProvider.tsx: 150`
`nextUrl = nextUrl.replace(/\/settings(?:\/[a-zA-Z0-9-]+)?\/?$/, '');`
That will remove anything after the `/settings/....` in the path, (when it is only one word => thanks to that `$`, remember it, it's useful later). 
And that makes all the urls like `..../settings/....` be the same to the urlResolver so only resolve them once.

But there's a problem with the innovation-packs. Urls of the innovation packs are:
`/innovation-packs/ip1` innovation pack profile
`/innovation-packs/ip1/template1` to view a template
`/innovation-packs/ip1/settings` to view settings of the IP
`/innovation-packs/ip1/settings/template1` to edit a template

So the url resolver is just removing `settings/template1` and the page is looking exactly as `/innovation-packs/ip1/settings`. The template dialog is not opening up and that's the bug reported in #8060

This is not happening on Spaces, because space's templates have these urls:
`/space1/settings/templates/:templateNameId`
The regex is not matching because of that `$` at the end, it's two words in the settings, and that is resolving to the templateId.


## Ways to solve this - Things to discuss:
- We can add the word `templates/` to the innovation-pack's template's urls too. I think this is the easiest and cleanest, so urls would become:
   - `/innovation-packs/ip1/templates/template1` to view a template
   - `/innovation-packs/ip1/templates/template1/settings` to edit a template or maybe it has to be `/innovation-packs/ip1/settings/templates/template1` to make it easier to the react router
   - Do we need to think about redirections for this?
- Maybe, settings tab selected should go in a query string, or we should agree that the routing is not path=entity anymore and have these kind of special cases in UrlResolverProvider
- Current approach to solve it in #8062: I have disabled that regex when the url starts with `/innovation-packs/`,


## Additional Context

Screen shots / UX designs / data that are relevant.

## Areas that will be affected

_To be added during the refinement_
t: Rework Innovation-Pack templates url

The me.service method `getCommunityApplicationsForUser` should be extended to include the applications to communities where the active user has admin memberships. 2. Opening similar to an invitation with accept & reject options. TBD #### Attention required The server's point 1 is tricky as obtaining all user's memberships is one of the heaviest requests. The logical approach is to: 1. Get all user memberships. 2. Get the applications for these. ___ Having these inside the existing `communityApplications` or as a separate field in the `me` request is also open for discussion. If they are in, how to group them on the client? Let's discuss other possible approaches.

b: **Describe the bug** A clear and concise description of what the bug is. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Go to acc env 2. Register new user with github - at the end of the flow user is registered but error is thrown **Expected behavior** Error is not thrown. **Additional context** Yes, it is possible for `createUserNewRegistrationMutation` (aliased as `createUserProfile`) to be executed more than once under certain conditions. Here's an analysis of the `useEffect` hook responsible for calling `createUserProfile`: ```typescript useEffect(() => { if (isAuthenticated && !loadingMe && !user && !loadingCreateUser && !error && !userProviderError) { createUserProfile(); } }, [user, loadingMe, createUserProfile, isAuthenticated, loadingCreateUser, error, userProviderError]); ``` The `createUserProfile` function is called if all the following conditions are true: 1. `isAuthenticated` is true. 2. `loadingMe` (loading state for `useCurrentUserFullQuery`) is false. 3. `user` (derived from `useCurrentUserFullQuery`'s data) is null or undefined. 4. `loadingCreateUser` (loading state for `useCreateUserNewRegistrationMutation`) is false. 5. `error` (error state from `useCreateUserNewRegistrationMutation`) is null or undefined. 6. `userProviderError` (error state from `useCurrentUserFullQuery`) is null or undefined. Consider this sequence of events: 1. The component mounts, `isAuthenticated` becomes true, and the initial `useCurrentUserFullQuery` completes. `loadingMe` becomes false. If no user exists, `user` is null. Assume no errors, so `error` and `userProviderError` are null. `loadingCreateUser` is initially false. 2. All conditions for the `if` statement inside `useEffect` are met. `createUserProfile()` is called for the first time. 3. When `createUserProfile()` is called, `loadingCreateUser` becomes true. The `useEffect` may re-run, but the `!loadingCreateUser` condition will be false, preventing an immediate second call. 4. The `createUserNewRegistrationMutation` executes. It is configured with `awaitRefetchQueries: true` and `refetchQueries: [refetchCurrentUserFullQuery()]`. This means the mutation will wait for `useCurrentUserFullQuery` to refetch before the mutation hook considers its execution complete (e.g., before `loadingCreateUser` becomes false and `error` is finalized). 5. During the refetch of `useCurrentUserFullQuery`, `loadingMe` will be true. If the `useEffect` re-runs, the `!loadingMe` condition will be false, preventing a call to `createUserProfile`. 6. The refetch completes, and `loadingMe` becomes false. 7. The `createUserNewRegistrationMutation` completes: * `loadingCreateUser` becomes false. * The `error` state of this mutation is set if the GraphQL mutation itself returned an error. Now, the `useEffect` dependencies (`loadingCreateUser`, `loadingMe`, `user`, `error`, `userProviderError`) have settled after the first attempt. The conditions are re-evaluated: If, after this entire process (first mutation call + refetch): * `isAuthenticated` is still true. * `loadingMe` is false (the refetch finished). * `loadingCreateUser` is false (the mutation finished). * `error` (from `createUserNewRegistrationMutation`) is still null (meaning the mutation GraphQL call itself was successful, it didn't return an error). * `userProviderError` (from `useCurrentUserFullQuery`) is still null (meaning the refetch query was successful, it didn't return an error). * **And critically, `user` is *still* null or undefined** (meaning the user creation attempt and subsequent refetch did not result in the `user` object being populated). Then, all conditions for the `if` statement would be met again, and `createUserProfile()` would be called a second time. This scenario could occur if: * The backend mutation succeeds from a technical perspective (no GraphQL error returned by the mutation itself) but fails to actually create a user record in a way that the subsequent `useCurrentUserFullQuery` refetch can pick it up. * There are eventual consistency issues on the backend where the newly created user is not immediately available for the refetch, despite `awaitRefetchQueries`. In essence, the logic is designed to retry creating the user profile if it's not detected after an attempt and no explicit errors were caught during the attempt. If the underlying reason for the user not being detected persists without flagging an error, repeated calls are possible. In a horizontally scaled application with a MySQL cluster that uses asynchronous replication (or even synchronous replication with a slight delay), the following can happen: 1. **Write Operation:** The `createUserNewRegistrationMutation` is handled by one application instance, which writes the new user data to a specific node in the MySQL cluster (let's call it Node A). 2. **Read Operation (Refetch):** Immediately after, the `refetchCurrentUserFullQuery` is triggered. Due to load balancing, this query might be handled by a *different* application instance, which in turn might read from a *different* node in the MySQL cluster (Node B). 3. **Replication Lag:** If the replication of the new user data from Node A to Node B has not completed by the time the refetch query hits Node B, Node B will not find the newly created user. 4. **Frontend State:** The `useCurrentUserFullQuery` will return data indicating the user still doesn't exist (`user` remains `null`). 5. **useEffect Trigger:** The conditions in your `useEffect` hook ( `!user`, `!loadingMe`, `!loadingCreateUser`, no errors) would then be met again, leading to another call to `createUserProfile()`. This is a common challenge in distributed systems with eventual consistency. The time it takes for data to propagate across all nodes (replication lag) can cause read-after-write inconsistencies, where a read operation doesn't see the effects of a very recent write. So, your backend architecture, specifically the asynchronous nature of replication in the MySQL cluster, could indeed be a contributing factor to the `createUserNewRegistrationMutation` being executed multiple times.

## Description
### Report Wave Plugin (log in page):
Using the WAVE plugin: https://wave.webaim.org/extension/
**Contrast Errors:**
In the following cases the colour is not a strong enough contract with the background. Adequate contrast of text is necessary for all users, especially users with low vision.

- [ ] Text: "Welcome to Alkemio"
- [ ] Text: "no account?" 
- [ ] Button: Sign Up / Log in 
- [ ] Button: Forgot Password 
- [ ] Button: Sign In

Updated Design: https://www.figma.com/design/pANR1cRI2D5WIF5cpkOwHu/Log-in---Sign-up-flow?node-id=211-119

**Empty button Errors** 
A button is empty or has no value text. When navigating to a button, descriptive text must be presented to screen reader users to indicate the function of the button.

- [ ] Connect with github
- [ ] Connect with Linekdin
- [ ] Connect with Microsoft

**Empty Link**

## Description

As a user I want a performant application.
As a developer, I want to use a supported framework to ensure maintainability and compatibility with the latest React versions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replace usage of Formik with built in React form management

## Additional Context

Why?
Formik is no longer actively maintained, with sporadic minor updates and significant periods of stagnation on core issues and pull requests. Many developers report crucial bugs and open PRs sitting unresolved, while the main maintainer is not actively developing new features or improvements.

What?
React Hook Form or React 19 native forms

[React 19 changes](https://alkem.io/building-alkemio-org/challenges/technicaldesigns-9853)
- `useActionState`: Handles server-side and async form submission, managing loading, pending, and error states automatically
    -  Yup is still useful for type-checking, chaining validation rules, dynamic/conditional logic, and providing custom error messages
    -  Any validation errors must be caught and returned from the action for useActionState to surface them in component state for error display*
- `useFormStatus`: Offers real-time access to whether a form is pending/submitting, useful for disabling buttons or showing loaders
- `useOptimistic`: Enables optimistic UI updates during async form actions, showing instant feedback before the server responds
- Functions as form `action`: Pass async functions to the form's `action` or button's `formAction` prop, enabling auto state, error, and reset management.

*Error management?
You will need to capture and return errors from Yup within your `action` function, then surface those in the state provided by `useActionState`, which your component can use to display messages.
The schema's validate or validateSync method should be called in the form action, possibly.

P.S. If you prefer fully automatic schema-driven validation, libraries like React Hook Form can integrate more deeply with Yup, but React 19's official APIs are more manual by design.
t: Switch to React forms (replace Formik)

### **Key Factors:**
1. **iOS 15.8.4 Release Date**:
   - Released in **July 2023** as a security update for older devices (iPhone 6s, iPhone 7, iPhone SE 1st gen, and some iPad models).
   - These devices **cannot** upgrade to iOS 16 or later due to hardware limitations.

2. **Device Compatibility**:
   - Only affects **iPhone 6s, 6s Plus, 7, 7 Plus, and SE (1st gen)**.
   - Apple stopped reporting iOS 15 adoption rates after iOS 16's release, but **iOS 15 was on ~20% of devices globally in late 2022** (Mixpanel, StatCounter).
   - By mid-2024, this percentage has likely dropped significantly as users upgrade devices.

3. **Western Europe iPhone User Base**:
   - ~**200–250 million iPhones** in Western Europe (estimates from Counterpoint, IDC).
   - **Older devices (iPhone 6s–7 series)** likely make up **<10%** of active iPhones (~20–25 million).
   - Not all of these are on iOS 15.8.4—some may be on **iOS 15.8.2 or earlier** (if never updated).

4. **Adoption Estimates**:
   - Assuming **5–15% of older iPhones** in Western Europe are still on iOS 15.8.4 (due to automatic security updates or manual updates).
   - This suggests **~1–3 million users** (very rough estimate).

### **Data Sources & Trends:**
- **Apple’s Security Updates**: iOS 15.8.4 was pushed to older devices for critical fixes, so many may have updated automatically.
- **Device Lifespan**: The iPhone 6s (2015) and 7 (2016) are **8–9 years old**; most users in Western Europe have likely upgraded.
- **Third-Party Data**:
  - **StatCounter (2024)** shows iOS 15 at **~5% globally**, but this includes newer devices stuck on iOS 15 (e.g., due to jailbreaking).
  - **Western Europe tends to have higher upgrade rates** than the global average.

### **Conclusion:**
A reasonable **estimate** for Western Europe is:
- **~1–3 million people** still using iOS 15.8.4 (mostly on iPhone 6s/7/SE 1st gen).
- The number is **shrinking rapidly** as users upgrade to newer iPhones or stop using old devices.

For precise data, you’d need **Apple’s internal analytics** or a **mobile analytics firm** (e.g., Mixpanel, App Annie), which aren’t publicly available. Would you like help finding regional survey data?

## Description

Higher SEO scores.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Should ‹testable condition that should be satisfied›
- [ ] …

## Additional Context
Here’s a **minimal SEO checklist for SPAs** (Single Page Applications):
---
## ✅ Minimal SPA SEO Checklist
### 1. **Robots.txt**
```txt
User-agent: *
Disallow:
```
(allows indexing everywhere)
---
### 2. **Meta Tags**
* Ensure each “page” (route) has:

  ```html
  <title>Unique Page Title | Brand</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Concise summary of this page">
  <meta name="robots" content="index, follow"> <!-- default -->
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://yourdomain.com/this-page" />
  ```
---
### 3. **Unique URLs for Routes**

* Every meaningful view in the SPA should have a unique URL (`/about`, `/products/123`, etc.).
* Avoid hash-based routing (`/#/about`) — use history mode (clean URLs).
---

### 4. **Pre-rendering or SSR**

* Crawlers may not execute heavy JavaScript well.
* Options:

  * **SSR (Server-Side Rendering)** with Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, etc.
  * **Pre-rendering** (e.g., [Prerender.io](https://prerender.io/), React Snap, Vite SSG) for static HTML snapshots.
---
### 5. **Sitemap**

* Generate a dynamic or static `sitemap.xml` and reference it in `robots.txt`:

  ```txt
  Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml
  ```
* Helps Google discover all routes.
---

### 6. **Open Graph & Twitter Cards**

* For social sharing:

  ```html
  <meta property="og:title" content="Page Title" />
  <meta property="og:description" content="Description here" />
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://yourdomain.com/preview.jpg" />
  <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
  ```
---

### 7. **Performance**

* Core Web Vitals affect SEO:

  * Optimize bundle size, lazy-load non-critical assets.
  * Use CDN for static assets.
  * Compress images (WebP/AVIF).
  * Use caching headers.
---
### 8. **Structured Data (Optional but Helpful)**

* JSON-LD for articles, products, FAQs, etc.
  Example (FAQ):

  ```html
  <script type="application/ld+json">
  {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "FAQPage",
    "mainEntity": [{
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What is your return policy?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "You can return items within 30 days."
      }
    }]
  }
  </script>
  ```
---

If you do just **robots.txt + meta tags + sitemap + pre-render/SSR**, you’ll already cover 90% of SEO basics for an SPA.


**pre-render/SSR - high effort**

_To be added during the refinement_

## Security Vulnerability: XSS in In-App Notifications

### Summary
The in-app notification system renders user-supplied content through  component which uses  plugin without proper sanitization, allowing potential XSS attacks through HTML injection in user messages.

### Root Cause
- **File**: `src/core/ui/markdown/WrapperMarkdown.tsx` (Line 76)
- **Issue**: `rehypeRaw` plugin is enabled without `rehype-sanitize`
- **Data Flow**: User content → `values.comment` → `WrapperMarkdown` → Raw HTML rendering

### Affected Components
The following notification views pass user-supplied content to the vulnerable markdown renderer:

1. **Organization Messages** (Critical):
   - `src/main/inAppNotifications/views/organization/InAppOrganizationAdminMessageView.tsx` (Line 15)
   - `src/main/inAppNotifications/views/organization/InAppOrganizationMessageSenderView.tsx` (Line 15)
   - Field: `payload.organizationMessage`

2. **User Messages** (Critical):
   - `src/main/inAppNotifications/views/user/InAppUserMessageView.tsx` (Line 14)
   - `src/main/inAppNotifications/views/user/InAppUserMessageSenderView.tsx` (Line 14)
   - Field: `payload.userMessage`

3. **Space Communications** (Critical):
   - `src/main/inAppNotifications/views/space/InAppSpaceLeadCommunicationMessageView.tsx` (Line 15)
   - Field: `payload.spaceCommunicationMessage`

4. **Forum Comments** (Critical):
   - `src/main/inAppNotifications/views/platform/InAppPlatformForumDiscussionCommentView.tsx` (Line 16)
   - Field: `payload.comment`

### Vulnerability Details
- **Attack Vector**: Malicious HTML/JavaScript injection in user messages
- **Execution Context**: Client-side in notification popup/dialog
- **Impact**: Session hijacking, credential theft, malicious actions on behalf of users

### Comparison with Existing Protection
The codebase already has proper sanitization in `src/core/ui/markdown/html/UnifiedConverter.ts` (Line 113) which uses `rehype-sanitize` with a secure schema. The same protection should be applied to `WrapperMarkdown`.

### Recommended Fix
Apply one of these solutions:

**Option A: Add sanitization (Recommended)**


**Option B: Disable raw HTML for notifications**
Add a `disableRawHtml` prop to `WrapperMarkdown` and set it to `true` when rendering user-supplied notification content.

### Reference
- **PR**: https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/pull/8696
- **Comment**: https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/pull/8696#discussion_r2339160076
- **Reported by**: @bobbykolev
- **Analysis by**: @coderabbitai

### Priority
**🚨 HIGH PRIORITY** - This is a client-side XSS vulnerability affecting user data in production.
t: XSS Vulnerability: In-App Notifications Render User Content Without Sanitization

**Feature Branch**: `feat/001-pexel-banner-integration`

**Input**: User description: "I want to have an integration for Pexel on Alkemio, where you can update banners of spaces, subspaces with the Pexel API. Preferably, you hover over the banner image of your (sub)space, then a button pops up to select an image, and then when you click you get a dialog where you can either upload your own image or search the Pexel repository from that dialog. credentials of the photographer can be captured in the Alt text. We don't want to send data about how many times a user has opened or downloaded an image to Pexel."

## User Scenarios & Testing _(mandatory)_

### User Story 1 - Update Banner via Pexels (Priority: P1)

As a Space or Subspace Admin, I want to search and select an image from Pexels to set as my space banner, so that I can easily find high-quality images without leaving the platform.

**Why this priority**: This is the core value proposition of the feature, enabling easy access to professional stock photos.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by navigating to a space, opening the banner dialog, searching Pexels, selecting an image, and verifying the banner updates.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am a Space Admin on my space page, **When** I hover over the banner and click "Change Banner", **Then** a dialog opens with a "Search Pexels" option.
2. **Given** the Pexels search tab is open, **When** I enter a keyword and search, **Then** a grid of relevant images from Pexels is displayed.
3. **Given** search results are displayed, **When** I select an image, **Then** I am presented with a cropping tool to adjust the image.
4. **Given** I have cropped the image, **When** I confirm, **Then** the space banner is updated with the cropped image.

---

### User Story 2 - Unified Banner Upload Dialog (Priority: P1)

As a Space or Subspace Admin, I want a unified dialog to either upload my own image or search Pexels, so that I have a consistent experience for updating banners.

**Why this priority**: Ensures the new feature integrates seamlessly with existing functionality (uploading custom images) without fragmenting the UI.

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by opening the dialog and verifying both "Upload" and "Pexels" options are available and functional.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the banner update dialog is open, **When** I choose "Upload Image", **Then** I can select a local file to upload.
2. **Given** I have uploaded a file, **When** I save, **Then** the space banner is updated with the uploaded image.

---

### User Story 3 - Automatic Photographer Attribution (Priority: P2)

As a Space Admin, I want the photographer's credentials to be automatically added to the image alt text when I choose a Pexels image, so that I give proper credit without manual effort.

**Why this priority**: Ensures compliance with attribution norms (even if not strictly enforced by API for all cases, it's good practice) and improves accessibility.

**Independent Test**: Select a Pexels image and inspect the resulting banner's alt text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I have selected a Pexels image, **When** the banner is updated, **Then** the alt text of the banner image contains the photographer's name/credits.

---

### User Story 4 - Visual Selection during Creation (Priority: P2)

As a User creating a Space or Subspace, I want to use the Pexels integration to select my banner or avatar immediately, so that my space looks professional from the start.

**Why this priority**: Improves the "first run" experience and adoption of the feature.

**Independent Test**: Run the Space and Subspace creation wizards and verify the visual selection steps use the new dialog.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am in the Space Creation wizard, **When** I reach the Banner selection step, **Then** the unified Upload/Pexels dialog is presented.
2. **Given** I am in the Subspace Creation wizard, **When** I reach the Avatar selection step, **Then** the unified Upload/Pexels dialog is presented.

---

### User Story 5 - Reuse Existing Visuals (Priority: P2)

As a Space Admin, I want to easily reuse my Page Banner or Avatar for the Card Banner, so that I can maintain visual consistency without re-uploading or re-searching.

**Why this priority**: Reduces friction and encourages consistent branding.

**Independent Test**: Open the Card Banner update dialog on a Space and a Subspace and verify the third option exists and works.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am updating a Space Card Banner, **When** I open the dialog, **Then** I see a third option "Use Page Banner".
2. **Given** I select "Use Page Banner", **Then** the Card Banner is updated to match the current Page Banner (triggering cropping if needed).
3. **Given** I am updating a Subspace Card Banner, **When** I open the dialog, **Then** I see a third option "Use Avatar".
4. **Given** I select "Use Avatar", **Then** the Card Banner is updated to match the current Avatar (triggering cropping if needed).

---

### Edge Cases

- What happens when the Pexels API is down or unreachable? (Should show an error message and allow fallback to upload).
- How does the system handle Pexels images that are deleted or become unavailable later? (We store the URL; if it breaks, the banner breaks. Should we cache/proxy? Assuming direct URL for now as per "integration" norm, but "don't send data" might imply proxying. *Assumption: We store the URL provided by Pexels.*)
- What happens if the search returns no results? (Display "No results found" message).

## Clarifications

### Session 2025-12-11

- Q: How should images be served to ensure privacy and persistence? → A: **Download & Host**. The system must download the image to Alkemio's storage and serve it from there, rather than hotlinking directly from Pexels.
- Q: How should the frontend access the Pexels API? → A: **Backend Proxy**. The frontend must query the Alkemio Backend (which holds the API key), which then proxies the request to Pexels. Direct browser-to-Pexels calls are prohibited.

## Requirements _(mandatory)_

Document how this feature satisfies the Constitution:

- **Domain Context**: `src/domain/space` (and potentially `subspace` if distinct, usually shared). The banner update logic resides here. Also affects `src/domain/space/components/CreateSpace` and `src/domain/space/components/CreateSubspace`.
- **UI Shell**: `src/main` shells rendering the Space layout will need to integrate the new `BannerUpdateDialog`.
- **GraphQL**:
  - New Query: `searchStockImages` (or similar) to proxy search requests.
  - Update Mutation: `updateSpace` or a new mutation must handle the "ingest from Pexels" logic (downloading and saving the image).
- **React 19**: Use `useTransition` for the search and update actions to keep UI responsive.
- **State**: Pexels search state (query, results, loading) should be local to the dialog or a transient hook, not global state.

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: System MUST provide a visual indicator (e.g., button) on the space banner area to initiate an update, visible only to users with permission.
- **FR-002**: System MUST present a modal dialog with two primary modes: "Upload" and "Pexels Search".
- **FR-003**: System MUST integrate with the Pexels API **via an Alkemio Backend proxy** to search for photos based on user input. Direct calls from the browser to Pexels are forbidden.
- **FR-004**: System MUST display Pexels search results in a responsive grid layout.
- **FR-005**: System MUST allow pagination or "load more" for Pexels search results.
- **FR-006**: System MUST automatically extract photographer credits from the Pexels API response and populate the banner's Alt Text field.
- **FR-007**: System MUST NOT make calls to Pexels "trigger download" endpoints or send user tracking data to Pexels, ensuring privacy.
- **FR-008**: System MUST allow the user to preview the selected Pexels image before saving.
- **FR-009**: System MUST persist the selected image by **triggering a backend download/ingestion process**, ensuring the image is served from Alkemio storage (not hotlinked).
- **FR-010**: System MUST allow the user to crop the selected Pexels image using the platform's cropping tool before saving.
- **FR-011**: System MUST integrate the unified Pexels/Upload dialog into the Space and Subspace creation wizards for Banner and Avatar selection respectively.
- **FR-012**: System MUST provide a "Use Page Banner" option when updating a Space Card Banner, which copies the source image of the Page Banner.
- **FR-013**: System MUST provide a "Use Avatar" option when updating a Subspace Card Banner, which copies the source image of the Avatar.

### Key Entities _(include if feature involves data)_

- **Space**: The domain entity being modified. Attributes: `bannerUrl`, `bannerAltText`.
- **PexelsImage**: Transient entity representing a search result. Attributes: `id`, `url`, `photographer`, `photographer_url`.

## Success Criteria _(mandatory)_

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Space Admins can successfully update a banner using Pexels in under 60 seconds.
- **SC-002**: 100% of banners updated via Pexels have photographer attribution in the alt text.
- **SC-003**: Zero analytics/tracking requests are sent to Pexels API endpoints (verified via network inspection).
- **SC-004**: Pexels search results load within 2 seconds (dependent on Pexels API latency).

## Assumptions

- Pexels API key will be configured in the backend/environment variables.
- The current `Space` entity already supports `bannerUrl` and `bannerAltText` (or similar fields).
- **Backend Dependency**: The Alkemio Backend will expose a GraphQL API for searching Pexels and handling the image download/ingestion. The frontend will not communicate with Pexels directly.
- **Cropping Tool**: A new cropping tool is being developed and will be available for use with this feature.
t: Pexels integration
