## Description

As a user I want to be sure time is correctly handled

- Sometimes the server defines a date as a timestamp, in most other places it's a string converted to js Date object.
- In most cases dates on the client are handled as strings
- MariaDB does not support dates in ISO 8601 format - [MariaDB no longer accepts ISO 8601 with trailing Z](https://jira.mariadb.org/browse/MDEV-13511) so information about the timezone is lost and the server interprets it as a date in its local zone.
- There is a problem with dates in the subscription a [manual creation of the date](https://github.com/alkem-io/server/blob/develop/src/domain/collaboration/callout/callout.resolver.subscriptions.ts#L62) is needed in order for the subscription to work properly - if not addressed an error is thrown in the terms of "a null is returned for "date field" where "date field" is not nullable"

## Description

As a user I want to be able to set the language I want to receive notifications in
As a user signing up, I expect that if I have chosen Dutch as my display language  that I receive identity emails in that language

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Ensure that kratos sign up flow can take the language as part of the sign up request
- [ ] User entity extended with a field for selecting a language for communications: communicationsLanguage
- [ ] Client updated to allow the user to select the language to use
- [ ] Client to pick up the selected display language from the user as part of the sign up process
- [ ] user profile update mutation to detect if selected language has changed, and if so send a call to Kratos to set this in the user profile in Kratos

## Additional Context
- Kratos supports multiple languages in its email templates - https://www.ory.sh/docs/kratos/emails-sms/custom-email-templates
- In order to pick up the language, `lang` needs to be set in the public metadata of the user. Then it is picked up in the template
- If there is an error with `lang` or a language can't be found, the fallback is to default settings

In order to add support for multiple languages, we need the following:
- Ability on the client to set the user language in Kratos. To access the public metadata, an access to the admin kratos endpoint is required, so we might need to proxy the call via our GraphQL API, as admin endpoint is not exposed publicly.
- Update of the email templates in the application with addition of the required translations.
Screen shots / UX designs / data that are relevant.
t: Prototyping end - end usage of language

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The current implementation of the guidance engine can only handle one chatbot session per user. If a user would have multiple alkemio tabs open and interact with the chatbot in more than one session, the guidance engine would mix the results from both sessions.

Furthermore, there is no timeout on an ongoing chatbot session, This means that if a user user the chatbot and return after some time (this can be days), the chatbot will act as if there is an onging conversation, whilst the user most probably assumes this is a 'fresh' session.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
As a user I want to be able to use the chatbot from different browser tabs and I want my chatbot sessions reset when i open the chatbot window.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep as is and set a time based timeout on the chatbot session.

**Additional context**
The easkiest solution might be to use a session-id instead of the user id for calls to the guidance engine and to send a reset when the session windows is opened.
t: Allow multiple chat sessions for same user in different tabs for guidance engine

```gql
query recentForumMessages($limit: Float = 5) {
  platform {
    id
    communication {
      id
      discussionCategories
      authorization {
        id
        myPrivileges
        anonymousReadAccess
        __typename
      }
      discussions(queryData: {orderBy: DISCUSSIONS_CREATEDATE_DESC, limit: $limit}) {
        ...DiscussionCard
        __typename
      }
      __typename
    }
    __typename
  }
}

fragment DiscussionCard on Discussion {
  id
  profile {
    id
    url
    displayName
    description
    tagline
    visual(type: AVATAR) {
      ...VisualFull
      __typename
    }
    __typename
  }
  category
  timestamp
  comments {
    id
    messagesCount
    authorization {
      myPrivileges
      __typename
    }
    __typename
  }
  createdBy
  authorization {
    id
    myPrivileges
    anonymousReadAccess
    __typename
  }
  __typename
}

fragment VisualFull on Visual {
  id
  uri
  name
  allowedTypes
  aspectRatio
  maxHeight
  maxWidth
  minHeight
  minWidth
  alternativeText
  __typename
}
```
with params
```json
{
  "limit": 5
}
```
4. You get error
`"User (admin@alkem.io) does not have credentials that grant 'read' access to Communication.discussions"`

**Expected behavior**
`RecentForumMessages` does not return error

b: ## Description As a Space admin, I want to invite an organization to join my Space, and as an org admin I want to be able to accept or decline that invitation on behalf of my organization. ## Acceptance criteria **Space community settings tab** - [ ] In the member organizations section, add button to invite organizations (also keep the 'add organization button for now: for `platform support`, `beta tester`, and `global admin` roles) - [ ] Invite flow is similar to the invite user's dialog. Includes a message and the role for the selected organizations: Member or Lead. (Member is always selected and disabled, because there's no way to be Lead without being Member). - [ ] Invitation should be sent to all organization admins (an org can have multiple admins - not just one) - [ ] If there are no organization admins at all, invitation should be sent to support@alkem.io, preferably with an indication - [ ] Revoke a pending org invitation, following the same behavior as revoking a pending user invitation **Organization profile settings** - [ ] Add an "Invitations" tab on the org profile listing pending Space invitations with Accept/Decline - [ ] Show message if any **Other** - [ ] Invite entry point is settings-only — no equivalent button on the community view - [ ] ~~Don't say members, but associates~~ — **superseded by ruling R15**: Space-side wording stays "Member organisations" / "Member" / "Lead"; "associate" is the organization-side word and appears nowhere in Space-side copy. (The organization settings tab has since been renamed *Community* → *Associates*.) - [ ] Adding a search bar for organizations in a Space community tab. Follow search for space members **Notifications** - [ ] Organization admins receive a notification that the organization is invited to join a Space (in app, push, email - all on) - [ ] Space admins receive a notification that the organization has accepted or rejected their invitation (in app, push, email - all on) - [ ] Accepting sends a "welcome" notification to the organization's admins, so the ones who did not accept know that no action is needed - [ ] Accepting must not trigger a double notification — the "joined" notification should only fire when there was no invitation or application step - [ ] Add the 2 notifications above to the user notification settings ## Additional Context Prototype (1-1 UI tested) for the org-side accept/decline UI: https://alkemio-prototype.vercel.app/organization/cityscale/settings/invitations ## Areas that will be affected - `alkem-io/server` — invite guards, organization opt-out setting, notification events + recipients, ancestor-Space enumeration — [server#6467](https://github.com/alkem-io/server/pull/6467) - `alkem-io/client-web` — unified invite dialog, Member Organisations list + revoke, organization *Invitations* tab, notification settings row, i18n ×6 — [client-web#10272](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/pull/10272) - `alkem-io/notifications` — email delivery: handlers and templates — [notifications#594](https://github.com/alkem-io/notifications/pull/594) - `alkem-io/test-suites` — live it-specs + Playwright acceptance walks — [test-suites#632](https://github.com/alkem-io/test-suites/pull/632) - The `notifications` json of every user is affected, so a verification that nothing is broken/changed from the user notification settings and that only the new values are added is required Cross-repo spec: `agents-hq/specs/061-organization-space-invitations` (branch `server-4100`). Related: [notifications#356](https://github.com/alkem-io/notifications/issues/356), epic [alkemio#1433](https://github.com/alkem-io/alkemio/issues/1433); fixes [server#4602](https://github.com/alkem-io/server/issues/4602). ## Delivered beyond these acceptance criteria — please confirm Not requested in this issue; recorded here so the decisions are visible rather than buried in the spec. 1. **Organization opt-out setting.** Organizations get a setting "Allow Spaces to invite this organisation" (default on); inviting an opted-out organization returns the outcome "organisation is not accepting invitations" and creates nothing. *(operator ruling R2)* 2. **Admins only — owners are not notified.** The notifications above go to organization **admins**, exactly as this issue and [notifications#356](https://github.com/alkem-io/notifications/issues/356) specify. Consequence worth a decision: an **owner** who is not also an admin *can* accept the invitation on the organization's behalf (they hold the same underlying credential), but receives no notification that there is anything to accept — and an organization with owners but no admins is treated as having none, so its invitation escalates to support@alkem.io. **Should owners be notified too?**
t: Inviting organizations to Space

**Describe the bug**
On the VC's membership page, the client checks for the "GRANT" privilege to determine if it is able to leave the community membership. 

As the GRANT privilege is only applied in memory on the server when the mutation is triggered (as request dependent) this means the client does not show the user that they can leave. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

As an Alkemio user I want accurate search results even during Elasticsearch ingestion process.

## Description
At the moment, during contents ingestion, there are moments where the search results are not complete.
This situation can be avoided with incremental updates to Elasticsearch indices, and that is also in mind, so that would make this issue useless. But this is a simple method that we (@hero101 and @ccanos) have discussed.



## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingestion is performed the same way it's done at the moment, but instead of deleting the indices at the beginning, and recreating them, we create new separate indices, and when the ingestion is finished we delete the original ones and rename the newly created ones.
- [ ] Failed ingestions don't leave orphan indices (or at least, orphan indexes are deleted at the beginning of the next attempt).

## Additional Context
Elasticsearch also support index aliases: https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/aliases.html
That could help, we can create the new index, and then point the alias to it, instead of deleting and renaming.

Screen shots / UX designs / data that are relevant.

## Areas that will be affected 
 Search
t: Ingest db contents into Elasticsearch into separate indices and then swap them when the ingestion is finished

## Description

As a user, I don't want to be constrained with character limits. I want to the be the one to choose how long my text will be. Current character limit of 8000 (client) is too little for some posts.

## Acceptance criteria

Does the limit have to be a power of 2? If not:
- [ ] Character limit for collaboration tool descriptions to be raised to 20k (client) and 64k (server)
- [ ] Character limit for post descriptions to be raised to 20k (client) and 64k (server)

## Additional Context

I asked ChatGPT..:
### **1. Purpose of the Platform**
- **Discussion Forums (e.g., Reddit)**:
  - **Ideal Limit for Comments**: 1,000–10,000 characters.
  - **Ideal Limit for Posts**: 10,000–20,000 characters.
  - **Reason**: Supports detailed discussions, with room for explanation without becoming overwhelming.

- **Content Platforms (e.g., Blogs, Medium)**:
  - **Ideal Limit for Posts**: No strict limit but can suggest up to 100,000 characters.
  - **Reason**: Designed for long-form content and storytelling.

---

### **2. Technical and Security Considerations**
- **Server Performance**: If the platform expects high traffic, smaller character limits (e.g., 1,000–5,000) are safer to reduce database load.
- **Network Bandwidth**: For mobile-first platforms, keeping limits low (e.g., <10,000) ensures smooth performance.

---

### **3. Audience and Engagement**
- **Short Attention Span**:
  - Lower character limits (<1,000) may be effective for platforms targeting younger audiences or casual use.
- **Depth of Engagement**:
  - Higher limits (5,000–10,000) are better for communities that value detailed discussions, such as niche forums or academic platforms.

---

### **4. Benchmarking Common Platforms**
- **Twitter (now X)**: 280 characters (microblogging standard).
- **Instagram Captions**: 2,200 characters (visual storytelling focus).
- **LinkedIn Posts**: 3,000 characters (professional context).
- **Reddit Comments**: 10,000 characters (longer discussions).
- **Facebook Posts**: 63,206 characters (rarely used in full).

---

### **Recommendations by Use Case**
1. **Casual, Quick Updates**:
   - Posts: 280–500 characters.
   - Comments: 100–200 characters.

2. **Engaging and Informative**:
   - Posts: 1,000–2,500 characters.
   - Comments: 250–500 characters.

3. **In-depth Discussions**:
   - Posts: 5,000–10,000 characters.
   - Comments: 1,000–5,000 characters.

> **This issue is now scoped to Slice A only.**
> Slice B (subtractive, breaking) moved to #6345 · migrating existing holders moved to #6344.

## What Slice A is

**Slice A adds the new role model without taking anything away.**

Every authorization rule this slice writes is a **union** — `{new owning role} ∪ legacy` — so a
capability reachable by `global-admin` today stays reachable by `global-admin` after it deploys.
Database changes only grow: `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`, idempotent role-row inserts, one table
column made nullable. The GraphQL surface is additive-only (58 additive changes, 0 breaking,
enforced by `schema:diff`).

**What Slice A gives you:** the 13 purpose-specific roles exist, are grantable and revocable
through a rule engine, carry an audit trail for every grant and revoke, and reach everything their
legacy counterparts reach.

**What Slice A deliberately does NOT do:** it does not reduce anyone's access, and therefore does
not by itself reduce standing privilege. `global-admin` still reaches every surface — that is what
makes the slice safe to deploy on its own, and it is also why the security benefit does not land
until #6345. A useful way to read it: Slice A builds the replacement, Slice B removes the original.

Two consequences worth stating plainly, because they surprise people:

- **The denial half of the test matrix cannot run yet.** All 134 executable matrix cells assert
  ALLOW; every DENY cell is gated behind `isStageB()`. While the legacy cascade still reaches every
  surface, a denial result would be meaningless. Slice A proves each role *can* do its own job; it
  cannot yet prove a role *cannot* do another's.
- **Nothing is migrated.** Existing holders keep their legacy roles and are unaffected. Moving them
  is #6344, and it happens around the Slice B release.

---

## Description

As a **platform / security owner**
I want the platform-wide (global) roles audited and redesigned so that **no single all-powerful role exists**
So that ordinary operational work can be delegated to tightly-scoped roles, the platform's blast radius is reduced, and every administrative action is attributable.

### Why

`Global Admin` today is god mode: unrestricted create/read/update/delete/grant across every entity tree, held by inheritance from a single root rule. A number of routine operational tasks — granting or revoking a user's or organization's roles, deleting a user, several admin-communication maintenance operations — cannot be delegated at all, so operators must be handed total control to do ordinary support work.

The audit surfaced five further problems:

1. **Unprincipled enforcement.** Some admin actions are gated on a broad "platform admin" capability that `Global Support` holds, while equivalent-severity actions are hard-locked to `Global Admin`. The "Support can / only Admin can" boundary is arbitrary.
2. **An inert role.** `Global Support Manager` is defined, assignable and seeded, yet gates no top-level admin action — an operational confusion and a misleading security surface.
3. **Overlapping purpose.** `Global Support` and `Global License Manager` both carry broad platform-admin power with no clean separation of responsibility.
4. **Silent-void roles.** Two roles are seeded with identifiers that do not match what the authorization checks expect — a user granted them may silently receive **no** access.
5. **Auth reset falls back to the broad role.** Several "reset authorization" actions still gate on the broad platform-admin capability instead of the dedicated, narrower authorization-reset capability that already exists.

**Scope:** global / platform-wide roles only. Per-space, subspace, organization and space-community roles are out of scope — the per-space model is relied upon but unchanged.

### Target role model

Global Admin is decomposed so that every sensitive family of administrative action is owned by **exactly one** role, granted explicitly rather than inherited from a blanket root grant. Two distinct sets of global roles result, with a deliberately one-way separation between them.

**1. Platform Administration roles** — high-risk; assigned **only** by Platform Roles Admin:

| Role | Owns |
|---|---|
| **Platform Roles Admin** | Assign/revoke the platform roles (sole authority) and the Feature roles |
| **Platform Content Full Access** | Full access and rights across all platform content; held by very few, only temporarily |
| **Platform Resource Admin** | Resource moves — space / innovation-hub / innovation-pack / virtual contributor to another account; promote, demote or move a space; move a callout to another space |
| **Platform Settings Admin** | Platform settings, integrations, notification config; defining and updating license plans and their entitlement mappings |
| **Platform Operations Admin** | Authorization reset and license-entitlement reset; the operational machinery — AI/search ingest and re-index, embeddings cleanup, body-of-knowledge refresh, avatar/whiteboard migration, notification prune, comms housekeeping, geolocation refresh. **No PII access** |
| **Platform Users Admin** | User-record lifecycle — login-email change, identity/account deletion and reset, PII read to support these — plus Feature-role assignment |
| **Platform Support** | Admin rights inside a space **only** where that space has enabled support-as-admin; the organization lifecycle (create/delete); the platform forum |
| **Platform License Manager** | License *usage* — assign/revoke plans on accounts and spaces; change space visibility |
| **Platform Spaces Reader** | Read across spaces; **service accounts only** |

**2. Feature roles** — low-risk, grant access to a capability and administer nothing; assigned by **Platform Users Admin or Platform Roles Admin**: **Feature Beta Tester**, **Feature Virtual Assistant**, **Feature Organization Creator**.

**The one-way rule:** Platform Users Admin can hand out Feature roles but can **never** assign a platform role. Granting a feature flag must never come with the ability to grant administrative power.

**Roles removed:** `Global Support Manager` (inert), `Global Community Reader` (redundant broad PII read), `VC Campaign` (retired).

## Acceptance criteria

**Audit**
- [ ] Complete, reviewable inventory of every global role — purpose, the concrete administrative actions it authorizes, and its health (active / inert / overlapping).
- [ ] Every administrative action that today requires god mode is explicitly identified, with either a justification or a "should be delegated" recommendation.
- [ ] Each structural finding (inert role, inconsistent enforcement, overlap, silent-void defect) recorded with its remediation.

**Operate without god mode**
- [ ] An operator holding **only Platform Operations Admin** can run an authorization reset and the operational/maintenance actions — and is denied user email change, identity deletion, Feature-role assignment and PII read.
- [ ] An operator holding **only Platform Users Admin** can change a user's login email, delete/reset an identity or account, and assign/revoke a Feature role — and is denied authorization reset.
- [ ] Neither can assign a platform role, administer content or settings, or act as admin inside a space.

**Separation of duties**
- [ ] No role can perform actions from more than one admin family; no role can reconstitute god mode.
- [ ] Each admin role assigned in isolation performs only its own family and is denied the others.
- [ ] Every sensitive administrative action maps to exactly one owning role; none is reachable purely by inheritance.
- [ ] The inheritance-root all-powerful grant and the platform-subtree CRUD cascade are both removed; the platform-admin catch-all capability is decomposed into per-family capabilities.

**No dead or ambiguous roles**
- [ ] Every remaining global role grants at least one defined, enforced capability — or is removed.
- [ ] Each role's documented purpose matches its enforced capabilities.
- [ ] An action a role is documented to allow is consistently permitted (or denied) from every surface that can trigger it; any intentional exception is documented.

**No silent-void roles**
- [ ] The stored form of every role matches the form authorization evaluates, verified by an automated check that prevents future drift.
- [ ] Granting a previously-affected role to a test user actually confers the intended access.

**Audit trail**
- [ ] Every global-role grant and revoke is written to a persistent, append-only audit record — acting operator, affected user/organization, role, action, timestamp — queryable after the fact. No grant or revoke occurs without one.
- [ ] High-risk actions beyond role assignment are recorded and attributable: all Platform Operations Admin actions, platform-settings and license-plan-definition changes, content deletions, resource moves, space-visibility changes, license assignments.

**Safety**
- [ ] The platform can never reach **zero Platform Roles Admins** — removing or downgrading the last one is prevented.
- [ ] A break-glass recovery path always exists despite no god-mode role existing.
- [ ] An operator cannot grant themselves or anyone else a role they are not authorized to grant; self-affecting grants are recorded, and whether Platform Roles Admin may assign admin roles to itself is an explicit documented decision.

**Migration**
- [ ] Existing holders are mapped onto the new roles **best-effort**. Dropping some assignments is acceptable provided **no holder is silently elevated** and dropped access is re-grantable afterward through the new roles. Lossless preservation is explicitly **not** required.
- [ ] Zero accounts hold an all-powerful role after migration (none exists); each operator holds only the role(s) their duties require.

**Delivery**
- [ ] The deliverable is the audit **and** the shipped redesign — new/renamed roles, re-gated actions, migrated holders. Acceptance is measured by operators actually performing each family of action holding only its owning role, not by a document.

## Problem
The current implementation in StorageBucketService allows saving documents before saving storage buckets, which can lead to implicit behavior based on TypeORM entity relationships.

## Impact
- If a storage bucket is not saved before its documents, the relationship between them may not be persisted correctly.
- This can result in orphaned documents or missing relationships in the database.
- The behavior depends on cascade settings and relationship types, making it less predictable.

## Context
- PR Discussion: https://github.com/alkem-io/server/pull/4763#discussion_r1878297104
- Related file: src/domain/storage/storage-bucket/storage.bucket.service.ts

## Proposed Solution
Ensure that storage buckets are always saved before their associated documents to maintain data integrity and explicit behavior.

## Tasks
1. Review and document all places where documents are saved in relation to storage buckets
2. Implement proper validation to ensure storage buckets exist before saving documents
3. Consider adding transaction support for atomic operations
4. Update tests to verify correct relationship persistence
t: Refactor StorageBucketService to handle document-bucket relationships safely

## Description

As a developer I want to be able to use the latest packages.

Part of **Phase 3** of Epic alkem-io/alkemio#1536. **Should be deferred until NestJS 12 ships native ESM support (~Q3 2026).**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Wait for NestJS 12 stable release with native ESM support
- [ ] Migrate tsconfig `module` from `commonjs` to ESM output
- [ ] Add `"type": "module"` to package.json
- [ ] Update `moduleResolution` to `node16` or `nodenext`
- [ ] Use full relative file paths for imports (e.g., `./index.js`)
- [ ] Use the `node:` protocol for Node.js built-in imports
- [ ] Replace `graphql-upload@13` with ESM-compatible alternative (`graphql-upload-ts` or `graphql-upload@17`)
- [ ] Wrap TypeORM entity relations with `Relation` type to avoid circular dependency issues
- [ ] Audit and update all ESM-only / CJS-only dependencies
- [ ] Update build scripts and Dockerfile `CMD` if needed
- [ ] All existing tests pass

## Additional Context

NestJS 12 (~Q3 2026) will make ESM the default module system. Key challenges:
- `graphql-upload` v14+ is ESM-only — current v13 is CJS
- TypeORM circular dependencies need `Relation` wrapper in ESM
- Some packages (chalk, node-fetch, ora, execa) have gone ESM-only in recent versions
- Node 24's `require(esm)` helps bridge the gap during transition

References:
- https://gist.github.com/sindresorhus/a39789f98801d908bbc7ff3ecc99d99c#how-can-i-make-my-typescript-project-output-esm
- [NestJS v12 PR](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/16391)

## Dependencies

- NestJS 12 stable release
- Phase 1 (Apollo 5 + NestJS 11) and Phase 2 (Node 24) should be completed first

## Description
NestJS has released version 11, which fixes security vulnerabilities, supports newer versions of Express and Fastify, developer QoL and optimizations, but also introduces some breaking changes and dropped support for older NodeJS versions.

Part of **Phase 1** of Epic alkem-io/alkemio#1536. Should be done together with Apollo 5 upgrade (#5541) as `@nestjs/apollo@13.x` bridges both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upgrade `@nestjs/*` core packages from 10.x → 11.x
- [ ] Handle Express v5 as new default — audit routes with `?`, `*`, `+` patterns
- [ ] Update `@nestjs/cache-manager` for latest cache-manager compatibility
- [ ] Verify middleware registration order changes (global modules now execute first)
- [ ] Verify file upload (multer) compatibility
- [ ] Upgrade `@nestjs/typeorm`, verify custom TypeORM fork compatibility
- [ ] Upgrade `@nestjs/cqrs`, `@nestjs/schedule`, `@nestjs/jwt`, `@nestjs/passport`, `@nestjs/axios`, `@nestjs/event-emitter`, `@nestjs/microservices`
- [ ] Update TypeScript if needed
- [ ] Investigate if any current packages or functionality are affected / not supported yet
- [ ] Create a list of actions and learnings along the way
- [ ] All existing tests pass

## Additional Context

NestJS 11 key changes:
- Express v5 is the default — route matching changed (`?`, `*`, `+` require named params)
- Middleware registration order: global modules execute first
- CacheModule updated for latest `cache-manager`
- Node.js >= 20 required (already satisfied)
- Does NOT require ESM (ESM planned for NestJS 12, ~Q3 2026)

## Resources
- [Announcing NestJS 11: What's New?](https://trilon.io/blog/announcing-nestjs-11-whats-new)
- [Migration guide 10 to 11](https://docs.nestjs.com/migration-guide)
- [NestJS Releases](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/releases)
t: [Spike] Research upgrading NestJS v10 to v11

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
During investigation of URL resolver errors ([Issue #8159](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/issues/8159#issuecomment-2871896847)), gaps were identified in how crawler bots navigate public spaces and documentation. Key issues include:

- 404 errors for private links in public spaces (e.g., callouts).
- Broken links in NL translation files and undocumented paths (e.g., /faq.en-US, /how-to/inviting.nl-NL).
- Lack of a structured way to guide search engines through public areas/spaces, impacting SEO.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Options that were raised:
- It would be nice to have a sitemap to guide search engines through the public common areas but also through public spaces. We could put a static sitemap.xml, but that would only cover the public areas. To generate a sitemap.xml that lists public spaces, it needs to be generated by the server, probably cached, and this feature requires some thinking.
- Another option is to generate a page in the client, not very visible to the human users, something that is just a list of the public areas and public spaces. Crawlers that can execute Javascript (I guess many of them nowadays) will navigate through it. All of this I would approach it from a SEO point of view and there are many other things that should be done together with this

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
-

**Additional context**
- This issue is for research/proposal only; implementation will follow in a separate issue.
Reference:[ Issue #8159 (URL resolver errors).](https://github.com/alkem-io/client-web/issues/8159#issuecomment-2871896847)
- SEO improvements should be scoped alongside this effort.
t: Research and Propose Solution for Dynamic Sitemap/SEO Crawler Guidance

b: ## Description As a lead, I sometimes use collections in a post not for external contributions, but instead, for organizing and sharing a set of information myself. Think of a set of project examples, brainstorm methods, interesting links, whiteboards that can be used for brainstorming, etc. It's a real pity that I currently cannot include them in my template. The solution: Allow adding contributions when creating/editing the template inside the library (space or global) ## Acceptance criteria Add option to add collection items in the template when this is created or edited through the library, same as we currently do with collection of links in normal callouts: - [ ] In the callout template create/edit form, change the settings button to be a settings icon button (label + tooltip "Collection Settings") - [ ] Add an add icon button (label + tooltip "Add item to this Collection") - [ ] Clicking on this icon opens the dialog to add a collection item, same as we use for normal contributions outside of a template - [ ] If there are items in the collection, show them below (see design) - [ ] Without a date - [ ] Author: use post creator - [ ] Note that the footer of the dialog should remain fixed (create button always visible) - [ ] When user clicks on contributions in template, it opens and user can edit or remove contribution ## Additional Context Design: https://www.figma.com/design/8iMJUUFrUGPDd0LDAHK8Vn/Callout-templates--Adding-items-to-a-collection?node-id=30-2&t=2PAwLNr8KDAuc9xD-1 ## Thoughts - Callout Templates - Callout Template dialog: - [ ] Change callout template model to support initial contributions - [ ] Add the dialog to create and edit contributions (post, whiteboard, memo...) - [ ] Ability to delete contributions before Creating the template (in memory), or when editing the template (saving existing template) - [ ] Change UI - [ ] Handle visuals inside the posts (temporary storage when creating the callout, contribution storage bucket when editing), - [ ] Handle images inside whiteboards. - Server side - create template: - [ ] Handle contributions in callout templates - create/delete contributions, when added/removed during editing, edit existing contributions. Do not notify any community. - [ ] Use template: - [ ] Add the contributions when the callout template has them. Author is the creator of the callout, date is now When creating callout templates and using callout templates, al the data is in the browser, so for the server it's just a normal "Create callout" with a copy of all the data retrieved from the template, and "Create callout template" with the data copied from the template. For spaces things are different, we have functions to "Create a space following this space template id" and the server does all the work without the data passing through the browser. Same for creating a Space template, we have server side code to create a template from a specific space. - [ ] Space Templates: - shouldn't be a lot of work but, do we want this now? - [ ] Make `input.creator.service` code aware of contributions and handle them - not sure yet but I think the same code executes when creating a template from a space and when creating a space from a template. - [ ] Add a flag to be able to include contributions in the template or not (And include only the contributions created by the user that is creating the template?) **OUT OF SCOPE** Create a template from an existing callout - [ ] Save callout as template dialog, is the same dialog and components. It will NOT contain contributions but contributions can be added manually ??? or it will contain contributions created by myself? - If we allow existing whiteboard contributions to be included in the template we need to copy the images inside the wbs to the storageBucket of the template. (I am not sure how is this handled at the moment for wbs in the framing) ## Areas that will be affected _To be added during the refinement_
t: Allow adding of contributions to a template

## Context
Feature 002 (PR #5471) introduced automated GraphQL schema diffing, lifecycle enforcement, and deprecation governance. Currently, re-adding an enum value that was previously deprecated & removed is treated as a simple ADDITIVE change.

## Problem
If an enum value was deprecated with a published removal schedule and removed after its `REMOVE_AFTER` date, later re-introducing the exact same value may:
- Reintroduce a concept that downstream clients adapted away from
- Create ambiguity in historical deprecation metrics
- Hide potential contract churn

The current classification (ADDITIVE) lacks nuance to distinguish "fresh new value" vs "reinstated value." This can reduce governance insight and potentially bypass product review expectations.

## Proposal
Introduce a new informational classification, e.g. `ENUM_VALUE_REINSTATED` (non-breaking, but highlighted), when ALL are true:
1. The enum value appears in the new schema but not in the previous snapshot.
2. Git history (or a persisted deprecation registry enrichment) shows the same value previously existed and was removed.
3. The prior removal flowed through a valid deprecation process (had a valid `REMOVE_AFTER` and was removed after that date) OR was removed before schedule (flag as a BREAKING chain, already covered today).

### Detection Strategy
- Extend diff engine to (optionally) load a lightweight historical ledger derived from prior `deprecations.json` entries or git blame scanning of `schema.graphql`.
- When encountering an ADDITIVE enum value, check ledger for prior existence.
- Annotate change entry with `previouslyRemovedAt` timestamp and original deprecation metadata if found.

### Classification Semantics
- `ENUM_VALUE_REINSTATED` → Gate: Pass (non-breaking) but surfaced in PR comment under a distinct section.
- Retains existing BREAKING logic if the original removal violated lifecycle rules.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a previously unused enum value → remains ADDITIVE.
- Re-adding an historically removed enum value → yields `ENUM_VALUE_REINSTATED` entry with metadata `{ priorRemoveAfter, priorDeprecatedAt, previouslyRemovedAt }`.
- JSON Schema updated to allow the new classification.
- Tests: (a) reinstatement detection, (b) additive fresh value control, (c) reinstatement after governance-compliant removal, (d) reinstatement after premature removal (should still flag historical chain integrity — document expected behavior).
- Documentation: Update `classification` section & governance README; add FAQ entry ("Why is this value marked reinstated?").

## Out of Scope
- Automatic blocking or warnings beyond surfacing classification.

## Follow-Up (Optional)
- Metric: count reinstatements per quarter.

Labels: enhancement, schema-contract, governance
t: Schema Contract: Nuanced Classification for Re-adding Previously Deprecated Enum Values

Feature 002 (PR #5471) introduced governance overrides for BREAKING schema changes using CODEOWNERS + `BREAKING-APPROVED` phrase detection. Current implementation matches individual usernames from reviews and CODEOWNERS entries but does not expand team slugs (e.g. `@alkem-io/platform-core`).

## Problem
Organizations commonly rely on GitHub team reviews rather than individual reviewers for domain ownership. Without team slug expansion:
- Overrides may appear "missing" despite an approved team review.
- Friction occurs in workflows where teams are mandated reviewers.
- Manual workaround (individual member approvals) increases review latency.

## Proposal
Add support for resolving GitHub team slugs in CODEOWNERS referenced patterns and PR review events.

### Resolution Flow
1. Detect CODEOWNERS entries beginning with `@org/team`.
2. Query GitHub Teams API to list active team members (cache w/ short TTL, e.g. 10m during a single run).
3. When evaluating override coverage, treat any approving review (or explicit override phrase) by a member of that team as satisfying the CODEOWNER requirement for paths touched by schema changes.
4. Provide trace metadata: `overrideSources: ["direct-user", "team-member"]`.

### Caching / Failure Strategy
- If team expansion fails (API error), fallback to current behavior and mark `overrideEvaluation.warnings` with a recoverable advisory.
- Add config env flag `SCHEMA_CONTRACT_ALLOW_TEAM_FALLBACK=false` to optionally fail hard instead.

## Security Considerations
- Ensure least-scope token (needs `read:org`).
- Avoid persisting member lists beyond runtime context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a BREAKING change and an approving review by any member of a CODEOWNER team, override is applied.
- Unit tests simulate team member resolution (mock API) including: success, partial failure, and failure fallback.
- Trace field includes `resolvedTeamMembers` size for each team.
- Documentation updated (governance README override section).

## Out of Scope
- Nested team membership recursion (resolve only direct members initially).

## Follow-Up (Optional)
- Add metrics: count of overrides satisfied via team membership vs direct user.

Labels: enhancement, schema-contract, governance
t: Schema Contract Overrides: Support @org/team Slug Expansion in CODEOWNERS Evaluation

## Context
Feature 002 (PR #5471) produces `change-report.json` describing schema changes. Each entry currently lacks historical origin data beyond classification and deprecation metadata.

## Problem
Governance and product stakeholders may need to answer:
- How long has this field/type existed?
- Is a BREAKING removal targeting a very recent addition (potential churn smell)?
- Are rapid add/remove cycles increasing maintenance cost?

Without origin timestamps, analysis requires manual `git blame` or archaeological diff traversal.

## Proposal
Augment change entries with `firstCommit` metadata referencing the earliest git commit introducing the symbol (type, field, enum value, scalar) still present or being removed.

### Extraction Strategy
1. On diff run, execute a targeted `git log -S` / `git blame` against `schema.graphql` lines relevant to the symbol (optimize by pre-building a line index map).
2. Cache per run to avoid redundant blame calls.
3. Populate fields:
   - `firstCommit.hash`
   - `firstCommit.date` (ISO8601)
   - `firstCommit.author`
4. For removed items, still attempt to retrieve origin via previous snapshot context or historical git log search.

### Performance Guardrails
- Provide env flag `SCHEMA_CONTRACT_ENRICH_ORIGIN=true` (default false initially).
- Hard cap on total blame invocations (e.g. 300) with graceful fallback (set `firstCommitResolution="partial"`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- ADDITIVE entry includes `firstCommit` for the newly added symbol.
- BREAKING removal entry includes `firstCommit` of the removed symbol.
- Report-level `metadata.enrichment.origin.enabled=true|false` and summary counts.
- Tests: origin extraction success, fallback when cap exceeded, disabled mode.
- Documentation update (governance README & quickstart advanced section).

## Risks / Mitigations
- Large git history performance → mitigate via batching & caching.
- Non-unique lines (collision) → fallback to first match; note limitation in docs.

Labels: enhancement, schema-contract, governance, observability
t: Schema Contract: Enrich Change Report Entries with firstCommit Metadata

## Context
Feature 002 (PR #5471) infers scalar JSON type categories (string|number|boolean|object|array|unknown) heuristically (description / naming hints). This is adequate for most internal scalars but can misclassify ambiguous or polymorphic scalars, and does not provide an explicit single source of truth for downstream tooling.

## Problem
- Ambiguity: Description-based inference may drift or break if wording changes.
- Interoperability: External consumers (SDK generators, analytics) may want guaranteed machine-readable typing metadata.
- Governance: A future BREAKING reclassification could appear inadvertent if prior intent was never explicit.

## Proposal
Introduce an optional directive (e.g. `@jsonType(category: STRING|NUMBER|BOOLEAN|OBJECT|ARRAY|UNKNOWN, stable: Boolean = true)`) attachable to custom scalar definitions.

### Behavior
- During diff, if directive present it overrides heuristic inference.
- If directive category differs from heuristic, include an INFO note (`scalarEvaluation.note = "jsonTypeOverride"`).
- If a scalar without directive changes heuristic category → still BREAKING (as today) unless both old and new categories are within a predefined compatible widening set (future extension, out of scope here).
- Add validator to ensure category is from enum set.

### Schema Printer Integration
- Preserve directive in `schema.graphql` (ensure printer keeps directive ordering stable).

### Acceptance Criteria
- New directive recognized and affects `scalarEvaluations` output.
- JSON Schema for `change-report` optionally includes `scalarEvaluations[].jsonTypeSource = "directive"|"heuristic"`.
- Tests: (a) directive overrides heuristic, (b) conflicting directive vs heuristic note, (c) unchanged directive stable, (d) missing directive fallback.
- Documentation: Quickstart advanced section + governance guidance for when to add directive.

## Migration Plan
- Initially optional; encourage adoption for public-facing or high-risk scalars first.

## Out of Scope
- Automatic inference of future widening compatibility sets.

## Follow-Up
- Potential lint rule to require directive for newly added scalars.

Labels: enhancement, schema-contract, developer-experience
t: Schema Contract: Directive to Explicitly Annotate Scalar JSON Type Category

## Epic: Automate Authorization Forest Regeneration via AST

### Goal
Eliminate drift between `authorization-forest.md` / `credential-based-authorization.md` and actual code by generating graphs + classification table automatically from `*.service.authorization.ts`.

### Business Value
- Trustworthy documentation
- Reduced manual maintenance & review overhead
- Faster onboarding & security auditing

### Success Metrics
- CI detects & blocks undocumented structural changes
- 100% of PRs modifying authorization services have regenerated artifacts
- >80% reduction in manual doc-only PRs touching forest structure after rollout

### User Stories
1. CLI Generation Command: As a developer, I can run `npm run auth:forest:generate` to regenerate JSON + Mermaid + table.
2. CI Drift Detection: As a developer, CI fails if generated artifacts differ after running generator.
3. JSON Graph Artifact: As a reviewer, I can inspect `authorization-forest.json` for machine-readable structure (nodes, edges, classifications, meta).
4. Root Change Alert: As a security engineer, I receive a PR comment summarizing added/removed roots.
5. Structural Diff Tool: As a developer, I can run `npm run auth:forest:diff -- --base <ref>` to see structural differences.
6. Pragmas Overrides: As a contributor, I can override classification with inline pragmas (e.g., `// auth-graph:force-leaf`).
7. Config Driven Rules: As a maintainer, I can adjust detection via `auth-graph.config.json`.
8. Guarded Blocks: As a documentation maintainer, only guarded sections inside `authorization-forest.md` are auto-updated.
9. Incremental Parsing Cache: As an engineer, generation time is reduced on subsequent runs via file content hashing.
10. Classification Tests: As a maintainer, unit tests validate classification logic & edge detection.

### Acceptance Criteria (Aggregate)
- Generator outputs: `authorization-forest.json`, updates guarded blocks in `authorization-forest.md`.
- Mermaid diagrams include Platform, User, Organization, Account, AiServer roots.
- JSON schema: `{ version, generatedAt, gitSha, nodes:[{name,filePath,classification,overrides}], edges:[{from,to,reason}], stats:{roots,edges,leaves,total} }`.
- CI workflow `auth-forest.yml` runs on PR changes to `src/**/*.service.authorization.ts`.
- Non-empty diff triggers failure with summary.

### Risks
- False positives if naming diverges → mitigated via config + pragmas.
- AST performance cost → mitigated by caching.
- Manual edits lost in auto sections → mitigated by guarded block markers.

### Out of Scope (Phase 1)
- Visualization web UI
- Historical diffs storage beyond current vs base

### Tasks (Initial)
- [ ] Scaffold generator script (ts-morph)
- [ ] Implement classification logic
- [ ] Build graph + JSON emitter
- [ ] Implement Mermaid template renderer
- [ ] Add guarded block replace logic
- [ ] Add diff command
- [ ] Add CI GitHub Action
- [ ] Add unit tests & config file
- [ ] Add pragma parsing + validation
- [ ] Documentation (README section)

### Follow-Up Phase 2
- Changelog integration
- PR comment bot enhancements (severity tagging)
- Cycle detection alerts

---
Feel free to adjust scope or add owners.
t: Epic: Automate Authorization Forest Regeneration via AST

## Epic: Authorization Forest Changelog & Structural Audit Trail

### Goal
Introduce a durable, queryable changelog capturing structural authorization graph changes (roots, edges, leaves, reclassifications) to improve auditability and governance.

### Business Value
- Historical traceability for security/compliance
- Faster incident / regression analysis
- Clear rationale trail for significant structural shifts

### Success Metrics
- 100% of structural changes produce a changelog entry
- Ability to answer "When did X become a root?" in <30s
- Zero undocumented root changes (CI enforced)

### User Stories
1. Markdown Changelog: As a reviewer I can read `authorization-forest-changelog.md` with chronological entries.
2. Auto Append: As a developer, structural changes auto-generate a dated changelog entry during CI.
3. Root Change Highlight: As a security engineer, root additions/removals are grouped under a dedicated heading.
4. Machine JSON Log: As a tooling engineer, I can consume `authorization-forest-changelog.json` for dashboards.
5. Rationale Preservation: As a maintainer I can add a manual rationale block per entry that is preserved on regeneration.
6. PR Summary Comment: As a reviewer I receive a PR comment summarizing structural changes and linking to new changelog section.
7. Snapshot Linkage: As an auditor I can navigate from a changelog entry to the exact JSON snapshot commit (blob URL) for that structure.
8. Aggregated Daily Entries: As a maintainer I want multiple commits in a single day collapsed into one dated entry per PR.
9. Semantic Version Enforcement: As a release manager I am prompted (CI fail) to bump version when roots change and no version bump detected.
10. Tag Filtering: As a security analyst I can filter entries for root changes only via markdown anchors or tags (e.g. `[ROOT]`).

### Acceptance Criteria (Aggregate)
- Changelog file includes current snapshot header (counts + root list) regenerated each run.
- Per-date section lists Added/Removed/Reclassified/Added Services/Removed Services with PR # and short SHA.
- JSON log mirrors markdown content (schema versioned).
- Guard markers protect manual rationale blocks.
- CI step fails if structural diff exists without matching new changelog entry referencing current commit SHA.

### Risks
- Merge conflicts on busy branches → mitigate via deterministic ordering + daily aggregation.
- Over-noise for minor reclassifications → allow opt-out label (e.g. `auth-changelog-skip`) with review gate.

### Out of Scope (Phase 1)
- External storage/DB of historical snapshots beyond repo
- Visualization UI

### Tasks (Initial)
- [ ] Define JSON schema for changelog file
- [ ] Extend generator diff to emit changelog fragment
- [ ] Markdown merge & anchor/tag rendering
- [ ] Preserve rationale blocks (marker parsing)
- [ ] CI validation step for required changelog updates
- [ ] PR comment integration
- [ ] Optional semantic version check
- [ ] Documentation of workflow & contribution guidelines

### Follow-Up Phase 2
- Dashboard integration
- SLA alerts for unexpected root churn
- Signed attestations for compliance exports

---
Adjust or assign as needed.
t: Epic: Authorization Forest Changelog & Structural Audit Trail

- [ ] Upgrade `graphql` to >=16.11.0
- [ ] Upgrade `@apollo/server` from 4.x → 5.x
- [ ] Upgrade `@nestjs/graphql` + `@nestjs/apollo` from 12.x → 13.x

- all resolver types + scalars

**Describe the bug**
The server code base has had circular dependencies introduced, which are both bad practice and a ticking bomb ready to go off (server will not start)






**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Go to '...'
2. Click on '....'
3. Scroll down to '....'
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
TypeORM one-one relationships should not have awareness of the parent within the child entity.

Places this has been introduced: CalloutsSet, Memo, Whiteboard at least. 



**Additional context**
They concern TypeORM one-one relations - which we pretty much always do as a one way relation to avoid circular dependencies. I came across them as the server failed to start for me, and when checking out circular dependencies (pnpm run circular-dependencies, after installing madge) I saw that a bunch had creeped back into the server repo:

What happens is that NestJS tries to load a file for starting but that another file it needs has not yet loaded. It is something I have had many fights with over the years, and is part of the reason I am so against any usage of forwardRefs. The issue is this case is the child one-one relation, which has been added to CalloutsSet, Memo, Whiteboard - back to their "parents". 

In theory these entities do not need to know about their parents, and doing so basically breaks the encapsulation.
t: BUG: circular dependencies in code base

## Description

As an architect I want to ensure granted consistency between existing user databases, as we can not have simple single source of truth because stack includes third-party products, which relies on their own sources of truth.
To be exact, I want reliable consistency between Alkemio user profiles, Kratos identities and Synapse user database, which can not be broken by infinite number of edge cases.
This will allow us to have less fragile and more secure system and will allow to reduce amount of code in different parts of system, when we can rely on this consistency.


## Acceptance criteria

### first line of priority 
- [ ] when user identity in Kratos is created, this automatically reflects in creation of user in the Alkemio DB, and this is granted and does not depend on availability of alkemio server at the moment of creation of Kratos identity or any other edge conditions. It is reflected in the Alkemio DB in 100% of cases, no matter what.
- [ ] when user profile is created in Alkemio DB, this automatically reflects in the creation of user in the Synapse, and this does not depend on edge cases, like availability of Synapse etc, and also granted to have this reflection in 100% cases.

### second line of priority 
- [ ] When user is removed/disabled in Kratos, then all OIDC sessions which belongs to this user are deleted. Granted in 100% of cases, regardless of current situation on the backend.
- [ ] ?  Possibly user is also removed from Synapse (subject of discussion)
- [ ] when user is logged out (Kratos session removed), corresponding OIDC session is also removed/invalidated. Granted in 100% of cases, regardless of current situation on the backend.

### third line of priority 
- [ ] when user change name in Alkemio interface, this gets reflected in the Kratos and, possibly, Synapse (subject of discussion). Granted in 100% of cases, regardless of current situation on the backend.
- [ ] when user change name via Kratos, this gets reflected in the Alkemio DB and, possibly, Synapse (subject of discussion). Granted in 100% of cases, regardless of current situation on the backend.
- - When user change name in Matrix client, then what? Do we enforce any reflection?

## Additional Context

### We have next boundary conditions :
1) When user is created in Kratos, the only subsystem is granted to work at this time is DB service, which is used by Kratos (otherwise user creation would fail)
2) We do not control Kratos code, and we should not touch manually Kratos DB for number of reasons.
3) When user is created in the Alkemio DB, the only granted subsystem to work at this time is DB service, which is used by Alkemio server (otherwise user creation would fail).
4) We control Alkemio DB and Alkemio server code.
5) When something is changed in Synapse, the only granted subsystem to work at this time is DB service, which is used by Synapse (otherwise modifications would fail). 
6) We don't control Synapse and should we should not touch manually Synapse DB for number of reasons.
7) user experience must be non-blocking. I.e. when user logs in for the first time and Synapse is not accessible due to some reasons, user flow should not be blocked waiting for synapse to get back online. Same for Kratos and Alkemio server 

### Solution:
tiny sync service (working title: Syncer) with, effectively, local to the services/databases persistent queues.

1) Syncer does not touch itself databases of Kratos, Alkemio server and Synapse, but operates via their APIs.

2) As we don't control Kratos, our Syncer should sit next to Kratos in the sidecar, this grants availability of it if Kratos running. 

3) Syncer register webhook in Kratos, which is called when new user if added (and later when name, email whatever is changed). All what webhook does it to add Kratos ID of newly created identity to "kratos_outbox" table(which resides on the same DB service with Kratos). This ensure that on Kratos user creation we get reflection in the "kratos_outbox"  with nearly 100% probability (same DB same pod etc).  <sub>
another possible design choice is to separate webhook sidecar (this part MUST be sidecar) and Syncer, which then live in separate deployment. Structurally I consider this to be a better solution, although I still would keep syncer and webhook in single repo, just build two containers. extremely tiny sidecar, and tiny syncer.)
</sub>

4)  Syncer has a worker, which "monitors" kratos_outbox table (there are different approaches, depending on the database used, postgres would be better, as it has listeners/notifiers, but mysql also can be done) and when there are new records (one or many) in the "kratos_outbox", it start process of creation of user(s) in the alkemio server (by using internal REST API trigger which is introduced in #5582 ). When and only new user successfully added to the alkemio server, authId is removed from kratos_outbox, if not, use typical flows to ensure it happens as soon as alkemio server is available. This gives as persistent queue independent on state of the system during creation of Kratos identity and granted propagation of such identity to the alkemio server with 100% guaranty. Of course, on start worker always checks is there are some remaining records in the kratos_outbox and handles them.

5) for creation of records in the "alkemio_outbox" table (which resided on the same DB service we have alkemio DB and keeps userIds of newly created users), we have two options (design choice):
a) we have a trigger on alkemio DB, which is triggered on adding record to the "user" table, and trigger adds record to "alkemio_outbox" table.
b) alkemio server creates record in alkemio_outbox table in the same transaction as creation of user.
In both cases, we have 100% guaranty of adding record to the "alkemio_outbox", if user was added to alkemio DB.<sub>
In general case, I'd prefer b) as better and cleaner solution, but with typeORM a) might be better way.
</sub>

6) Syncer has another worker which monitors "alkemio_outbox" table, for the records indicating that new user was created in alkemio DB. Then similarly reflects them in the Synapse similar to process in 3) . With 100% guaranty, regardless of conditions.

7) we can also add manual or scheduled triggers for consistency checks and resynchronizations, if there is a edge-case, which, after all, still can not be handled by this approach, as all infrastructure is there and all what those checks need to do is to populate respective outboxes for missing IDs. Rest is taken care automatically.

In this case we always granted to have consistency and users to be present everywhere at any meaningful moment of time.



Cost of development:
While it might look complex, it is in reality very simple, trivial and straightforward service, with tiny amount of code. With SDD, most likely, can be finalized over a day. Then there extra work on integration into k8s deployment etc. And some work around in terms of creation of repo, github CI etc (but workflows themself is a part of initial writeup).

Impact:
1) this allows us to remove fragility from the system (which is present there now and over last week I've already  meet cases when consistency is lost) and increases rigidity where it matters.
2) it allows us to write code under assumption of present consistency and reduces amount of communication between server and matrix-adapter, and some code from server and matrix adapter.
3) it solves for number of edge cases we currently have uncovered and additional ones we will have when we open Synapse and even more of them, once we allow use of alkemio OIDC provider for more than just Synapse.

_To be added during the refinement_

# Feature Specification: Messaging Image Upload

**Feature Branch**: `021-messaging-image-upload`
**Created**: 2026-01-13
**Status**: Draft
**Input**: User description: "We are working user to user messaging, and I want to expand it with being able to send images (through a button, but also just by pasting it into the chat dialog). Can you help me specify?"

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-01-13

**Please review the below clarifications - mainly around storage**

- Q: Can a message contain both text and images? -> A: Mixed Content: A message can contain both text and an image (effectively an image with a caption).
- Q: How should the upload API be structured? -> A: Two-Step (Separate Storage API): Client uploads to a dedicated Storage Endpoint first, receives an ID/URL, then sends the Chat Message referencing that ID. (Matches Memo implementation).
- Q: How to model message types (Text vs Image)? -> A: Flexible (Single Type): One `Message` type with optional/nullable fields for text and attachments.
- Q: Image lifecycle/deletion policy? -> A: Deferred: Message deletion is not supported in the current system, so image cleanup is out of scope (Additive Only).
- Q: Where should the image be stored (storage bucket)? -> A: Room-Bound: The Room entity should have its own dedicated Storage Bucket for chat assets.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Send Image via Upload Button (Priority: P1)

As a user in a chat, I want to click a button to select an image from my device so that I can share visual context with my conversation partner.

**Why this priority**: Core functionality requested by the user.

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by opening a chat, clicking upload, selecting a file, and verifying it appears in the sent message stream.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a chat conversation is open, **When** I click the image upload button and select a valid image file, **Then** the image is uploaded and sent as a message.
2. **Given** an invalid file (wrong type or too large), **When** I try to upload it, **Then** I see an error message explaining why it failed.

---

### User Story 2 - Send Image via Clipboard Paste (Priority: P1)

As a user, I want to paste an image directly into the chat input area so that I can quickly share screenshots or copied images without saving them to a file first.

**Why this priority**: improved workflow efficiency, explicitly requested.

**Independent Test**: Copy an image to clipboard (e.g. screenshot), focus chat input, press Ctrl+V/Cmd+V, verify image is staged or sent.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an image in my clipboard, **When** I paste into the chat input, **Then** the image is recognized and prepared for sending (previewed or uploaded).
2. **Given** the image is ready, **When** I confirm send, **Then** the image appears in the chat stream.

---

### User Story 3 - View Received Images (Priority: P1)

**Anything we can/should take over from the image work from Valentin?**

As a chat participant, I want to see images sent to me within the chat history so that I can understand the visual information being shared.

**Why this priority**: Required for the feature to be useful to the receiver.

**Independent Test**: Have User A send an image, User B views the chat and sees the rendered image.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a message with an image, **When** I scroll to it in the chat, **Then** the image is displayed (thumbnail or full width).
2. **Given** a large image, **When** I click it, **Then** it opens in a larger view/lightbox (Optional but standard UX).

### Edge Cases

- What happens when network fails during upload? (Should retry or show error).
- How does system handle very large images? (Validation error).
- What if the receiver is on a slow connection? (Load thumbnail first).

## Requirements *(mandatory)*
"Mixed Content" - optional text caption alongside the image attachment in a single message bubbl
### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: System MUST accept image files of types JPEG, PNG, WEBP.
- **FR-002**: System MUST validate file size is under 10MB (Assumed reasonable limit).
- **FR-003**: System MUST store the uploaded image securely and provide a retrievable URL.
- **FR-004**: Message schema MUST support "Mixed Content" - optional text caption alongside the image attachment in a single message bubble.
- **FR-005**: UI MUST provide an "Upload Image" button in the chat interface.
- **FR-006**: UI MUST detect image paste events in the chat input area.
- **FR-007**: UI SHOULD display a preview of the image before sending.
- **FR-008**: System MUST reject non-image files uploaded via this mechanism.
- **FR-009**: The upload process MUST follow a Two-Step pattern: 1) Upload to Storage Service -> 2) Send Message with reference.
- **FR-010**: The specific Storage Service used MUST be consistent with the Memo implementation (likely StorageBucket or similar).
- **FR-011**: Message Schema MUST use a single type configuration: `text` (optional) and `image` (optional).
- **FR-012**: System MUST enforce that a Message has at least one content element (Text OR Image).
- **FR-014**: The Room entity MUST have a `storageBucket` reference to simple asset management.
- **FR-015**: Uploads MUST be directed to the Room's storage bucket.

### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*

- **Message**: Single entity. Fields: `content/markdown` (nullable strings), `attachments` (nullable list).
- **Room**: Modified to include `storageBucket` reference
- **Message**: Single entity. Fields: `content/markdown` (nullable strings), `attachments` (nullable list).
- **ImageResource**: Represents the stored file reference.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Users can successfully upload and send a supported image in under 10 seconds on broadband.
- **SC-002**: 100% of uploaded valid images are displayed correctly to the receiver.
- **SC-003**: System rejects invalid file types or oversized files 100% of the time with a user-friendly error.

## Assumptions

- We are using the existing file storage infrastructure.
- Messaging is within the context of existing "Rooms".
- Standard Authorization applies (Room members can view).
t: Image upload for chats

## Summary

The migration `1764897584127-conversationArchitectureRefactor.ts` has a bug that left **28 orphaned `conversation_direct` rooms** in the database. These rooms exist but have no conversation linking to them, making their messages (110 total) inaccessible through the API.

## Root Cause

**Race condition in Step 2B's CTE-based deletion:**

The migration's Step 2B merges USER_USER conversation pairs that shared the same Matrix room (via `externalRoomID`). The logic:

1. Find conversation pairs by shared `externalRoomID`
2. Insert memberships for the "kept" conversation (rn=1)
3. Delete the "duplicate" conversation (rn=2)
4. Delete the "duplicate" room (rn=2)

**The bug:** Each SQL statement recomputes the CTE independently:

```sql
WITH paired AS (
  SELECT c.id as conv_id, r.id as room_id, ...
  FROM conversation c
  JOIN room r ON c."roomId" = r.id  -- ← This JOIN breaks after conversation deletion
  ...
)
```

When the conversation deletion runs first, it succeeds. But when the room deletion runs next, the CTE **can't find the rn=2 room anymore** because the conversation that referenced it has been deleted, breaking the JOIN.

## Evidence

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| Total `conversation_direct` rooms | 56 |
| Rooms linked to conversations | 28 |
| **Orphaned rooms (no conversation)** | **28** |
| Messages in orphaned rooms | 110 |
| Messages in linked rooms | 251 |

Every orphaned room has a "twin" linked room with reversed user UUIDs:
- **Linked**: `conversation-a92a9063-...-35ae549c-...` ✓
- **Orphaned**: `conversation-35ae549c-...-a92a9063-...` ✗

## Affected Room IDs (Production)

```
78e01bc6-2ce5-4b1a-bb72-b650a2ddb8e1, 7e49dcce-1d6d-4bb5-a6ae-6bb4a4c45de3,
83ff7993-c752-4179-acca-707ee2396121, 861e45f7-1556-4e05-82a2-b255f062f3cc,
986223b8-af60-4789-8fdf-62619337fcdd, a11b2be0-4fc3-45fb-a18b-e01b2838a7e0,

```

## Recommended Fix

Create a cleanup migration:

```sql
-- Delete orphaned conversation_direct rooms
DELETE FROM room 
WHERE type = 'conversation_direct' 
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conversation c WHERE c."roomId" = room.id);
```

**Important:** Do NOT delete the corresponding Matrix rooms in Synapse - they are shared with the "linked" twin rooms and contain the actual messages.

## Impact

- 28 orphaned database records consuming space
- 110 messages technically inaccessible (but duplicated in linked rooms via shared Matrix room)
- No data loss since paired rooms shared the same Matrix room

## Labels

`bug`, `database`, `migration`
t: [Bug] Migration left 28 orphaned conversation_direct rooms due to CTE race condition

## Description

A user was able to create a duplicate account using the same email address with different letter casing. This was reported by our customer success manager:

> A user signed up and created a new account, despite already having an existing account from 2 years ago. Both profiles have the same email address but with different casing (e.g. `user@example.com` vs `User@example.com`).

The platform is treating email addresses as case-sensitive, allowing two separate accounts to be created for what is effectively the same email address (per RFC 5321, the domain part of email addresses is case-insensitive, and in practice the local part is also treated as case-insensitive by virtually all mail providers).

## Root Cause

This is likely a regression introduced during the **MySQL → PostgreSQL migration**. MySQL's default collation (`utf8_general_ci`) is case-insensitive, meaning email lookups would naturally match regardless of casing. PostgreSQL, however, uses case-sensitive text comparison by default, so `user@example.com` and `User@example.com` are treated as distinct values.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register an account with email `user@example.com`
2. Sign up again (possibly via a different auth method such as LinkedIn or Microsoft) with email `User@example.com`
3. Two separate accounts are created for the same email address

## Expected Behavior

Email addresses should be treated as case-insensitive throughout the platform. Signing up with `User@example.com` when `user@example.com` already exists should either:
- Recognize the existing account and prevent duplicate creation, or
- Normalize email addresses to lowercase on registration/login

## Suggested Fix

Consider one or more of:
1. **Normalize emails to lowercase** on registration, login, and any email-based lookups
2. **Use `ILIKE` or `LOWER()` in PostgreSQL queries** where email comparison is performed
3. **Add a unique constraint using `LOWER(email)`** on the database column to prevent future duplicates at the DB level
4. **Run a data migration** to identify and merge existing duplicate accounts caused by this issue

## Immediate Action

- [ ] Inform the customer success manager about the known duplicate accounts so they can decide whether to merge them or notify the affected user(s) directly

## Description
As a facilitator/(sub-)space owner/administrator, I want to communicate with my space members. It is the equivalent of a "team channel". It allows the members to reach others easily. 

This is different from a group chat, in that the group is defined by default. It is different from "Status Updates from Leads" in that this will be many-to-many.  

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The membership of the chat/channel is the membership of the (sub-)Space. 
- [ ] Messages should have all existing features of 1-to-1 messages, including emoji reactions. 
- [ ] Messages should be able to tag a (sub-)Space member. 
- [ ] Messages should have a "reply-to" option. User must be able to select a certain message for a "quoted" response. 
- [ ] Messages should be multi-modal, i.e., non-text based messages should be permitted. This includes images, photos, videos, audio,  attachments, etc. 
- [ ] The push/poll limit must be minimal, ensuring live communication. 
- [ ] In a ideal stage, the chat window/interface should not disrupt the user's workflow, i.e., the user must be able to work simultaneously while the chat in ongoing. 


## Expected Behaviour

- [ ] Every new (sub-)Space create a channel with the membership of the channel tied to the (sub-)Space. This is a "room". 
- [ ] The (sub-)Space admin can only enable/disable this channel. The (sub-)Space admin cannot add or remove members from this channel. If a new member joins, they will be added to the channel. If a member leaves, they will be removed from the channel. 
- [ ] The (sub-)Space admin can set the history for the channel, including disappearing messages and available history for new member (all available, past month, past week, past three days, past day, since joining etc.). 
- [ ] The (sub-)Space channel should have an option to view all members from within the chat window. This will match the (sub-)Space membership, however, visible within the communication panel. 
- [ ] A user must be able to edit a message. Edited messages will carry an "Edited" tag. 
- [ ] A member user must be able to delete only their message. A member user cannot delete another member's message. 
- [ ] A (sub-)Space admin can delete any message. The deleted message will be replaced with "The message has been deleted by the (sub-)Space admin." 
- [ ] Any member must be able to report a message. The reported message will be reviewed by the (sub-)Space admin. The (sub-)Space admin can action on the reporting by deleting the message, or resolving the "report". 
- [ ] Each (sub-)Space member can set their notification preferences for each channel/(sub-)Space chat they are present in. 
- [ ] Each (sub-)Space member can also mute notifications for a set period, even if/when they general notifications is turned on. 

## Additional Context 
- [ ] Should an admin be able to create multiple channels per (sub-)Space? E.g. Fun, coordination, team updates, meme, etc. channels. _Recommendation: Start with 1-to-1 mapping, one channel per (sub-)Space._ 
- [ ] Where does this chat/channel reside (UI/UX)? Some options: Within the current chat dialog, pinned somewhere in the (sub-)Space, somewhere along the Guidance Chat, in the sub-(Space) panel, etc. _Recommendation: Start within the chat dialog for v1. It will continue to be disruptive to the user's workflow, but it can be a start._ @jeroentskui for your inputs/ideas.
- [ ] Include a button to start the Jitsi meeting. _Recommendation: Avoid in v1 since Jitsi meetings are not ready for sub-spaces._ 
- [ ] In a future state where multiple channels are allowed, admin must choose chat mode v. post mode. Chat mode is regular chat, while post mode requires specific posts (think, Teams channel). Recommendation: Since 1-to-1 for (sub-)Space to channel, start with chat only channel. 
- [ ] In a future version, admin must be able to invite a VC/agent to the chat. The agent must be able to respond to specific tagged asks, e.g., "summarise today's chat discussions." Recommendation: Avoid in v1, since AI architecture work requires an overhaul.
t: (Sub)-Space Chat

## Summary

All singular nested DTO fields in `src/domain/collaboration/callout-contribution/dto/callout.contribution.dto.create.ts` (`post`, `whiteboard`, `link`, `memo`, `collaboraDocument`) currently use `@ValidateNested({ each: true })` without the `@Type()` decorator from `class-transformer`.

This is incorrect for singular (non-array) nested objects:
- `{ each: true }` is intended for array elements and is a no-op / incorrect for singular fields.
- Without `@Type(() => NestedType)`, NestJS's `ValidationPipe` cannot properly transform and validate the nested plain object into the target DTO class.

## Required Changes

For each of the following fields, replace `@ValidateNested({ each: true })` with `@ValidateNested()` and add `@Type(() => NestedType)`:

- `post?: CreatePostInput`
- `whiteboard?: CreateWhiteboardInput`
- `link?: CreateLinkInput`
- `memo?: CreateMemoInput`
- `collaboraDocument?: CreateCollaboraDocumentInput`

### Example fix

```diff
+import { Type } from 'class-transformer';

   @Field(() => CreateCollaboraDocumentInput, { nullable: true })
   @IsOptional()
-  @ValidateNested({ each: true })
+  @ValidateNested()
+  @Type(() => CreateCollaboraDocumentInput)
   collaboraDocument?: CreateCollaboraDocumentInput;
```

## Context

This pattern was identified during PR #5970 (https://github.com/alkem-io/server/pull/5970) review (comment: https://github.com/alkem-io/server/pull/5970#discussion_r3077367924). It was intentionally deferred from that PR to keep the new `collaboraDocument` field consistent with pre-existing fields, and to address all fields together in a dedicated cleanup.

Requested by: @antst
t: Cleanup: Fix @ValidateNested({ each: true }) and missing @Type() on singular nested DTO fields in CreateCalloutContributionInput
