## Background

PR #6014 surfaced a recurring architectural pattern across leaf services:

```ts
// 1. Build entity in memory
// 2. Create EXTERNAL resource (Matrix room) OR call self-saving child service
const room = await roomService.createRoom(...);
entity.comments = room;
// or:
entity.whiteboard = await whiteboardService.createWhiteboard(...);  // self-saves + materializes

// 3. Save parent
const saved = await this.repo.save(entity);  // <-- if this throws, step 2's effect leaks

// 4. Phase-2 materialize via OrRollback helper (covers post-save only)
```

If step 3 fails:
- Matrix rooms are orphaned (no Alkemio entity references them).
- Self-saved children (Whiteboard, Post, Memo) persist with no parent ownership.

The post-save `materializeProfileContentAndVisualsOrRollback` helper protects only the post-save phase; the pre-save side-effect leak is a separate concern.

## Sites fixed in PR #6014

- [x] `discussion.service.ts` — Matrix room before save
- [x] `event.service.ts` — Matrix room before save
- [x] `post.service.ts` — Matrix room before save (audited beyond CR's list, same pattern)
- [x] `template.service.ts` WHITEBOARD branch — whiteboard self-completes before parent save
- [x] `templates.set.service.ts` — template self-completes before attach-save

## Sites with the same pattern, NOT touched by PR #6014

- [ ] `callout.service.ts:133, 426` — Matrix room created before parent save in regular callout flow
- [ ] `callout-framing.service.ts:244` — `whiteboardService.createWhiteboard` (self-saves) before parent framing save
- [ ] `callout-framing.service.ts:265` — `memoService.createMemo` (self-saves) before parent framing save
- [ ] `callout-framing.service.ts:278, 498` — `linkService.createLink` (in-memory, lower risk)
- [ ] `callout-contribution.service.ts:120` — `whiteboardService.createWhiteboard` (self-saves)
- [ ] `callout-contribution.service.ts:128` — `postService.createPost` (self-saves)
- [ ] `callout-contribution.service.ts:137` — `linkService.createLink` (in-memory)
- [ ] `callout-contribution.service.ts:144` — `memoService.createMemo` (self-saves)
- [ ] `communication.service.ts:42` — Matrix room before save
- [ ] `forum.service.ts:70, 82, 219, 234` — `communicationAdapter.createSpace` patterns
- [ ] `admin.communication.space.sync.service.ts:94, 207, 250` — admin-time Matrix space creation

## Suggested fix shape

The pragmatic per-site fix is the same "wrap parent save in try/catch with explicit cleanup of the pre-save effect":

```ts
let saved: T;
try {
  saved = await this.repo.save(entity);
} catch (error) {
  await this.cleanupPreSaveEffect(...).catch(logErrorAndContinue);
  throw error;
}
```

A more architectural fix would be to flip self-saving leaves (Post, Whiteboard, Memo) to in-memory-only `createX` methods (parent saves via cascade), with separate `materializeXContent(saved, rollback)` methods called by the orchestrator. We already did this for Link, CalloutFraming, CalloutContribution in PR #6014. Extending it to Post/Whiteboard/Memo would eliminate the self-saved-child leak class entirely.

The Matrix room leak class still requires explicit cleanup regardless (Matrix is non-transactional), but consolidating the pattern in one helper method per service keeps the noise low.

## Why split out

The fixes in PR #6014 were already large, focused on fixing #6004 / #6005 (template profile materialization) plus the Tier 2 wave that CR's review surfaced. Tackling every callout/framing/contribution leaf and the Matrix-create patterns elsewhere would have ballooned the PR and slowed merge. Tracking here so it isn't lost.

## References

- PR #6014 — initial fix and the audit that surfaced this list
- File-service-go migration PR #5969 — original split that introduced the two-phase materialize pattern
t: Resource-leak pattern: external/self-saved resources before parent save

## Problem

`@IsUUID('4')` rejects UUIDv7. The platform is transitioning to v7 (file-service-go already emits v7), so DTOs locked to v4 will reject server-issued IDs once those propagate into the affected flows.

Discovered while triaging PR #5970 — Valentin flagged it on `collabora.document.dto.update.ts`. The Collabora DTOs were fixed in 65025a6cd by switching to `@IsUUID('all')`. The remaining `'4'`-locked sites still need the same treatment.

## Sites to update

```
src/domain/communication/conversation/dto/conversation.dto.create.ts:36   — @IsUUID('4', { each: true })
src/services/api-rest/identity-resolve/dto/identity-resolve.request.dto.ts:4   — @IsUUID('4')
src/services/api-rest/identity-resolve/dto/identity-resolve.response.dto.ts:4  — @IsUUID('4')
src/services/api-rest/identity-resolve/dto/identity-resolve.response.dto.ts:7  — @IsUUID('4')
```

Three files, four call sites.

## Recommended fix

Switch each `@IsUUID('4')` (and `@IsUUID('4', { each: true })`) to `@IsUUID('all')` (preserving the `{ each: true }` option where used).

class-validator 0.14 types `IsUUID` as `'3' | '4' | '5' | 'all'`, but the underlying `validator` package's `'all'` regex matches v1–v8 plus `nil`/`max`. So `'all'` widens correctly without becoming permissive (it still rejects garbage strings).

## Out of scope (don't change)

The 20 bare `@IsUUID()` calls (no version) — those already accept any version (the runtime defaults `version` to `'all'` when undefined). Leave them alone.

## Why a separate PR

This is a small, mechanical sweep that touches identity-resolve and conversation flows. Keeping it out of #5970 (Collabora) avoids mixing a security-validation change with the feature PR's review surface.
t: Widen @IsUUID('4') → @IsUUID('all') for UUIDv7 transition

## Description

As an **authenticated Alkemio user**
I want **to see the list of my currently-active sessions in a dedicated page, revoke any individual session, and optionally sign out of all my other devices (or everywhere) in one click**
So that **if I forget to sign out on a shared device, suspect a session is compromised, or just want to clear stale logins, I can do so myself without having to wait for the absolute session TTL to expire or contact an operator.**

### Context

Once the OIDC MVP lands, user sessions live as Redis-backed records keyed per session id, holding the Kratos identity, the OIDC token set, and timestamps. The only user-facing teardown today is the standard logout, which terminates the *caller's own current* session via RP-initiated logout. There is no way for a user to:

- See what sessions they have open across devices and browsers,
- Revoke a specific session other than the one driving the current request,
- Bulk-terminate all their sessions in one action.

This story adds the self-service session-management surface on top of the MVP. Admin / operator force-revoke of another user's sessions is **not** part of this story.

### Dependencies

- Depends on the OIDC MVP being merged: the Redis session model, the cookie-based authentication path, the audit event pipeline, and Hydra's token revocation endpoint must all be in place.

## Acceptance criteria

### Server (`alkemio-server`, OIDC module)

#### Listing

- [ ] Should expose `GET /api/auth/oidc/sessions` returning the caller's active sessions, filtered to those whose stored identity matches the caller. Response shape per item: `{ session_id, created_at, absolute_expires_at, last_active_at, user_agent, ip_hash, is_current }`. The response **MUST NOT** include any token material (access, refresh, or id tokens).
- [ ] Should add a per-user Redis set index that enumerates a user's active session ids in O(k), populated at OIDC callback success and pruned on every teardown path (logout, refresh-failure teardown, absolute-TTL breach, and the new revoke endpoints). The set's TTL is rolled to the latest member's absolute expiry.

#### Per-session revoke

- [ ] Should expose `DELETE /api/auth/oidc/sessions/:session_id` that:
  - [ ] Authenticates via the existing cookie path and returns `401` for unauthenticated callers.
  - [ ] Loads the target Redis record, verifies its stored identity equals the caller's; returns `403` otherwise — users may only revoke their own sessions.
  - [ ] Deletes the Redis session key, deletes any associated refresh-lock key, and removes the session id from the per-user index.
  - [ ] Calls Hydra's OAuth2 revocation endpoint for the session's refresh token to invalidate downstream RP refresh chains.
  - [ ] If the revoked session is the caller's *own current* session, clears the session cookie (`Max-Age=0`) and returns `204` so the SPA can redirect to the post-logout page; otherwise returns `204` with the caller's session untouched.
  - [ ] Emits exactly one audit event of type "session ended" with `outcome=success`, a `reason` value of `user_self_revoke`, the RP identifier of the web client, and an `initiator_sub` field equal to the caller's identity.

#### Bulk revoke ("sign out of all devices")

- [ ] Should expose `POST /api/auth/oidc/sessions/revoke-all` accepting a JSON body `{ "scope": "others" | "everywhere" }` (default `"others"` if omitted):
  - [ ] `scope=others` — revokes every session in the caller's per-user index **except** the current `session_id`. Caller stays signed in on this device.
  - [ ] `scope=everywhere` — revokes every session in the index **including** the current one; clears the session cookie; the SPA redirects through the post-logout page.
  - [ ] Authenticates via the cookie path and returns `401` for unauthenticated callers.
  - [ ] Iterates the per-user index and applies the same teardown as the per-session endpoint to each member (Redis key deletes + Hydra revocation for each session's refresh token).
  - [ ] Tolerates partial Hydra failures: continues teardown of remaining sessions, collects per-session outcomes, and responds with a multi-status body listing which sessions revoked cleanly (`207 Multi-Status` vs `200` with a result array — choose during refinement). Local Redis state MUST be cleared even when Hydra revoke fails for that particular session.
  - [ ] Emits **one** "session ended" audit event **per revoked session**, with `outcome=success|warn`, a `reason` value of `user_self_revoke_bulk_others` or `user_self_revoke_bulk_everywhere`, the web RP identifier, and `initiator_sub` equal to the caller's identity.
  - [ ] On success with `scope=everywhere`, returns `204` and the cleared cookie; on `scope=others`, returns the per-session summary body and the caller's session is preserved.

#### Cross-cutting server behaviour

- [ ] Should treat Redis unavailability consistently with the rest of the OIDC module: list endpoint returns `503` with `Retry-After: 5`; revoke endpoints return `503` and do not partially mutate.
- [ ] Should reject revoke attempts against a `session_id` that does not exist with `404`, and align the response shape between the "unknown" and "not yours" cases to avoid a minor existence info-leak (decide on the chosen shape during refinement).
- [ ] Should be covered by e2e tests in `test-suites` for: listing returns ≥1 session for an authenticated caller; revoking a non-current session by id; revoking the current session via the per-session endpoint; revoking someone else's session → `403`; revoking an unknown id → `404`; bulk revoke with `scope=others` from one of two sessions leaves the caller's current one alive; bulk revoke with `scope=everywhere` signs the caller out and revokes all peers; listing while Redis is down → `503`; bulk revoke where one Hydra revocation fails returns the per-session outcomes correctly.

### Web (`alkemio-client-web`)

- [ ] Should add a route under the account / security area (final path subject to design alignment) rendering a table of the user's active sessions sourced from `GET /api/auth/oidc/sessions`.
- [ ] Each row should show: a device / browser summary (parsed client-side from the user-agent string), an approximate location label derived from the IP hash (a non-geo placeholder is acceptable for v1), session created-at, last-active-at, and an explicit "this device" badge on the current session.
- [ ] Should provide a per-row "Revoke" action that calls `DELETE /api/auth/oidc/sessions/:id`, confirms via a modal, refreshes the list on success, and shows a toast on failure.
- [ ] Should provide two page-level actions:
  - [ ] **"Sign out of all other devices"** — calls `POST /api/auth/oidc/sessions/revoke-all` with `scope=others`, confirms via modal, refreshes the list on success.
  - [ ] **"Sign out everywhere"** — calls the same endpoint with `scope=everywhere`, confirms via a modal with a stronger warning ("you will be signed out on this device too"), then follows the standard logout redirect on success.
- [ ] Should redirect the user through the standard logout flow whenever they revoke their *own current* session (whether via per-row Revoke on the current row, or via "Sign out everywhere").
- [ ] Should surface partial-failure results from the bulk endpoint (e.g. a yellow toast: "3 of 4 sessions signed out; 1 could not be reached — please retry").
- [ ] Should be navigable from the existing account / security area of the user menu.

### Cross-cutting

- [ ] Audit events for the new surface MUST flow through the existing "session ended" audit pipeline. The only additions are the new `reason` enum values (`user_self_revoke`, `user_self_revoke_bulk_others`, `user_self_revoke_bulk_everywhere`) and the `initiator_sub` field.

## Additional Context

Deliberately **out of scope** for this story (still deferred, tracked separately):

- Admin / operator force-revoke of another user's session.
- Account-event cascade (deactivate / password-changed / admin-force-revoke) and the associated webhook → Hydra / Synapse fan-out.
- Per-RP / per-scope revoke (e.g. "sign me out of Synapse but keep me on the web client"). Bulk revoke here is all-sessions of the user, not all-RPs of one session.

Security note: align on a single response shape for both "unknown session id" and "not your session" during refinement, to avoid a minor info-leak.

## Areas that will be affected

_To be added during the refinement_
t: OIDC: session management UI — per-session revoke + sign out of all devices

## Description

As part of the OIDC migration ([parent #1692](https://github.com/alkem-io/server/issues/1692), and the in-flight `003-alkemio-oidc-idp` work), investigate whether OAuth 2.0 / OIDC **scopes** can be meaningfully mapped onto Alkemio's existing **credential-based authorization framework** — and whether doing so is desirable at all.

Alkemio today authorizes via `Credential` objects (e.g. `global-admin`, `space-member:{spaceID}`, `organization-admin:{orgID}`, etc.) attached to an `Agent`, evaluated against `AuthorizationPolicy` rules at every resolver/REST entry point. Scopes, by contrast, are coarse capability claims minted at token-issue time and carried on the access token.

The question is: do these two models compose, conflict, or operate on orthogonal axes?

## Why this matters now

- OIDC migration introduces machine-to-machine and delegated access patterns (bearer tokens, refresh re-resolution) where scopes are the OAuth-native authz primitive.
- `oidc-service` already implements FR-005 scope-gate behavior — we need clarity on what scopes *mean* in our ecosystem before we widen their use.
- FR-024a rejects bearer tokens without `alkemio_actor_id`, implying we still treat the credential set on the resolved actor as authoritative. Is the scope then redundant, additive, or constraining?

## Research questions

- [ ] What is the conceptual difference between a **scope** (issuer-asserted capability) and a **credential** (platform-asserted role/relationship) in our model?
- [ ] Can credentials be enumerated densely enough to fit in a token? (E.g. a user member of 200 spaces — does `space-member:*` scope make sense, or do we keep credentials server-side and use scopes only for *intent narrowing*?)
- [ ] Should scopes act as an **upper bound** on what credentials are evaluated for a request (deny-by-omission), or just as an **audit/intent signal**?
- [ ] How do third-party / external clients (future M2M, future SDK consumers) request and obtain scopes? Consent UI implications.
- [ ] What does refresh-token re-resolution (FR-006/006a) imply for scope stability across token lifetimes?
- [ ] Do any peer platforms (e.g. Auth0 RBAC + scopes, Keycloak roles + scopes, Ory Keto + Hydra) have an established pattern we can adopt rather than invent?
- [ ] Does it make sense at all, or are scopes better left as a thin OAuth-protocol detail (`openid profile email offline_access`) with all real authz remaining credential-driven?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Written analysis comparing scope and credential semantics in Alkemio's context
- [ ] Concrete recommendation: **map**, **layer**, or **keep separate** — with rationale
- [ ] If mapping/layering is recommended: sketch the canonical scope catalog and the credential-resolution rules per scope
- [ ] Identify breaking changes or follow-up tickets needed in `server` / `oidc-service` / `client-web`

## Out of scope

- Actual implementation of any mapping (this is a spike)
- Changes to the `Credential` data model
- Consent UI work (tracked separately under the OIDC migration)

## References

- Parent: alkem-io/alkemio#1692
- OIDC migration spec: `specs/003-alkemio-oidc-idp/` (in `oidc-migration` repo)
- Current authz framework: `src/services/authorization/` and `src/domain/agent/credential/`
t: Spike: Research OIDC scope → credential mapping for authz framework

## Description

As a developer of a backend service, scheduled job, or third-party integration that talks to Alkemio
I want to obtain an access token that authenticates my service itself (not a human user)
So that my service can call Alkemio's GraphQL API non-interactively, without depending on a person's login, refresh-token rotation, or continued employment.

## Context / Background

Today, every access token issued by Alkemio is bound to a human user identity. Non-interactive callers — data pipelines, scheduled jobs, third-party integrations, internal automation, ecosystem analytics tools — therefore have to pick one of two unsatisfying paths:

1. Have a real human log in once, capture the refresh token, store it in the service, and rotate it forever. If the human leaves the organisation the integration breaks. If the refresh chain dies (token expiry, idle period, revocation, password change) the integration breaks and needs a human to re-bootstrap.
2. Create a synthetic "service user" with a human-shaped account. Same fragility, and the audit log attributes service actions to a fake person.

Neither shape suits machine-to-machine traffic. OAuth2 already defines a dedicated grant for this case — `client_credentials` — where the access token represents the registered client itself. There is no user identity attached: `sub` is the client id, and the token is minted directly from the client's credentials at the token endpoint, with no browser flow, no user session, and no refresh-token chain to maintain.

Alkemio uses Ory Hydra as its OAuth2 authorization server, and Hydra natively supports `client_credentials`. What is missing is the supporting work on the Alkemio side: registering and managing service clients, mapping a client's identity to an authorization principal the server can reason about, validating bearer tokens that carry no user claim, and exposing that principal to the authorization framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Should allow access tokens to be issued via the `client_credentials` grant for clients explicitly registered as service clients.
- [ ] Should provide an admin-only registration surface for creating, listing, rotating credentials of, and revoking service clients. Each client carries a human-readable name, a description / owner, and a configured set of scopes and audiences.
- [ ] Should treat tokens issued via `client_credentials` as authenticating the **service** itself — `sub` is the client id and there is no user-identity claim. The server's authentication pipeline must accept these tokens and resolve them to a service principal rather than rejecting them for a missing user claim.
- [ ] Should expose the resolved service principal to the authorization framework so resolver-level checks can grant or deny access based on the service's identity and scopes, independently of any user identity.
- [ ] Should support per-service scope configuration so that a service client only receives a token bearing the scopes it was registered for, and the authorization framework honours those scopes when deciding which operations or fields the service can reach.
- [ ] Should record every action performed under a service token in audit logs with the service's client id as the actor (not a human user, not anonymous).
- [ ] Should provide credential rotation: an admin can issue a new secret for a service client and invalidate the previous one without disrupting other clients.
- [ ] Should provide revocation: an admin can disable a service client immediately, after which any subsequent token request, and any already-issued bearer presented to the server, are rejected.
- [ ] Should be covered by e2e tests in `test-suites` for: registering a service client; minting a token via `client_credentials`; calling GraphQL with that bearer and observing the service principal in the audit trail; scope enforcement (a client without scope X cannot reach operations gated on X); credential rotation; revocation takes effect for both new token requests and already-issued tokens; revoked / unregistered client_id returns the expected OAuth2 error.
- [ ] Should document, for service-client maintainers: how to register a client, how to request a token, how to call the API with the bearer, how to rotate credentials, and what scopes are available.

## Additional Context

Deliberately **out of scope** for this story:

- Self-service registration of service clients by end users. v1 is admin-only.
- User-bound long-lived tokens (a separate problem — this story is specifically about identity-less service tokens).
- A UI for service-client management beyond what the admin surface needs to be usable; full UX polish can follow.

Security considerations to settle during refinement:

- Default scopes for a freshly-registered service client (deny-all? read-only? admin-configurable per client?).
- Whether a service client may act across all spaces / organisations or whether it can be scoped to a subset.
- Token lifetime defaults for the `client_credentials` grant — shorter than user tokens, since there is no refresh path.
- Whether `client_credentials` tokens may invoke mutations or are read-only by default.
- Storage and display of the client secret at registration time (one-time reveal, hashed at rest).

## Description

As a logged-in user
I want to change the email I use to log in to Alkemio
So that I can switch authentication to a new mailbox I own, with the platform proving I control the new address before the change is committed.

## Context

This story tracks the **self-service** email-change path. It is a follow-up to umbrella issue #6064 (which originally framed both the admin-on-behalf and self-service paths together) and lands on top of the audit foundation introduced by spec 097.

- **Umbrella story**: #6064 — "Allow changing a user's login email while preserving their Alkemio profile"
- **Sibling (ships first)**: spec 097 — Platform Admin Change User Login Email (no verification). The admin-on-behalf path, where the admin verifies the subject's identity out-of-band. Replaces the manual DB-edit workaround that originally motivated #6064.
- **This story**: spec 098 — Self-Service Email Change. Introduces the **platform-mediated email-ownership verification** machinery that 097 deliberately omits, for the case where no admin is in the loop.

Spec lives on branch `098-self-service-email-change`; PR #6076 carries the spec artifacts.

## Why this is separate from #6064 / spec 097

The motivating incident on #6064 (platform admins resorting to direct DB edits during support flows) is fully addressed by 097 alone — coupling it to the verification machinery would have delayed the fix. The split lets 097 ship a smaller MVP first while preserving #6064's full scope across both stories.

## What this story delivers

- A user-initiated mutation `meUserEmailChangeBegin(newEmail)` that creates a short-lived pending row and emails a single-use confirmation token to the proposed new mailbox.
- A **session-less** root mutation `userEmailChangeConfirm(token)` that the user invokes from a client-web deep link (no Alkemio session required — the token is the sole authority). On valid token + uniqueness re-check, the platform commits the change synchronously across Alkemio and Kratos, inheriting 097's two-side commit + drift handling.
- A `me.pendingEmailChange` query so the user can observe the in-flight change (state, expiry, masked target address).
- A new entity `email_change_pending` tracking in-flight verification rows (states: `initiated`, `confirmed`, `committed`, `rolled_back`, `expired`, `superseded`, `drift_detected`; 30-day retention past terminal state).
- 7 additive values on the cross-category `platform_audit_outcome` enum (introduced by 097): `initiated`, `initiation_failed`, `confirmed`, `expired`, `superseded`, `rejected_used_token`, `rejected_expired_token`. Every state transition writes to the same `platform_audit_entry` audit log 097 introduces.
- Self-service `committed` outcomes inherit 097's three post-commit notifications (security signal to OLD address, acknowledgement to NEW address, global-admin fan-out) — with `initiatorRole = SELF` in the payload instead of `PLATFORM_ADMIN`.
- A new notification event `USER_EMAIL_CHANGE_CONFIRMATION` (sent to the proposed new mailbox at initiation time, carrying the confirmation deep link).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A logged-in user can invoke `meUserEmailChangeBegin(newEmail)` to start a self-service email change for their own account. Authorization: the caller's own account only (no admin path here — admin-on-behalf is 097's `adminUserEmailChange`).
- [ ] **Ownership of the new address is proven before the switch commits**: the platform sends a single-use, short-lived (≤1 h TTL) token to the proposed new mailbox. The change does NOT commit until the user clicks the confirmation deep link and the token is redeemed.
- [ ] `userEmailChangeConfirm(token)` is a **session-less root mutation** — no Alkemio session required. The token is the sole authority. This is so the user can confirm from a different device or browser than the one they initiated from.
- [ ] On confirm, the platform re-checks uniqueness (someone else may have claimed the address in the interim) and then commits across Alkemio + Kratos using 097's two-side atomic commit + bounded retry + drift handling. Inherits 097's three post-commit notifications.
- [ ] Tokens are: single-use (atomic consume-or-fail), short-lived, unique per pending row, and superseded by any new pending row for the same subject (`superseded` state on the prior row).
- [ ] `me.pendingEmailChange` returns the user's currently-active pending row (if any) — state, expiry, and a masked rendering of the target address. Returns null when no pending row exists.
- [ ] Distinct, deterministic error codes for the verification failure modes: `EMAIL_CHANGE_TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `EMAIL_CHANGE_TOKEN_USED`, `EMAIL_CHANGE_TOKEN_INVALID`, `EMAIL_CHANGE_MAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED`. All other error semantics inherited from 097's contract.
- [ ] Audit logging: every state transition (initiate / confirm / commit / rollback / expire / supersede / each rejection mode) writes a row to the same `platform_audit_entry` table 097 introduces, under `category = 'email_change'`. The drift-detection and drift-resolve paths from 097 work unchanged on self-service drift incidents (FR-009b-EXT extends the existing admin drift-resolve mutation's service-side behaviour to also transition the 098 pending row).
- [ ] Failure modes from 097 (Kratos unreachable, partial-failure rollback, drift detected, conflict, malformed) surface with the same error codes and audit outcomes 097 already establishes — 098 inherits them by reference and does NOT re-define them.
- [ ] GraphQL surface follows existing conventions: `me.pendingEmailChange` under `me`, `meUserEmailChangeBegin` under Mutation (`me`-shape input), `userEmailChangeConfirm` at root (no `me` / no `platformAdmin` — session-less by design).

## Out of scope (for this story)

- The admin-on-behalf path — covered by 097 / #6064 itself.
- Email change for credential types other than Kratos (this story inherits 097's "all credential types supported" guarantee — FR-002a).
- Bulk migration tooling.
- A client-web UI for the initiation entry point and the confirmation landing page (the spec covers the server contract; client-web work is tracked separately).
- Changing the user's display name, contact preferences, or any non-login email fields (097's out-of-scope list applies here too).

## Dependencies

- **Hard dependency on #6064 / spec 097 implementation landing first**. 098 reuses 097's `UserEmailChangeService` (`commitAcrossSides` helper), the `platform_audit_entry` table + cross-category Postgres enums, the bounded-retry helper, the email-masking utility, the three post-commit notifications, and the drift-detection / drift-resolve paths. Building 098 against a not-yet-merged 097 would force coordination overhead and risk drift between the two specs' service contracts.

## Areas affected

server (User domain, Kratos adapter via 097's `KratosService` extensions, GraphQL `me` + root mutations, mail/courier for the confirmation event, new `email_change_pending` entity + migration), client-web (initiation UI entry point + confirmation landing page — tracked separately).

## References

- Spec branch: `098-self-service-email-change`
- Spec PR: #6076
- Sibling spec / branch: `097-change-user-email` (#6066)
- Umbrella story: #6064
t: Self-service email change with platform-mediated ownership verification

b: ## Description As a logged-in Alkemio user viewing another member's public profile I want the "Resources Hosted" tab (Spaces, Virtual Contributors, Template Packs, Custom Homepages) to show the public resources that user's account hosts, or the ones I have access to see, So that I can discover what a contributor has created and made public - not just the spaces they happen to lead - instead of being told "No resources hosted yet" when they actually host public content. **Problem context** Today the account field on User is authorization-gated to the account owner (and platform admins). When viewer ≠ owner, `lookup.user(ID).account` returns `null`, so the client has no `account.id` to feed `AccountResourcesInfo`, and the tab renders its empty state. This is a pre-existing backend authorization behavior (the old MUI profile had the same gate) — not a frontend regression. The only public path to a user's hosted content today is `rolesUser`, which surfaces spaces via role membership but has no equivalent for VCs, template packs, or custom homepages. The fix must live in the backend: a non-owner needs a way to read the publicly visible subset of an account's hosted resources. ## Acceptance criteria **(TBD)** - [ ] A non-owner authenticated viewer can resolve a user's account identity sufficiently to query its hosted resources (e.g. `lookup.user(ID).account` is no longer hard-null for non-owners, OR a dedicated public field/query exposes the hosted-resources grouping). - [ ] For a non-owner viewer, the account's hosted Spaces are returned filtered to those the viewer is authorized to see (public / visible-to-the-viewer spaces only; private spaces excluded). - [ ] For a non-owner viewer, the account's hosted Virtual Contributors are returned filtered to those publicly listed / visible to the viewer; non-public VCs are excluded. - [ ] For a non-owner viewer, the account's hosted Template Packs (InnovationPacks) are returned filtered to those publicly listed / visible to the viewer. - [ ] For a non-owner viewer, the account's hosted Custom Homepages (InnovationHubs) are returned filtered to those publicly listed / visible to the viewer. - [ ] Sensitive account-level data (entitlements/licensing, storage usage, billing, anything currently owner-only beyond the resource lists) remains gated to the owner / platform admin and is NOT exposed to non-owners. - [ ] An owner viewing their own profile sees no change in behavior (all current sections still populate, including private resources). - [ ] An anonymous (unauthenticated) viewer's behavior is explicitly decided and implemented (either same public subset, or no access) — and documented. - [ ] When a user hosts zero publicly visible resources, the response distinguishes "genuinely none public" from "blocked" so the client can choose its copy appropriately. - [ ] GraphQL schema changes are reflected in schema.graphql and pass the schema contract; any breaking change to the account field's auth surface is flagged with CODEOWNER approval. - [ ] Authorization is enforced per-resource at the domain/authorization layer (not just by hiding fields in the resolver), so the same filtering holds across any query path that reaches these resources. ## Additional Context Looking at someone else's profile: - Frontend chain: useCrdUserProfilePageData.ts:14-19 → useUserAccountQuery (lookup.user(ID).account.id) → useAccountResources(accountId) (AccountResourcesInfo). When accountId is undefined, AccountResourcesInfo is skipped- confirmed in the network panel (UserAccount 200, no AccountResourcesInfo call). - Public reference path that already works: rolesUser(actorID) → "Leading" / "Member Of". The same 3 spaces appear there because a top-level space host is automatically its Lead/Admin. This is why "Spaces" is partially recoverable via roles, but VCs / packs / homepages have no public role-based equivalent — they require this backend change to ever be visible to non-owners. - Decision needed during refinement: extend the existing account field's authorization to return a filtered public view, or introduce a dedicated public field/query (e.g. a publicResources projection) so the owner-only account semantics stay intact. Recommend the latter to avoid weakening existing owner-only guarantees. ## Areas that will be affected _To be added during the refinement_
t: Profile: My Resources Hosted not visible for others

## Description
As a Signalen community member arriving at a Subspace via a shared link
I want to apply to the Subspace directly and be added to the parent Space automatically
So that I can register for the Community event without the friction of a separate Space sign-up step

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Should let a user start with the Subspace application as their entry point
- [x] Should automatically add the user to the parent Space under the hood, without a separate sign-up step
- [x] Should only be possible when the parent Space is public (otherwise users have no permission to see the Subspace without first being a member of the parent Space)
- [x] Should only enable this flow when the parent Space setting "allow subspace admins to invite to space" is turned on
- [x] Should update the text of that setting to reflect that it now covers applications as well, not just invitations
- [x] Should manage the user's application within the Subspace context (visible in the Subspace community settings, not the Space)
- [x] Should present the Subspace application questions as part of this flow
- [ ] Should work when the user arrives via a direct link to the Subspace
- [x] Should reuse the existing "double invitation" logic where applicable, adapted for the application flow
- [x] Should correctly add the user in both the Space and the Subspace upon completion of the registration/application

## Additional Context
This is driven by the Signalen rollout: around 300 people will be directed (via Teams and likely email) to apply to a Subspace as registration for their Community event on October 7th. For almost all of them this is their first step into Alkemio, so the flow needs to be as smooth as possible. They are using the application flow, so sign-up includes answering a few questions.

The user's entry point is the Subspace application. Being added to the parent Space happens automatically under the hood; the user does not complete a separate Space sign-up. The application itself is managed within the Subspace context, so it appears in the Subspace community settings rather than the Space's. The current flow requires signing up for the (public) Space first before applying to the Subspace, which is unnecessarily painful.

This flow is only logically possible when the parent Space is public. If it is not, users do not have permission to see the Subspace at all without first being a member of the parent Space, so there is no entry point for the combined flow.

On top of that, the combined flow should only be available when the parent Space setting "allow subspace admins to invite to space" is enabled. Since this setting now governs applications as well as invitations, its descriptive text should be updated to reflect both.

Related: the "double invitation" logic already exists and may be adaptable here (note: this refers to the existing technical invitation feature, which is distinct from the outreach described above). This has been prioritised above the org invitations/associations work.

## Areas that will be affected
_To be added during the refinement_
t: Combined Subspace application and Space sign-up

## Summary

New **L0 spaces do not get a Contributors callout in the Community tab** on a clean DB (or any environment where the backfill migration ran before the L0 template existed). The Contributors-callout feature (workspace#008 / epic #1541) shipped the one-time backfill migration for *existing* spaces, but the **bootstrap L0 space content template was never updated**, so *newly created* spaces — which clone that template — have no Contributors callout.

- Feature PR: #6200 · Migration fix: #6212 · Spec: [agents-hq#24](https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/pull/24) (`specs/008-contributor-collection-callout`) · Client story: alkem-io/client-web#9928 · Epic: #1541

## Expected behavior

On a clean DB, after running migrations and creating an L0 space, the space should have the default **Contributors** callout at the top of the **Community** tab (users + organizations + virtual contributors; default type USER; default view LIST) — matching what an existing/migrated environment shows and what the spec intends (the intentional reversal of the original FR-023 "new spaces get nothing" decision, per the migration docstring).

## Actual behavior

A newly created L0 space has **no** Contributors callout. Verified on a local `develop` stack:

- Migration `BackfillContributorsCalloutL0Community1782467322859` is recorded in `migrations_typeorm`.
- Yet `SELECT type, count(*) FROM callout_framing GROUP BY type;` → `none = 22`, **`contributors = 0`** (none exist anywhere).
- 3 L0 template content spaces + 2 L0 spaces exist, none with a contributors framing.
- New spaces created via the API have no Contributors region on Home or Community.

## Root cause

Two independent facts combine:

1. **The bootstrap L0 template has no Contributors callout.** In
   `src/core/bootstrap/platform-template-definitions/default-templates/bootstrap.template.space.content.space.l0.ts`,
   `collaborationData.calloutsSetData.calloutsData` contains **only the `welcome` callout** (Home flow state). The `Community` flow state exists but has **no callout defined**. New spaces clone this template, so they inherit no Contributors callout.

2. **The migration is a retrofit, not a new-space mechanism, and is order-sensitive.**
   `1782467322859-BackfillContributorsCalloutL0Community.ts` backfills L0 spaces *and* the L0 space content template that exist **at migration time**. On a clean DB, `migration:run` executes **before** bootstrap seeds the L0 template — so it backfills nothing. Then bootstrap creates the template (without the callout), and every subsequently created space clones a template that has none.

So the Contributors callout only ever appears in environments where the migration happened to run **after** the L0 template already existed (e.g. dev, where the record was removed and the fixed migration re-run + `authorizationPolicyResetAll`). Clean/fresh provisioning — including a from-scratch **ACC** — will not have it.

### Secondary issue (migration visibility)

The migration inserts callouts with **empty authorization policies** (it bypasses the service layer), so even when it *does* backfill, the callouts are invisible until a mandatory `authorizationPolicyResetAll` post-step is run (documented in the migration header). A server restart does **not** fix this — `BootstrapService.ensureAuthorizationsPopulated()` only resets platform + AI-server auth, and only when their rules are empty.

## Proposed fix

Update **both** paths (standard "migration for existing data + seed for new data" pattern):

1. **Add the Contributors callout to the bootstrap L0 template** so clean DBs / fresh ACC / prod get it via the normal service layer (correct auth, no reset needed, new spaces inherit it on clone). In `bootstrap.template.space.content.space.l0.ts`, add to `calloutsData`:

   ```ts
   {
     nameID: 'contributors',
     sortOrder: 1,
     classification: { tagsets: [{ name: TagsetReservedName.FLOW_STATE, tags: [FlowState.COMMUNITY] }] },
     framing: {
       type: CalloutFramingType.CONTRIBUTORS,
       profile: { displayName: 'Contributors', description: 'The contributors to this Space.' },
     },
     settings: {
       framing: {
         contributors: {
           contributorTypes: [ActorType.USER, ActorType.ORGANIZATION, ActorType.VIRTUAL_CONTRIBUTOR],
           defaultContributorType: ActorType.USER,
           defaultView: ContributorCollectionView.LIST,
         },
       },
     },
   },
   ```

   (The create DTOs already support this: `CreateCalloutFramingInput.type` + `CreateCalloutSettingsInput.framing.contributors` → `CreateCalloutContributorsSettingsInput`.)

2. Keep the migration for **already-deployed pre-feature spaces** only.

## Suggested regression test

A server-api test asserting that a freshly created L0 space has exactly one Contributors callout at the first position of the Community flow state (type `CONTRIBUTORS`, default types = all three, default view = LIST), so this can't regress.

## Impact / severity

- Any clean deployment (fresh ACC/PROD, local dev from scratch) → the headline feature (a self-updating contributor collection replacing the removed hard-coded community widget) is **silently missing** on all new spaces, so the Community tab has no contributor content at all.
- The current behavior depends on migration timing + a manual auth-reset post-step, which is not reproducible on clean provisioning.

## Environment

- Server `develop`; local hybrid docker-compose + k8s dev stack (`alkemio_dev_postgres`, DB `alkemio`).
t: L0 spaces created from bootstrap template have no Contributors callout on clean DB (Community tab)

   `collaborationData.calloutsSetData.calloutsData` contains **only the `welcome` callout** (Home flow state). The `Community` flow state exists but has **no callout defined**. New spaces clone this template, so they inherit no Contributors callout.

2. **The migration is a retrofit, not a new-space mechanism, and is order-sensitive.**
   `1782467322859-BackfillContributorsCalloutL0Community.ts` backfills L0 spaces *and* the L0 space content template that exist **at migration time**. On a clean DB, `migration:run` executes **before** bootstrap seeds the L0 template — so it backfills nothing. Then bootstrap creates the template (without the callout), and every subsequently created space clones a template that has none.

So the Contributors callout only ever appears in environments where the migration happened to run **after** the L0 template already existed (e.g. dev, where the record was removed and the fixed migration re-run + `authorizationPolicyResetAll`). Clean/fresh provisioning — including a from-scratch **ACC** — will not have it.

### Secondary issue (migration visibility)

The migration inserts callouts with **empty authorization policies** (it bypasses the service layer), so even when it *does* backfill, the callouts are invisible until a mandatory `authorizationPolicyResetAll` post-step is run (documented in the migration header). A server restart does **not** fix this — `BootstrapService.ensureAuthorizationsPopulated()` only resets platform + AI-server auth, and only when their rules are empty.

## Proposed fix

Update **both** paths (standard "migration for existing data + seed for new data" pattern):

1. **Add the Contributors callout to the bootstrap L0 template** so clean DBs / fresh ACC / prod get it via the normal service layer (correct auth, no reset needed, new spaces inherit it on clone). In `bootstrap.template.space.content.space.l0.ts`, add to `calloutsData`:

   ```ts
   {
     nameID: 'contributors',
     sortOrder: 1,
     classification: { tagsets: [{ name: TagsetReservedName.FLOW_STATE, tags: [FlowState.COMMUNITY] }] },
     framing: {
       type: CalloutFramingType.CONTRIBUTORS,
       profile: { displayName: 'Contributors', description: 'The contributors to this Space.' },
     },
     settings: {
       framing: {
         contributors: {
           contributorTypes: [ActorType.USER, ActorType.ORGANIZATION, ActorType.VIRTUAL_CONTRIBUTOR],
           defaultContributorType: ActorType.USER,
           defaultView: ContributorCollectionView.LIST,
         },
       },
     },
   },
   ```

   (The create DTOs already support this: `CreateCalloutFramingInput.type` + `CreateCalloutSettingsInput.framing.contributors` → `CreateCalloutContributorsSettingsInput`.)

2. Keep the migration for **already-deployed pre-feature spaces** only.

## Suggested regression test

A server-api test asserting that a freshly created L0 space has exactly one Contributors callout at the first position of the Community flow state (type `CONTRIBUTORS`, default types = all three, default view = LIST), so this can't regress.

## Impact / severity

- Any clean deployment (fresh ACC/PROD, local dev from scratch) → the headline feature (a self-updating contributor collection replacing the removed hard-coded community widget) is **silently missing** on all new spaces, so the Community tab has no contributor content at all.
- The current behavior depends on migration timing + a manual auth-reset post-step, which is not reproducible on clean provisioning.

## Environment

- Server `develop`; local hybrid docker-compose + k8s dev stack (`alkemio_dev_postgres`, DB `alkemio`).

## Summary

`ISearchCategoryResult.cursor` is non-null whenever a category returns **at least one** result, even when Elasticsearch has already returned everything it has. The client reads `!!cursor` as "there are more pages", so a single-result search renders a **"Load more"** button that fetches an empty page.

Found while re-testing office-document content search (server#6196 / client-web#9950), but the defect is generic — it affects every search category and predates that work.

## Reproduction

Search a term carried by exactly one document (`KRYPTOFERN`, unique to one file in the test corpus).

`GET /graphql` — one result, but a cursor:

```json
"framingResults": {
  "cursor": "15.845037::a3977951-413a-4945-8b0b-79e9e8449205",
  "results": [ { "type": "COLLABORA_DOCUMENT", "score": 15.845037, ... } ],
  "total": -1
}
```

The underlying `_msearch` shows Elasticsearch is exhausted — it was asked for 8 and returned 1:

```json
"hits": { "total": { "value": 1, "relation": "eq" }, "hits": [ { "_score": 15.845037, ... } ] }
```

The client then shows "Load more", because:

```ts
// client-web/src/main/crdPages/search/CrdSearchOverlay.tsx:170
setCanFramingLoadMore(!!data.search.framingResults?.cursor);
// :519
hasMore: filteredPosts.length > 0 && (visibleCounts.posts < filteredPosts.length || (allLocalShown && (canCalloutLoadMore || canFramingLoadMore)))
```

## Root cause

`calculateSearchCursor` returns a keyset cursor for any non-empty array. It has no notion of whether the page was full:

```ts
// src/services/api/search/util/calculate.search.cursor.ts:12-22
export const calculateSearchCursor = (array: Array<ISearchResult>): string | undefined => {
  const lastElement = array.at(-1);
  if (!lastElement) return undefined;
  return `${lastElement.score}::${lastElement.result.id}`;
};
```

Called unconditionally from `buildResults`:

```ts
// src/services/api/search/result/search.result.service.ts:1602-1604
const rankedAndLimited = resultsRanked.slice(0, filter?.size);
const cursor = calculateSearchCursor(rankedAndLimited);
```

Note the cursor's first segment is the **`_score` of the last hit** (a `search_after` sort value, per `sort: { _score: 'desc', id: 'desc' }`), not a count. `15.845037` is the relevance score of the single hit — it carries no information about remaining results.

## Why the naive fix is wrong

You cannot infer exhaustion from the *post-authorization* result count. The server deliberately over-fetches — `resultCount = Math.round(size * SIZE_MULTIPLIER)` with `SIZE_MULTIPLIER = 2` (`build.multi.search.request.items.ts:48`, `search.extract.service.ts:176`) — precisely because the query-time auth filter drops hits afterwards. A category that returns 1 result out of 8 ES hits may genuinely have more pages once the next page is authorized.

So `rankedAndLimited.length < filter.size` is **not** a sound exhaustion signal, and this is why the current code doesn't attempt one.

## The signal that *is* sound

The **pre-authorization ES hit count** for the category. If Elasticsearch returned fewer hits than `resultCount`, the index is exhausted and no subsequent page can exist, regardless of what authorization does to the results already in hand.

That count exists but is discarded. `processMultiSearchItem` maps `item.hits.hits` straight into `ISearchResult[]` (`search.extract.service.ts:449`), and `processMultiSearchResponses` flattens every category into one flat array — so by the time `buildResults` runs, both the per-category grouping and the raw hit count are gone.

## Proposed fix

1. Thread the per-category raw hit count (`item.hits.hits.length`) and the `resultCount` that was requested out of `SearchExtractService`.
2. In `buildResults`, return `cursor: undefined` when `esHitCount < requestedResultCount`.
3. Leave the client's `!!cursor` read as-is — it is a faithful implementation of the contract; the contract is what's broken.

Optional hardening: `hits.total.value` (with `track_total_hits`) would give an exact per-category total and could also close server#3700, but the cheap `hits.length < requested` check fixes the visible bug on its own.

## Related

- `total` is hardcoded `-1` for every category (`search.result.service.ts:1589`, `:1634`) — server#3700. Same family: pagination metadata the API doesn't currently expose. A UI cannot fall back to a count today.
- Surfaced during review of server#6196 and client-web#9950; tracking issue client-web#9881.
- Deliberately **not** in scope for those PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search whose category returns fewer ES hits than requested yields `cursor: null` for that category.
- [ ] "Load more" is not rendered for a single-result search (e.g. `KRYPTOFERN`).
- [ ] A search with a full page still returns a cursor and pages correctly, with no duplicates or dropped results across pages.
- [ ] Authorization-filtered results still page correctly: a full ES page reduced to few authorized results must still offer the next page.
t: Search: cursor is non-null when Elasticsearch is exhausted, so 'Load more' shows for a single result

## Summary

Subspace/community setup creates Matrix rooms **sequentially**, each taking **~1 second** via Synapse. When a setup path creates several rooms in series, the total server-side latency crosses 5 seconds, which is slow for real users and breaks the nightly test suite (the client aborts at ~5s — see alkem-io/test-suites#563).

## Evidence (k8s-hetzner-test, server logs, 2026-07-11)

Consecutive `communication.room.create` calls (`type: "direct"`, 2 initial members) run back-to-back, ~1s each, no overlap:

```
room.create-41  13:00:34.524 → 35.577  = 1053ms
room.create-29  13:00:36.533 → 37.610  = 1077ms
room.create-43  13:00:38.606 → 39.684  = 1078ms
room.create-19  13:00:40.674 → 41.732  = 1058ms
```

Contrast: Matrix member-*adds* are fast (~0.2s). It is specifically **room creation** that costs ~1s (Synapse room + state), and the calls are serialized, so N rooms ≈ N seconds.

Confirmed via Traefik access log that the corresponding GraphQL mutations were still in-flight on the server at 5002ms (HTTP 499, upstream `:4000` not yet responded) — i.e. the server, not a proxy, is holding the request open while it serially creates rooms.

## Impact

- **Real users:** subspace/space creation (and any flow spawning multiple rooms) is unnecessarily slow, scaling linearly with room count.
- **CI:** nightly `journey/subspace/*`, `journey/subsubspace/*`, and `entitlements/*` files fail as the test client aborts at ~5s (test-suites#563). ~8 files affected per run.

## Candidate locations

- `src/domain/communication/room/room.service.ts` (`createRoom` → `communicationAdapter.createRoom`)
- `src/domain/communication/communication/communication.service.ts`
- `src/domain/communication/conversation/conversation.service.ts` (direct-room creation per membership)
- Whatever orchestrates per-member / per-callout room creation during subspace + community bootstrap (the serial `await createRoom(...)` sites).

`space.move.rooms.service.ts:106` already uses `Promise.all` for a similar batch — the creation-during-setup paths do not.

## Fix direction

1. **Parallelize** independent room creations during subspace/community setup (`Promise.all` / bounded concurrency), rather than `await`-in-series. Individually ~1s rooms then overlap instead of summing.
2. **Or decouple** room materialization from the synchronous mutation — create rooms via an async job/event after the entity is persisted, so the GraphQL response doesn't block on Synapse. (Rooms already arrive via events; the mutation need not await all of them.)
3. Consider whether every membership needs an eager direct room at creation time, or if it can be lazily created on first use.

Prefer (1) as the low-risk first step; (2) is the durable win.

## Refs
- Discovered while root-causing test-suites#563 (the 5s client-abort / socket-hang-up nightly failures).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
t: Subspace/community setup creates Matrix rooms sequentially (~1s each) — parallelize or make async

**Release 67** · server slice of the continuous file-backup feature.
Parent story: [alkem-io/alkemio#1983](https://github.com/alkem-io/alkemio/issues/1983) · Spec: `workspace#008-continuous-file-backup` · DR epic: alkem-io/infrastructure-operations#2351

## What ships

Server owns the alkemio-DB schema, so it owns the **outbox table** that the new `file-backup-service` consumes. This is DDL only — **server does not read or write the outbox at runtime** (file-service does the INSERT; file-backup-service does the claim/UPDATE).

| PR | Change |
|---|---|
| [#6239](https://github.com/alkem-io/server/pull/6239) | Migration `1783508955161-FileBackupOutbox.ts` — creates `file_backup_outbox` + indexes, and the NOLOGIN `filebackup_consumer` role with `SELECT, UPDATE` on the outbox + `SELECT` on `file` |
| [#6265](https://github.com/alkem-io/server/pull/6265) | Dev-quickstart image pin `file-backup-service` v0.0.2 → v0.0.4 (**local dev stack only** — no production surface) |

Both merged to `develop`. Neither is in `v0.157.0` (Release 66) — confirmed by ancestry; they ship with the **Release 67** server image.

## Release impact — low, and deliberately unlike R66

- **Purely additive DDL.** New table + indexes. **No data backfill, and no `authorizationPolicyResetAll` required** — unlike the R66 migrations.
- **No app-code behaviour change.** No entity maps the table; no resolver, no service reads it.
- The `filebackup_consumer` role is created **NOLOGIN and password-free** — it is a privilege grant, not a credential. infra-ops attaches LOGIN + a password separately, so the migration stays self-contained and secret-free.
- Column names are **quoted camelCase** per the contract (TypeORM's snake_case default would break the consumer). The consumer's startup probe SELECTs every column, so any schema drift fails loudly at deploy rather than silently.
- `down()` drops the table — destructive only in the sense that a rollback discards queued outbox rows, which are a **replayable queue**, not source data. The objects themselves are never at risk.

Validated up → schema → down on PG16 via `.scripts/migrations/run_validate_migration.sh`; ships through the existing `server-migration` cron.

## Deploy ordering

The table **must exist before** the file-service producer flag flips (alkem-io/file-service#56) and before `file-backup-service` starts. Server therefore **leads** this feature's rollout — which it does naturally, since the migration ships in the server image.
t: [008] Backup outbox: file_backup_outbox table + scoped consumer role

A whole-day event is a **bare calendar date** ("all day on 3 December") — no time, no timezone. Production runs UTC (Alpine default, no `TZ`); the fix was validated on the dev stack pinned to `Europe/Amsterdam` ("works on my machine") and is **still broken on dev/acceptance**. It did not close server#6267. ## The fix One invariant across **server** + **client-web**: > A whole-day event's start is **UTC-midnight of the intended date**; all whole-day date math is in **UTC**, never re-projected through a local offset. - **client-web** — write as UTC-midnight (not local `startOfDay`); display as a local "floating" date so every viewer sees the right day; whole-day durations computed in UTC (DST-safe). - **server** — derive `DTSTART`/`DTEND` from **UTC** parts (keeps server#6271's exclusive end). - **Timed events unchanged** · **no schema/GraphQL change** · **fix-forward, no data migration** (existing events self-correct on next edit). ## Scope creep (added while testing): multi-day events highlighted too many days & whole-day events have no time-of-day ### 1) multi-day events highlighted too many days While reviewing the whole-day fix we found a related, pre-existing bug in the calendar / badge / batch-export display: a **multi-day event covered too many days**. **Describe the bug**

`authorizationPolicyResetAll` returns a `Task` id that can **never** reach `COMPLETED`, and the error path is inverted: a reset that *fails* gets marked `COMPLETED`, while one that *succeeds* stays `IN_PROGRESS` forever.

Any caller polling the returned task id as a completion signal will hang indefinitely. The task's `results[]` array does populate, so the reset itself works — it is only the `status` that is unreliable.

**Root cause**

`publishResetAll()` creates the task with **no** `itemsCount`:

```ts
// src/services/auth-reset/publisher/auth-reset.service.ts:27-28
public async publishResetAll(taskId?: string) {
  const task = taskId ? { id: taskId } : await this.taskService.create();   // <-- no itemsCount
```

`TaskService.create()` then leaves `itemsDone` undefined, because `&&` returns its falsy left operand:

```ts
// src/services/task/task.service.ts:68-77
public async create(itemsCount?: number) {
  ...
  itemsCount,
  itemsDone: itemsCount && 0,   // undefined && 0  ===  undefined  (not 0)
```

With both fields `undefined`, the two update paths disagree:

```ts
// task.service.ts:101-106  (updateTaskResults) — success never completes
if (task.itemsDone !== undefined && completeItem) task.itemsDone += 1;   // never runs
if (task.itemsCount && task.itemsCount === task.itemsDone)               // itemsCount falsy
    task.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED;                                  // unreachable

// task.service.ts:123-128  (updateTaskErrors) — error DOES complete
if (task.itemsDone !== undefined && completeItem) task.itemsDone += 1;   // never runs
if (task.itemsCount === task.itemsDone)                                  // undefined === undefined → TRUE
    task.status = TaskStatus.COMPLETED;                                  // fires on first error
```

`updateTaskErrors` omits the truthiness guard that `updateTaskResults` has. That single difference is what inverts success and failure.

Note also that the sibling publishers (`publishAuthorizationResetAllAccounts` etc.) *do* call `create(accounts.length)` when invoked standalone — so they behave correctly on their own. Only the `publishResetAll` aggregate path, which creates one countless task and passes its id down to all of them, is broken.

**To Reproduce**

1. Run `mutation { authorizationPolicyResetAll }` as an actor holding `AUTHORIZATION_RESET`.
2. Poll `{ task(id: "<returned id>") { status itemsCount itemsDone results } }`.
3. `results[]` grows and the reset completes in the logs, but `status` stays `IN_PROGRESS` and `itemsCount`/`itemsDone` are both `null` — indefinitely.
4. For the inversion: cause any item to error, and observe `status` flip to `COMPLETED`.

**Expected behavior**

- A successful full reset ends as `COMPLETED`.
- A reset with failures ends as `ERRORED` (or `COMPLETED` only once every item is accounted for), never `COMPLETED` on the first error.
- `itemsCount` / `itemsDone` reflect real progress so the task id is usable as a progress handle.

**Suggested fix**

- Have `publishResetAll` compute the total item count up front (accounts + organizations + users + licence resets) and pass it to `taskService.create(total)`.
- Fix `itemsDone: itemsCount && 0` → `itemsCount === undefined ? undefined : 0` (or default to `0`).
- Align the guard in `updateTaskErrors` with the one in `updateTaskResults` so an undefined-count task cannot complete on an error.

Any fix should touch **both** update paths — fixing only the success side leaves errors still completing early.

**Additional context**

- Pre-existing, **not** a regression: the guard dates to `5ec9592ed` (2024-06-10). `src/services/task/` and `src/services/auth-reset/` are untouched by the in-flight spec 027 branch.
- Found while running an authorization reset during live verification of `workspace#027-platform-role-redesign`; filed separately because it is unrelated to that feature and should not ride its PR.
- Operator-facing impact: several migration doc-comments in this repo instruct operators to run `authorizationPolicyResetAll` after migrating. Those operators have no reliable way to tell when it has finished.
t: BUG: authorizationPolicyResetAll task never reaches COMPLETED; error path inverts it

**Describe the bug**

**When a user is deleted, their OIDC (BFF) session — and the upstream Kratos SSO session — are not revoked/deleted.** The session outlives the user, so the browser keeps a *live, authenticated* session that no longer maps to any Actor/User. This orphaned session is the root cause; everything below is a downstream symptom of it.

Because the session is still valid:

- The BFF still reports the session as active (`/oidc` id-token-hint returns `200`), so `client-web` treats the person as logged in (`isAuthenticated = oidcActive`).
- The GraphQL `me` resolver runs against an actor context whose `actorID` is **empty**, so:
  - `query me { me { id } }` returns `{ "me": { "id": "me-" } }` — the id is built as `` `me-${actorContext.actorID}` `` (`src/services/api/me/me.resolver.fields.ts:75`); an empty suffix means no actor.
  - `me.user` is `null`.
  - Every user-scoped `me` field then throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` ("… as no userID provided"): `unreadNotificationsCount` (`:61`), invitations (`:110` / `:135`), **`communityApplications` (`:161`)**, conversations (`:223`). The originally-reported error (`Unable to retrieve applications as no userID provided`) is one instance of this.

Net effect: the deleted user's browser is stuck in a broken "logged-in but no account" state until they manually clear cookies.

**To Reproduce**

1. Log in as a user; keep the browser session (`alkemio_session` cookie + live BFF OIDC session).
2. **Delete that user** (admin deletion / GDPR removal / DB removal) — without terminating their sessions.
3. Reload the app. The BFF id-token-hint probe still returns `200`, so the client shows *authenticated*.
4. Run `query me { me { id } }` → `{ "me": { "id": "me-" } }` (empty actor). Any user-scoped `me` field (e.g. `UserPendingMemberships` → `me.communityApplications`) throws `BAD_USER_INPUT`, and the `me` payload nulls out.

(Locally this is trivially reproduced by reseeding/restarting the DB while holding a session — same orphaned-session state at smaller scale.)

**Expected behavior**

**Deleting a user must terminate/revoke that user's sessions** — the BFF OIDC session and the Kratos SSO session (and any refresh/consent grants) — so no live authenticated session can survive without a backing Actor/User. After deletion, the next request should be treated as **unauthenticated** (clean anonymous / `401`), and the client should render logged-out.

Secondary hardening (defense in depth, so a stray orphaned session degrades instead of crashing): the `me` sub-resolvers should return their empty value (`[]` / `null` / `0`) for a session with no `actorID`, rather than throwing `BAD_USER_INPUT`.

**Where this can happen (beyond local dev)**

- **Prod:** any account **deletion/deactivation** while the user still holds a live session → orphaned authenticated session, broken UI for that person.
- **Staging:** DB refreshes/restores while testers hold live sessions (same state at scale).
- **Local:** DB reseed/restart with a live session — the easy repro.

**Additional context**

- Two-session model in `client-web`: Kratos SSO (`useWhoami`) + BFF OIDC (`useOidcSessionStatus`, id-token-hint). `isAuthenticated = oidcActive` (client-web#9965), so a live OIDC session alone reads as "logged in" regardless of whether an Actor/User exists.
- Root-cause fix belongs to **user deletion → session revocation** (oidc-service / kratos-webhooks / server delete flow). A complementary `client-web` hardening (detect authenticated-but-empty `me` → force re-auth / clear state) is worth a separate follow-up, but this issue tracks the server/session-lifecycle cause.
- Observed with `server` on `develop`.

**Areas that will be affected as part of the fix**

The user-deletion flow and its session/grant teardown (OIDC/Hydra sessions, Kratos SSO session, refresh/consent grants); secondarily the `me` sub-resolvers in `src/services/api/me/`.


---

## Root cause analysis (added after code investigation)

The empty-`me` state traces to an **identity-key swap that leaves active sessions unresolvable until re-login**, not to a single deletion:

1. **Identity key changed.** `1764590889000-userIdentityCleanup` (~Jan 2026) dropped `user.accountUpn` (which held the email) and added a **nullable `user.authenticationID`** (the Kratos identity UUID). Its `up()` **does not backfill** `authenticationID` — and it *can't* in pure SQL, because the Kratos identity UUID is not derivable from the old email-based `accountUpn`.
2. **Auth resolves by that key.** A request/session is mapped to a user via `getUserByAuthenticationID(...)` (`src/core/actor-context/actor.context.service.ts`, `src/domain/community/user-identity/user.identity.service.ts`). A user whose `authenticationID` is `NULL` is unresolvable → empty `actorContext.actorID` → `me.id = "me-"` and every user-scoped `me` field throws.
3. **Re-link is lazy, login-only.** The backfill happens on the login handshake: `resolveByAuthenticationId` misses on `authenticationID` → fetches the Kratos identity → **looks the user up by email → sets `authenticationID`** (`user.identity.service.ts:168–174`, `linkAuthenticationId`). The **per-request actor-context resolution does the quick `authenticationID` lookup only — no email fallback.**
4. **Consequence:** any session **held across the migration** (or against a DB migrated after the session was minted) keeps presenting a Kratos id whose user still has `authenticationID = NULL`. It never self-heals during normal use — only a fresh login re-links it. That is the "authenticated but `me` is empty / logged-out-but-not" state.

Note: `1771000002000-MigrateUserToActor` (PR #5856) is **correct and not the cause** — it preserves `user.id` as `actor.id` and keeps the `user` table; it does not delete users.

### Suggested fix scope

- **Revoke/expire sessions when the backing user record changes** (deletion, or an identity-key migration) so a session can never outlive a resolvable user — the core of this issue.
- **And/or backfill `authenticationID` at migrate time** via a Kratos lookup (email → identity id) so already-active sessions resolve without requiring a manual re-login.
- **Defense in depth:** either give the per-request actor-context resolution the same email fallback used at login, or have the `me` sub-resolvers return empty (`[]`/`null`/`0`) instead of throwing when `actorID` is absent.

### No self-service recovery — the user is trapped

There is **no in-app way out of this state: logout is also broken.** The logout flow depends on a resolvable session/user too, so a user in the empty-`me` state cannot log out, cannot reach a clean state, and cannot re-authenticate to trigger the email re-link. This is why session revocation must happen **server-side** — the client cannot self-recover. It raises the severity: an affected user is fully locked out (broken UI *and* no working logout) until their session is cleared for them (or, on a machine you control, by manually wiping cookies / the Kratos + Hydra session).
t: BUG: Deleting a user does NOT revoke their session (their session stays active BUT cannot login)

Follow-on to #4764 (*Proper design of platform level roles*, delivered as workspace spec `027-platform-role-redesign`).

## Description

As a **platform operator**
I want **to grant a platform role for a bounded period, after which it lapses on its own**
So that **elevated access ends when the work does, instead of accumulating until someone remembers to revoke it**

#4764 decomposes Global Admin into 13 single-purpose global roles. Every one of them is still **granted indefinitely**: once assigned, a role is held until a human revokes it. For roles that exist precisely to be *narrow* — Platform Support, Platform Content Full Access, Platform Resource Admin — an indefinite grant quietly rebuilds the standing privilege the decomposition was meant to remove. The common real-world need is a **lease**: "give me Content Full Access for the next 4 hours while I clean up this incident", expiring by itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Should **deny** an action whose only authorizing credential has an `expires` in the past — today it is granted
- [ ] Should apply the expiry **on the holder's next request**, with no authorization reset, re-login or cache flush (FR-031/SC-016, matching the guarantee grants and revokes already carry)
- [ ] Should write a `platform_role_assignment` audit row when a grant lapses, attributed to `system` (FR-018 — "no revoke without a record")
- [ ] Should make it **impossible for a lease to strand the platform** without a Platform Roles Admin (FR-013a); the chosen mechanism is a design decision, see *Open questions*
- [ ] Should treat a NULL `expires` as "never expires", leaving every existing credential row unaffected — additive, no backfill
- [ ] Should propagate expiry of an **organization-held** `feature-*` role to that organization's admins and owners on their next request, via the same path demotion uses (FR-002/FR-031)
- [ ] Should report, per environment, how many credentials already carry a past `expires` **before** enforcement is enabled — switching it on is retroactively revoking them
- [ ] Should express "reaches this surface, conditionally on time" in the FR-034 reachability derivation rather than silently widening it

## Additional Context

### The part that changes how this should be scoped

`Credential` **already has an `expires` column, and nothing enforces it.**

| | Where |
|---|---|
| Declared | `src/domain/actor/credential/credential.entity.ts` — `@Column({ type: 'timestamp', nullable: true }) expires?: Date;` |
| **Written** | `src/platform/licensing/credential-based/license-credential-issuer/license.issuer.service.ts:24-41` |
| **Exposed** on the API | `src/domain/actor/credential/credential.resolver.fields.ts:13` |
| **Read** for display | `src/domain/space/account/account.service.ts:496` |
| **Never consulted in authorization** | `src/core/authorization/authorization.service.ts:211-213` matches on `type` and `resourceID` only; `src/core/actor-context/actor.context.service.ts:160,194` loads credentials into the actor context without filtering |

**So an expired credential authorizes exactly as well as a live one.** There is a field named `expires`, visible through the GraphQL API, that carries no expiry semantics.

Two consequences:

1. This is **not greenfield** — it is finishing a half-built mechanism. Storage and API surface exist; enforcement, lifecycle and audit do not.
2. There is a **latent gap today, independent of this story**. Any credential the license issuer has already stamped with a past `expires` still authorizes. A dev database shows `3604` credential rows with `0` non-null `expires`, so the local blast radius is nil — **production and acceptance must be counted before enforcement is switched on**. That count is the first task, not an afterthought.

### Interactions with #4764 that will bite

Where a naive "add a TTL" breaks invariants #4764 spent fifteen clarification passes establishing.

**1. Lease expiry bypasses the assignment rule engine — including the lockout guard.**
`PlatformRoleAssignmentRulesService` enforces six rules on every grant/revoke, among them `last-roles-admin`: the platform must always retain at least one Platform Roles Admin (FR-013a), and a revoke that would remove the last one is rejected. **A lease simply expiring is a revoke that never passes through that engine.** If the last Platform Roles Admin holds their role on a lease, the platform locks itself out when the clock runs out — the exact failure FR-013a exists to prevent, arriving by a path it cannot see.

**2. FR-031 immediacy — expiry is time-based, revocation is event-based.**
FR-031/SC-016 require a grant or revoke to take effect on the operator's next request, asserted with no sleep by `immediacy.it-spec.ts` and `flows/org-inheritance-demotion.it-spec.ts`. Revocation achieves that by invalidating the actor-context cache *at the write*. Expiry has no write to hang that on, so a cached actor context can outlive the lease. Either the cache entry's TTL is bounded by the nearest credential expiry, or the filter is applied on read.

**3. FR-018 — "no revoke without a record".**
An expiry is a revoke and needs an audit row. Open: written at expiry time (needs a sweeper) or lazily on first denied use (cheap, but the trail then says "expired at first attempted use", which is not when it expired).

**4. Bootstrap re-seed.**
`grantSeededCredentials` (`src/core/bootstrap/bootstrap.service.ts`) re-grants seeded credentials on start — unconditionally for service accounts, break-glass-only for humans (FR-012, FR-013b). Whether a re-seed **renews** an expired lease or **respects** it must be stated; getting it wrong makes a seeded lease either immortal or a startup-time surprise.

**5. Organization-held Feature roles.**
FR-002/FR-031: an organization holding a `feature-*` role confers it on that organization's admins and owners. A leased organization grant must propagate its expiry to every inheriting user.

### Open questions

- **Which roles are leasable?** All 13, `Platform …` only, or per-role opt-in? Standing operational roles like `platform-spaces-reader` on a service account arguably never should be.
- **Who sets a lease, and who extends it?** Is extension a fresh grant or a distinct, separately-audited "renew"? May a holder extend their own — and does FR-015's self-assignment block apply?
- **Maximum length and default.** Is an unbounded lease just a permanent grant with extra steps?
- **Warning before expiry.** #4764 settled the comparable question with "queryable only, no alerting" (fourth clarification pass). The same answer probably applies, but silently losing incident-response access at hour 4 is a different risk profile.
- **How is the FR-013a lockout prevented?** Forbid leases on `platform-roles-admin`; refuse an expiry on the *last* holder's grant; or let the rule block expiry at evaluation time — which means an expired-but-still-authorizing credential plus a loud alarm.

### Scope boundary

**In:** expiry enforcement in authorization and actor-context loading; lease-aware grant/renew/revoke surface; audit rows for expiry; the rule-engine interaction above; the pre-enforcement count of already-expired credentials per environment.

**Out:** per-space and per-organization role leases (this stays global-role scoped, as #4764 does); approval workflows; anything requiring a new store — #4764's FR-018 volume assumption should hold.

### Sequencing

Depends on `027-platform-role-redesign` **Slice A** landing — the roles, the rule engine and the audit trail are prerequisites. It does **not** need Slice B, and is better started before it: Slice B removes the legacy broad grants, and the least pleasant moment to discover a lease can strand the last Platform Roles Admin is right after the fallback paths are deleted.

## Areas that will be affected

_To be added during the refinement_ — first indications: `core/authorization`, `core/actor-context`, `domain/actor/credential`, `platform/platform-role` (rule engine + audit), `core/bootstrap`.

---
