## What this is

The server's chat API does two different jobs today: managing conversations (create, add or remove members, rename) and relaying messages to and from Synapse. The browser will stop using the relay part. This task writes down which is which, adds the "is my room ready?" answer the new read path needs, counts how much the relay is still used, and plans its removal so nothing is deleted while something still calls it.

Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801. Needed before the read path (alkem-io/client-web#10158) can switch on for anyone.

## What changes

- An inventory of every GraphQL query, mutation, subscription and cache path that touches messages, and every caller (browser, tests, tools), each labelled: keep as control, keep as backend integration, replaced by the browser, or later. A contract test keeps the list honest.
- Room readiness: a conversation's room reports `READY`, `PENDING` or a named failure; members can call `repairConversationRoom`; direct conversations can be resolved without the server sending a message on the user's behalf. This is the fix path for "chat created but missing room" (alkem-io/alkemio#2015).
- A control-plane event stream that carries governance outcomes (room ready, member added) but never message content, so a migrated browser has exactly one source of messages: Synapse.
- Usage counters on every relay operation, by caller kind (the browser declares its transport in a header), exported daily. This is the data for the "zero relay use for 14 days" gate.
- The #1946 attachment surfaces are marked "keep" so they are not deleted with the text relay.
- A test that the server never holds or hands out a Matrix credential.
- The removal itself, modelled now as a final wave with dates and code-owner approval, executed only after the 14 clean days.

## Done when

- [ ] The inventory names every surface and every caller before anything is removed.
- [ ] After cutover the browser uses GraphQL only for control actions, non-chat data, and the documented attachment operations.
- [ ] Room readiness and partial-failure recovery are unambiguous in the API.
- [ ] Schema changes follow the deprecation policy and break no other caller.
- [ ] Zero relay traffic from migrated browsers for 14 consecutive production days before removal starts.
- [ ] The server's remaining responsibilities stay documented after removal.
- [ ] Metrics tell the intentional attachment path apart from obsolete text traffic.

## Depends on

Removal waits for rollout evidence; the inventory and readiness work start now. Until alkem-io/matrix-adapter#69 lands, a removed member still keeps read access (#6329 cause 2).

## Read more

Spec: https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/064-conversation-control-contracts/specs/064-conversation-control-contracts

## What this is

When the browser sends messages straight to Synapse, the Alkemio server no longer sees them at send time. Emails, audit entries and other backend reactions must still happen, exactly once. This task proves that the existing path (Synapse → adapter → server) already handles this for messages sent from Element, hardens the few places it can lose or duplicate an event, and records what the notifications service and the PWA push work need.

Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801. This is the brake on gate 7: no write cohort may grow until this passes.

## What changes

- A trace table: for each event kind (message, reply, edit, deletion, reaction, receipt, membership change, media) which consumer needs it, today's path, the direct path, and the verdict.
- One dedupe marker at the server's front door, `msg:inbound:dedupe:{kind}:{eventId}` in the messaging Redis for 24 hours, so retries and redeliveries never notify twice; all nine downstream consumers inherit it.
- Adapter hardening: report "not ready" until Synapse, the bot and the queue are up (so Synapse holds and retries instead of dropping); confirm and retry queue publishes; hold timeline events briefly during a room repair; reject edits from a different sender; fix a wrong "retry forever" flag.
- Delete dead code: a receipt fan-out nothing consumed; three implicit "is the sender the assistant?" checks replaced by one guard.
- No Matrix room event is redelivered to a migrated browser through GraphQL.
- Notifications repository: assessed, verdict "no change needed" (it is an email-only consumer; the server already provides what it needs).
- PWA push (alkem-io/client-web#9501): the server-side integration point is documented; nothing new is emitted.

## Done when

- [ ] Events from web and from Element reach every required consumer exactly once, under retry and reconnect.
- [ ] Notification eligibility and counts are identical for direct and group chats, active and background tabs, offline users.
- [ ] Removed members get no later notification after the measured window.
- [ ] Browser sync and backend processing are observably separate: no loops, no double notifications.
- [ ] Consumers, dedupe keys and deliberately unsupported event types are documented.
- [ ] No change to the notifications repository unless the assessment proves one is required (it did not).

## Known trade-off

The marker fails open: if Redis is down or Synapse retries more than 24 hours later, a duplicate notification is possible. Accepted over the alternative of losing events.

## Depends on

alkem-io/matrix-adapter#69's event bridge and #6378's inventory.

## Read more

Spec: https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/066-matrix-event-continuity/specs/066-matrix-event-continuity

**Describe the bug**

Downloading a Collabora document via `File → Download → PDF Document (.pdf)` ends the editing session. The Kit process handling the document dies mid-export, the editor disconnects showing **"The collaboration session was closed"** with **"A service is temporarily unavailable"** in the status bar, and the document has to be reopened.

Scope notes:
- **Not specific to PDF source documents** — reproduced on a `.xlsx` spreadsheet.
- **Print is not affected** and works normally.
- **The document is not damaged** — reopening works, no content lost.

Surfaced while putting #6254 (Add PDF) through QA, but it is not caused by the PDF work.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open a space with a Collabora document contribution (any type — reproduced on `.xlsx`)
2. Open the document in the embedded Collabora viewer
3. `File → Download → PDF Document (.pdf)`
4. The editor disconnects and reports that the collaboration session was closed

**Expected behavior**

The document downloads as a PDF and the editing session continues uninterrupted.

**Desktop**

- OS: macOS
- Browser: Chrome
- Collabora: `collabora/code:26.04.2.4.1` (local dev stack)

**Additional context**

Investigated 2026-08-19. Collabora's log at the moment of the click:

```
ERR Exception: filesystem error: cannot create directory: No such file or directory [/tmp/user/docs//<hash>]
WRN DocBroker got disconnected from its Kit unexpectedly. Closing
ERR Cannot save because CanSave::NoKit though NeedToSave::Maybe. May have data loss, but must stop
```

The stack runs Collabora with `--o:security.capabilities=false`, which disables the chroot-jail path. In that mode Collabora writes per-document temp dirs under `/tmp/user/docs`. `quickstart-services.yml` provisions a tmpfs for `/opt/cool/child-roots` but **nothing for `/tmp/user`**, so the `mkdir` fails with ENOENT and takes the Kit process down with it.

**Verified locally:** adding a tmpfs for that path removes the crash entirely — `cannot create directory` drops to zero occurrences, the session survives, and the failure degrades into an ordinary in-app error dialog. One detail is still outstanding: with the mount at `/tmp/user/docs`, Collabora then reports `Access to /tmp/user/docs/<hash> was denied` (it runs as UID 1001, and Docker creates the mountpoint's parent as root-owned `0755`). Mounting `/tmp/user` itself at `mode=1777` is the obvious next step and has not yet been tested.

**Ruled out:** the `wopi-service` `DownloadAsPostMessage=true` approach (branch `fix/collabora-download-as-pdf`). Verified by calling CheckFileInfo directly with a live token that the flag *is* served and postMessage *is* working, but Collabora 26.04.2.4.1 never emits a `Download_As` message and still runs the export itself. That branch does not fix this.

**Areas that will be affected as part of the fix**

Container / deployment configuration rather than application code — `server/quickstart-services.yml` for local dev, plus the equivalent Collabora configuration in `dev-orchestration` and `infrastructure-operations`, which run the same `capabilities=false` setting.

Related: #6254
t: BUG: Download As → PDF ends the Collabora editing session

## Summary

`SearchIngestService.ingestFromScratch` (the full search re-index) has **no in-progress admission guard** and is started **fire-and-forget** from two entry points. Two overlapping full rebuilds can race, and in the worst case search **silently serves a stale index while the newer, complete index is deleted**. A separate throw-ordering bug can also leave the re-index task stuck `IN_PROGRESS` forever.

This is generic search-rebuild concurrency — **not** related to the collab/Yjs work. It was found while reviewing the `006-collab-content-unification` branch but predates it and affects **every indexed entity**.

## Where

- `src/services/api/search/ingest/search.ingest.service.ts` → `ingestFromScratch(task)` (generates a `YYYYMMDDHHmmss` suffix via `generateSuffix()`, creates suffixed indices, ingests, atomically flips aliases, deletes old indices).
- Started fire-and-forget from **two** entry points, no guard between them:
  - `src/platform-admin/services/search/admin.search.ingest.resolver.mutations.ts` → `void this.searchIngestService.ingestFromScratch(task)` (GraphQL, `PLATFORM_OPERATIONS_ADMIN`).
  - `src/services/api-rest/internal-admin/internal-admin.controller.ts` → `.ingestFromScratch(task).catch(...)` (unauthenticated **in-cluster** `POST /rest/internal/admin/search-ingest`, returns 202 for retry/poll automation).

## Failure modes

**(1) Different-suffix overlap — CORRECTNESS (the dangerous one).**
Run A starts first (`suffix_A`), reads the DB, begins ingesting, and stalls. Run B starts later (`suffix_B`), reads a *newer* DB state, finishes, and atomically flips the aliases to `suffix_B` (deleting the previously-active indices). Run A then finishes **last**, flips the aliases to `suffix_A` (the *older* data), and **deletes `suffix_B`'s indices** (treating B's active set as the old set to clean up). Result: search serves the **staler** rebuild and the **newer complete index is deleted**. No primary data loss (a later clean rebuild fixes it), but search silently serves stale results.

**(2) Same-second suffix collision — OPERATIONAL only.**
Two runs in the same second get the same suffix, try to create the same physical indices, and one/both hit `resource_already_exists` and abort **before** the alias flip. Result: errors + orphaned unaliased indices, but the active aliases usually stay on the old set (no active-index corruption).

**(3) Secondary bug — task leak.**
`generateSuffix()` runs **before** the `try` block, so a throw there leaves the task `IN_PROGRESS` forever. (Also: `TaskService.create` hardcodes `action: 'auth-reset'` for this reindex task — the `Task` abstraction is status storage, not an admission primitive.)

## Reachability

The overlap window is **minutes** (10 index families, paged, 500ms sleep per batch). A double invocation, an automation retry after a lost 202 response, a GraphQL + REST overlap, or a rollout are all enough. `replicas: 1` does **not** make a process-local guard sufficient — both entry points overlap in the same process today, and a Kubernetes `RollingUpdate` briefly runs old+new pods that the internal Service can route to.

## Priority

Medium-high (correctness/operations). No primary data loss, but a later-started successful rebuild can be silently replaced and deleted. **Fix before relying on automated reindex retries or scaling server replicas > 1.**

## Proposed fix

**Reject, do not queue** (a queued duplicate is expensive and may be obsolete):

1. One shared entry method both call sites use (`SearchIngestService.startFromScratch()`), which atomically claims a **global rebuild slot BEFORE task creation**, launches the run, and releases in `finally` after the task reaches a terminal state.
2. Cross-pod admission via a **PostgreSQL session advisory lock** (`pg_try_advisory_lock` on a dedicated TypeORM `QueryRunner`, namespaced by the Elasticsearch `indexPattern`); hold the connection for the whole run; `pg_advisory_unlock` + `QueryRunner.release()` in `finally`; process/connection death releases automatically. (Not a local mutex — cross-pod; not Redis — unbounded duration would need lease renewal.)
3. Busy → **409 / typed GraphQL conflict** ("search rebuild already running"); caller retries after the active job completes. GraphQL authorizes **before** calling start (avoid creating a task for an unauthorized request).
4. Use the **Task UUID** as the index suffix (optionally date-prefixed for readability), not second-resolution time — solves retry/orphan name collisions.
5. Move `generateSuffix()` and every failure path **inside** the run's `try/finally` so a throw can't leak `IN_PROGRESS`.
6. Hold the guard through create → ingest → alias promotion → old-index cleanup → task terminal state.

**Do not** add pointer-version / Yjs-specific plumbing (irrelevant), a generic distributed-lock framework, or a `getAll(IN_PROGRESS)`-then-create check (cross-pod check-then-act race).

## Tests

- Barrier test through the public start: A owns the guard and pauses; B is **rejected** and creates no task/index; release A; C is then admitted.
- Guard releases after success, ingest failure, task-creation failure, and detached-launch failure.
- Both entry points exercise the same public start and map busy correctly.
- Suffix uses distinct task ids (no clock mocking).

## Symptom

The server process **exits** when a forum-discussion-comment notification is built for a discussion that no longer exists. Observed on a local `develop`-based stack; the process dies and `nest start --watch` does not respawn it (it waits for a file change), so the API stays down until someone manually restarts.

```
EntityNotFoundException: Unable to find discussion with ID: <uuid>
    at new BaseException (src/common/exceptions/base.exception.ts:22:5)
    at new EntityNotFoundException (src/common/exceptions/entity.not.found.exception.ts:11:5)
    at UrlGeneratorService.getForumDiscussionUrlPath (src/services/infrastructure/url-generator/url.generator.service.ts:1203:13)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:105:5)
    at async NotificationExternalAdapter.buildPlatformForumCommentCreatedOnDiscussionPayload (src/services/adapters/notification-external-adapter/notification.external.adapter.ts:1001:7)
    at async NotificationPlatformAdapter.platformForumDiscussionComment (src/services/adapters/notification-adapter/notification.platform.adapter.ts:258:9)
```

## Root cause

`room.service.events.ts:205` invokes the notification adapter as a **floating promise** — no `await`, no `.catch()`:

```ts
this.notificationPlatformAdapter.platformForumDiscussionComment(
  forumDiscussionCommentNotificationInput
);
```

`getForumDiscussionUrlPath` legitimately throws `EntityNotFoundException` when the discussion row is gone. Because nothing handles the rejection, Node 22's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` terminates the process.

Note this is the **only** un-awaited notification call in that file — the other five are awaited. It reads as an oversight rather than a deliberate pattern.

## Why it matters

Any notification whose payload builder references a since-deleted entity can take the whole API down. It needs no privileged access to trigger: comment on a forum discussion, delete the discussion, let the notification drain. Availability impact is platform-wide, not scoped to the forum.

## Proposed fix

Keep it fire-and-forget (a notification failure must not fail the user's comment), but stop the rejection escaping — the same best-effort posture already used for `deleteUser`'s post-commit legs:

```ts
this.notificationPlatformAdapter
  .platformForumDiscussionComment(forumDiscussionCommentNotificationInput)
  .catch(error =>
    this.logger.error?.(
      `Failed to send forum discussion comment notification: ${error?.message}`,
      error?.stack,
      LogContext.NOTIFICATIONS
    )
  );
```

Awaiting it instead would also remove the crash, but would make a missing discussion fail the user's *comment* mutation — worse behaviour for a best-effort notification.

A regression test should assert that a rejecting notification adapter does not propagate out of `processNotificationForumDiscussionComment`.

## Related — not proposed here

There is **no** `unhandledRejection` or `uncaughtException` handler anywhere in `src/` (verified by grep). So this failure mode is not specific to forum notifications: *any* floating promise rejection anywhere in the server terminates the process. Deliberately not proposing a global catch-all here — one that logs and continues can leave the process in an undefined state and would mask exactly this class of bug — but the systemic exposure is worth a deliberate team decision.

## Repro

1. Comment on a platform forum discussion.
2. Delete that discussion before the notification is processed.
3. The notification drains; the server process exits with the trace above.

**Describe the bug**
Since the per-document whiteboard content storage rework (#6193, #6399), every whiteboard create writes its initial Yjs snapshot into the whiteboard's own storage bucket with **no authorization policy, by design** (`FileServiceAdapter.createSnapshotInBucket` deliberately omits `authorizationId` — "the snapshot is an INTERNAL infra blob … NOT tracked as a server-side `Document` entity").

However, that snapshot row **does** surface in the `StorageBucket.documents` GraphQL collection, and `StorageBucketService.getFilteredDocuments` → `hasAgentAccessToDocument` → `AuthorizationService.isAccessGrantedForCredentials` **throws** on the missing policy instead of filtering the row out. This poisons the entire `documents` field for any whiteboard profile — including buckets that also contain perfectly valid documents (e.g. an uploaded visual):

```
EntityNotInitializedException: Authorization: no definition provided
code: ENTITY_NOT_INITIALIZED, numericCode: 12108
path: ["lookup","callout","contributions",0,"whiteboard","profile","storageBucket","documents"]
    at AuthorizationService.isAccessGrantedForCredentials (src/core/authorization/authorization.service.ts:125)
    at StorageBucketService.hasAgentAccessToDocument (src/domain/storage/storage-bucket/storage.bucket.service.ts:563)
    at StorageBucketService.getFilteredDocuments (src/domain/storage/storage-bucket/storage.bucket.service.ts:531)
    at StorageBucketResolverFields.documents (src/domain/storage/storage-bucket/storage.bucket.resolver.fields.ts:57)
```

The error reproduces even on the `createContributionOnCallout` mutation response itself (path `createContributionOnCallout.whiteboard.profile.storageBucket.documents`), i.e. **after** `CalloutContributionAuthorizationService.applyAuthorizationPolicy` has run — the auth reset cannot help a row that is supposed to be invisible and has no policy to reset.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a whiteboard contribution on a whiteboard-collection callout (`createContributionOnCallout`), or any whiteboard via the new flow (`CreateWhiteboardInput` no longer takes `content`, so every create goes through the snapshot write in `WhiteboardService` phase 3 → `createSnapshotInBucket`).
2. Optionally upload an image on the whiteboard's CARD visual (a real, valid document in the same bucket).
3. Query `whiteboard.profile.storageBucket.documents` (any actor, including GLOBAL_ADMIN).
4. The whole `documents` field errors with 12108; the valid visual document is unreachable through the collection.

**Impact**
- QA server-api storage-auth suites: all whiteboard document-authorization scenarios fail (~36 tests per spec file in `storage/auth/*` — "Call for Whiteboards", "Whiteboard Callout", "WhiteboardRt Callout" blocks), first observed on the 2026-08-26 nightly after the local stack picked up #6399.
- Any client feature that lists a whiteboard profile's storage bucket documents will hit the same error.

**Expected behavior**
The internal snapshot blob never appears in `StorageBucket.documents` (matching the `createSnapshotInBucket` doc contract), or at minimum `getFilteredDocuments` treats a document without an authorization policy as not-readable and filters it instead of throwing, so the remaining documents still resolve.

**Relation to alkem-io/client-web#10210**
Sibling bug from the same rework, but a distinct defect needing a distinct fix. In client-web#10210 ("Importing a whiteboard template with visuals throws errors"), the failing documents are the media copies made by `rehomeSnapshotAssets` during `replaceWhiteboardContentFromSource`: `copyDocumentToBucket` → `persistDocumentWithPreparedAuth` pre-creates an **empty** authorization policy that only a later auth reset would populate with credential rules — and unlike `updateWhiteboard`, the `replaceWhiteboardContentFromSource` mutation never applies one. Result there: policy exists but has no rules → 11106 `AUTHORIZATION_INVALID_POLICY` on `lookup.document`.

So the shared invariant broken by the new copy/snapshot paths is "every GraphQL-visible document carries a populated authorization policy":
- client-web#10210: copied media docs → empty-rules policy → 11106 (fix: apply/copy credential rules after the re-home in `replaceContentFromSource`).
- this issue: snapshot blob → no policy at all, leaking into the documents collection → 12108 (fix: exclude snapshot rows from the collection, or filter policy-less rows gracefully).

Fixing one will not resolve the other.
t: BUG: whiteboard snapshot blob (NULL authz) leaks into StorageBucket.documents — 12108 ENTITY_NOT_INITIALIZED poisons the whole documents field

Found by adversarial review during `workspace#054-delete-own-account` (self-service account deletion). Recorded there as finding `sec-client-web-1`, **medium**, accepted for v1 — this issue tracks making it real.

## Summary

The privileged-session gate in front of self-service account deletion is a **session-age gate, not a re-authentication gate**. It does not verify that a human with credentials is present. Anyone holding a live authenticated browser can satisfy it with no credential prompt and irreversibly delete the account.

## Why

The server gates on `ActorContext.issuedAt`:

- `src/services/api/registration/registration.resolver.mutations.ts` — the gate tests only `Date.now() - actorContext.issuedAt > PRIVILEGED_SESSION_WINDOW_MS`.
- `src/core/auth/oidc/strategies/cookie-session.strategy.ts` — `issuedAt` is `payload.created_at * 1000`, i.e. the **BFF session record's creation time**.
- `src/core/auth/oidc/oidc.controller.ts` — the OIDC callback sets `s.created_at = now` **unconditionally on every callback**, inside `req.session.regenerate()`.

So "freshness" means *the session row is young*, not *the user recently proved who they are*. Any login round trip resets it, including one that required no credential.

## Abuse path

An actor has the victim's authenticated browser (unattended unlocked device, shared machine, or a stolen `alkemio_session` cookie) but **not** their password or passkey.

1. They navigate once to `/api/auth/oidc/login?returnTo=/`.
2. Hydra completes that round trip **silently** against the still-live Kratos SSO session. This repo documents that behaviour in two places independently of this feature — `client-web/src/core/auth/authentication/hooks/useOidcSessionRecovery.ts` ("Hydra completes it silently against that session, with no credential prompt") and the `useDeleteAccount` docblock added by the feature itself.
3. A new `alkemio_session` is issued with `created_at = now`.
4. They call `deleteUser` directly — or simply reopen the delete-account card, which now sees `sessionFresh: true` and skips re-authentication entirely.

The account and its Kratos identity are permanently destroyed, and the audit record cannot distinguish them from the legitimate owner.

Note the BFF **does** send `prompt: 'login'` to Hydra unconditionally (`oidc.controller.ts`). The exposure is that this is not honoured end to end by the login provider.

## Why the client-side mitigation is not sufficient

`client-web` ends the browser's Kratos SSO session (fail-closed) before redirecting to the BFF login route, which makes the prompt genuine **for a user going through the product UI**. That is worth keeping as UX hardening, but it is not a boundary: it only executes if the caller runs the application's own JavaScript. An actor who navigates directly is unaffected by it.

## Severity and framing

**Medium.** Two independent verifiers confirmed the mechanism and reachability; the impact assessor rated it medium rather than high because it requires possession of an already-authenticated browser.

**This is not a regression.** Before this feature, `deleteUser` was already self-callable with **no gate at all** — `USER_SELF_MANAGEMENT` grants `DELETE` and the resolver carries no admin-only guard. The feature strictly improves the position by adding a confirmation, a session-age gate and an audit trail. The problem is that the control **claims more than it delivers**.

## Remediation — two legs, both outside the feature that found it

1. **Identity-provider leg (`oidc-service`)** — honour `prompt=login` (and `max_age=0`) from the BFF authorization request instead of auto-accepting against the live Kratos SSO session. This also makes the client-side `endKratosSsoSession` step redundant rather than load-bearing.
2. **Server leg (this repo)** — derive `ActorContext.issuedAt` from the ID token's `auth_time`, and assert an `amr`/`acr` indicating an interactive credential method, rather than from the BFF session row's `created_at`. A silent session re-mint then cannot reset the window.

Until both land, the gate should be treated and described as a session-age gate only.

## Already done, so nobody re-derives it

- **`FR-024`/`FR-013` in `agents-hq/specs/054-delete-own-account/spec.md` have been amended** to state that this is a session-age gate and that it **MUST NOT** be described as re-authentication in an ADR, release notes, or the App Store / Play submission.
- The user-facing help page is **not** affected and needs no change: a real user going through the UI genuinely is prompted, because the client ends the Kratos SSO session first.
- Full analysis and the two verifier verdicts are in `agents-hq/specs/054-delete-own-account/forge-run.md`.

## Related

- Feature: `alkem-io/client-web#10107`, workspace spec `054-delete-own-account`
- `kratosService.getAuthenticatedAt` is a separate false control — it takes `MAX(authenticated_at)` across **all** of an identity's active sessions and returns `undefined` on error (fails open). Nothing in feature 054 depends on it, deliberately, but it must not be used as the fix for this issue.
- GDPR/Legal tracking for the same feature: alkem-io/alkemio#2103
t: Account-deletion step-up gate is a session-age gate, not re-authentication

## Problem

Template whiteboards are effectively **creator-only editable**. The template authorization chain (`TemplatesSet → Template → Whiteboard`) never grants `CONTRIBUTE` to space members or space admins, so under `contentUpdatePolicy=contributors` (the default) the privilege rule `CONTRIBUTE → UPDATE_CONTENT` fires for nobody except the creator (via the `whiteboard-created-by` rule).

**Concrete consequence:** if the user who created a whiteboard template becomes unavailable, no one — not even a space admin or global admin — can edit the template's drawing. The only remediation is delete-and-recreate.

## Evidence (dev stack, 2026-08-29, discovered during 006 lifecycle live verification)

Stored policy of a whiteboard-template WB (created via UI, policy untouched since creation — verified via `authorization_policy.updatedDate`):

| rule | credentials | privileges |
|---|---|---|
| credentialRuleTypes-platformGlobalAdmins | global-admin | create, read, update, delete, grant |
| credentialRuleTypes-spaceGlobalRead | global-spaces-read | read |
| credentialRule-spaceMembersRead | space-member | **read only** |
| credentialRule-spaceAdmins | space-admin, global-admin | create, read, update, delete, grant |
| whiteboard-created-by | user-self (creator) | update-content, contribute, delete |

Privilege rule `CONTRIBUTE → UPDATE_CONTENT` (contributors policy) exists but no non-creator credential carries `CONTRIBUTE`. A global admin was verified live to be read-only on the canvas while able to rename/delete.

## Code path

- `TemplateAuthorizationService.applyAuthorizationPolicy` (WHITEBOARD case) passes only `template.authorization` into `WhiteboardAuthorizationService.applyAuthorizationPolicy` — no `spaceSettings`/role-set, so no member/admin CONTRIBUTE rules are appended (contrast: live callout whiteboards inherit the base CONTRIBUTE rule via `CollaborationAuthorizationService.appendCredentialRulesForContributors` through Callout → Framing).
- Same applies to callout-template framing whiteboards/memos.
- Related: `Whiteboard/MemoResolverMutations` only re-apply authorization on `contentUpdatePolicy` change when the document is attached to a callout framing/contribution — a standalone template WB whose policy is changed later keeps stale rules.

## Proposed direction (initial lean, to be refined)

Grant `CONTRIBUTE`/`UPDATE_CONTENT` on template whiteboards to the space's admins (and possibly members, per `contentUpdatePolicy` semantics) — e.g. append the role-set-derived CONTRIBUTE rules in the template auth chain, or default template WBs to `ADMINS` content policy. Needs a deliberate authz decision + policy-reset/migration consideration for existing templates.

## Notes

- Not a regression of the 006 collaboration-lifecycle delivery — creation-time authz design, pre-existing.
- Discovered while root-causing an admin's read-only canvas during live parity verification.
t: Template whiteboards are creator-only editable — no CONTRIBUTE/UPDATE_CONTENT for space admins

## Problem

Whiteboard preview images are generated **client-side on dialog close** by every write-admitted user with edit mode — canvas render → visual upload → `updateWhiteboard` mutation — with no dirty check. Consequences:

- A board opened by N contributors "just to look" gets its preview regenerated and re-uploaded N times (redundant renders, uploads, mutations, `updatedDate` churn).
- The close path must talk to the server for a *clean* board, which produced a real UX defect (offline clean close trapped by the failing metadata call — fixed client-side as best-effort + zero-local-edits skip, but the architecture remains backwards).
- Preview freshness depends on the *last editor closing their dialog* — a board edited but never closed (tab killed, crash) keeps a stale preview indefinitely.

This is inherited from the legacy (pre-Yjs) design where close was also the content-save moment. Under the unified collaboration model (006), content persistence is server-owned (debounced flush to file-service), so close-time client preview generation is the only remaining reason a clean close performs server work.

## Proposal

Move preview generation **server-side, on content flush**: the server already owns headless scene conversion for whiteboards (006 `whiteboard.fork`/conversion utilities, headless `@excalidraw-yjs/excalidraw` usage). On (debounced) snapshot flush — or on a slower dedicated cadence — render the preview from the flushed content and update the whiteboard's visuals, removing the client close-time leg entirely for all users.

Benefits: one render per content change instead of per closing editor; previews stay fresh regardless of how sessions end; the client close path performs zero server work beyond the existing durability barrier; deletes a whole class of close-time failure modes.

Considerations: render cost/scheduling on the service or server side (cadence/debounce, size limits), parity of the rendered preview with the client-side render (fonts/assets), and removal/deprecation of the client upload path once server-side rendering ships.

## Context

- Interim client-side mitigations shipped separately: metadata/preview close leg made best-effort (cannot trap the dialog, per architecture E6/§6) and skipped entirely for sessions with zero local edits.
- Discovered while testing the 006 unified collaboration lifecycle delivery (2026-08-31).
t: Generate whiteboard preview images server-side on content flush (remove client close-time preview upload)

## Description

A **space member** does not see the **"Add post"** button, even though:

- the `createPost` widget is enabled on the tab layout, and
- the space collaboration settings have **"members can create posts" ON** (`settings.collaboration.allowMembersToCreateCallouts: true`).

Space admins see the button; plain members don't, so members cannot create posts despite the setting.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a space, enable the Create Post widget on a tab's layout and set collaboration settings → allow members to create posts = ON.
2. Open that tab as a plain space member (no admin role).

**Actual:** no "Add post" button (neither the sidebar widget nor the create flow).
**Expected:** the member sees the button and can create a post.

## Analysis — the client faithfully mirrors `myPrivileges`; the grant chain breaks server-side

Client-web was ruled out: every "Add post" surface is a direct mirror of the calloutsSet privileges, with no additional client-side gating —

- `useCalloutsSetAuthorization` (client): `canCreateCallout = lookup.calloutsSet.authorization.myPrivileges.includes(CREATE_CALLOUT)`;
- `CrdSpaceTabPage` passes it as `canCreatePost` to the sidebar (`createPost` widget renders iff the wire plan contains it AND `canCreatePost`), and gates the `CalloutFormConnector` on the same flag. The sidebar plan itself (`resolveSidebarPlan`) does no privilege filtering — it renders exactly the server-provided widget list.

So the member's `CalloutsSet.authorization.myPrivileges` evidently does **not** contain `CREATE_CALLOUT` even with the setting ON. The intended server chain exists:

- `callouts.set.service.authorization.ts` (`appendPrivilegeRules`): when `collaborationSettings.allowMembersToCreateCallouts` is true, a privilege rule maps `CONTRIBUTE` → `CREATE_CALLOUT` (`POLICY_RULE_CALLOUT_CONTRIBUTE`) on the calloutsSet policy.
- `updateSpaceSettings` (`space.resolver.mutations.ts`) triggers an authorization-policy reset for this settings change (`shouldUpdateAuthorizationPolicy` exempts only `collaboration.allowEventsFromSubspaces`).

Since both pieces exist, the failing link is one of:

1. the settings-triggered reset not cascading down to the **calloutsSet** policy (stale policy keeps serving the member's old `myPrivileges`);
2. the member not actually holding **CONTRIBUTE** on the calloutsSet policy (the privilege rule expands only privileges granted on that same policy), e.g. the member credential → CONTRIBUTE rule not cascading to the calloutsSet;
3. `myPrivileges` resolution not applying privilege-rule expansion for this policy.

## Verification

As the affected member:

```graphql
query($id: UUID!) {
  lookup { calloutsSet(ID: $id) { authorization { myPrivileges } } }
}
```

With the setting ON, `myPrivileges` must contain `CONTRIBUTE` and `CREATE_CALLOUT`. Whichever of the two is missing identifies the broken link ((2) vs (1)/(3) above). If both are present, the bug would move to client-web — but given the direct `includes()` gate there, that is unlikely.
t: Space member lacks CREATE_CALLOUT on the calloutsSet despite allowMembersToCreateCallouts ON — Add post button hidden

## Description
As a Space or Subspace admin
I want to add a **Form** to a Post, define its questions, decide who can see the responses, and review what came in
So that I can structure the input I'm asking my community for, keep sensitive answers away from the whole Space, and act on them

## Acceptance criteria

**Creating the Form**
- [ ] "Form" is offered as a framing option in the existing create/edit-Post flow, only to admins of the Space or Subspace the Post lives in
- [ ] The server rejects creating a Form, or switching an existing Post to a Form, by anyone without admin rights there — also when members are allowed to create Posts
- [ ] The server rejects a Form in a Virtual Contributor knowledge base
- [ ] I can add, edit, reorder and remove questions; each question has a prompt, an optional explanation and a required flag
- [ ] Publishing is blocked with a clear message if the Form has no questions
- [ ] V1 questions are plain text with a default length limit (answer types are server#6434, after V1)

**Settings**
- [ ] Response visibility is set in the Form settings dialogue: **Admins only** (default) or **Space members**
- [ ] "Space members" never includes anonymous visitors or non-members, also on a public Space
- [ ] Once a response exists, visibility can only be narrowed (Space members → Admins only), never widened; the dialogue explains why the option is unavailable
- [ ] The visibility setting is clearly shown on the Form to a respondent before they submit
- [ ] The admin can choose single or multiple responses per member

**Viewing responses**
- [ ] Admins of the Space/Subspace can open a single response and see all responses at once (Figma: "Seeing Response", "Seeing All Responses")
- [ ] Admins of a parent Space can read responses too, as they can read draft Posts today
- [ ] Admins can download all responses as a CSV file (one row per response: submitter, submitted date, one column per question); the export guards against spreadsheet formula injection

**Lifecycle**
- [ ] Questions have a stable identity, so editing a Form that already has responses never rewrites or deletes them
- [ ] Removed questions keep their collected answers; added questions apply to new submissions only
- [ ] Deleting a Form Post that has responses asks for confirmation and states how many responses will be deleted
- [ ] Until server#6435, a Form Post is left out when a template is created from it or from its Space, as Polls are today

## Additional Context
- The existing `Form` entity (used for application forms) stores questions as a JSON array without IDs, and its `required`/`maxLength` are not enforced on submit — both need addressing if it is reused.
- Admin-only framing guard precedent: `assertAdminOnlyCollaborationFraming` (callouts-set create) and the Contributors guard on update.
- Design: [Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/pC2rRylUzu88mxGb0Zdffl/Forms-on-Callouts-%E2%80%94-Dev-Handoff--Spec-011-?node-id=0-1&t=s3npL6TevJIRSz9p-1) — "Form Settings dialogue", "Seeing Response", "Seeing All Responses"
- Spec: `alkem-io/agents-hq` → form-callout-framing spec (PR alkem-io/agents-hq#62), US1, US3, US4a · FR-001–FR-005, FR-017–FR-021, FR-028–FR-029

## Areas that will be affected
server (framing type, Form reuse, guards, response queries, export data); client-web (issue to be filed)
t: Form Post: create a Form Post, view and export its responses

I want to fill in and submit a response to a Form
So that I can give the admin the information they asked for, in the shape they need it, knowing who will read it

## Description

**As a** product owner tracking Task board adoption
**I want** task boards, tasks, and task replies to emit their own contribution-event types
**So that** Kibana can tell a Tasks board apart from an ordinary Posts callout, a task apart from a post, and a reply-to-a-task apart from a reply-to-a-post — instead of all six collapsing into `CALLOUT_CREATED` / `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED` / `CALLOUT_POST_COMMENT_CREATED`.

### Why this is invisible today

A Tasks board is not a new entity — it is an ordinary **POSTS callout** whose classification carries the reserved `task` tagset (`TagsetReservedName.TASK`), and a task is an ordinary **POST contribution** whose own classification carries the same tagset naming its column. That design choice (workspace spec `042-kanban-task-board`) is deliberate and good, but it means the board inherits the entire post analytics pipeline and emits nothing of its own:

| Action | Contribution event today | Distinguishable? |
|---|---|---|
| Create a Tasks board | `CALLOUT_CREATED` | ❌ identical to any callout |
| Create a task | `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED` | ❌ identical to a post |
| Reply to a task | `CALLOUT_POST_COMMENT_CREATED` | ❌ identical to a post reply |

So today every board inflates the callout count, every task inflates the post count, and every task discussion inflates the post-engagement count. There is no field on the indexed document to filter on afterwards — the reporter records the post/callout id, the display name and the space, and nothing about the board.

Spec `042` explicitly scoped board analytics out of the MVP ("no notifications, no activity-feed additions"), so nothing is broken. This story adds the missing slice.

---

## Scope

Add three values to `CONTRIBUTION_TYPE` and emit them at the three existing report sites. **No new table, no migration, no GraphQL schema change** — this is purely additive instrumentation on paths that already report.

### 1. `TASK_BOARD_CREATED` — board vs. ordinary callout

**Where:** `src/domain/collaboration/callouts-set/callouts.set.resolver.mutations.ts` (~L373)

Emit **in addition to** `CALLOUT_CREATED`, exactly mirroring the `CALLOUT_POLL_CREATED` precedent already sitting ten lines below it (L386). Gate on `TaskBoardService.isTaskBoard(callout)`; `name` stays `callout.nameID` to match `calloutCreated`.

The callout is already loaded with `classification: { tagsets: { tagsetTemplate: true } }` on this path, so `isTaskBoard()` needs no extra query — please confirm during implementation.

### 2. `TASK_CREATED` — task vs. post

**Where:** `src/domain/collaboration/callout/callout.resolver.mutations.ts` → `processActivityPostCreated` (~L863)

Branch on the **contribution's own** classification, not the callout's: `contribution.classification?.tagsets` containing `TagsetReservedName.TASK`. That marker is built in memory by `buildTaskClassification` (`callout-contribution/callout.contribution.service.ts:233`) during the same mutation, so the branch costs **zero extra queries**. Using the contribution rather than the callout is also more precise — it is the per-row truth, and it is the same predicate `TaskBoardMoveService` already uses (`task.board.move.service.ts:74-76`).

⚠️ **Verify** that `contribution.classification` survives the `calloutContributionService.save(contribution)` at `callout.resolver.mutations.ts:552`. If TypeORM drops the cascaded relation off the returned entity, capture the flag *before* the save, or add `classification: { tagsets: true }` to the reload — do not add a fresh round-trip.

Emit `TASK_CREATED` **instead of** `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED`, not alongside it. See "Decision" below.

### 3. `TASK_COMMENT_CREATED` — task reply vs. post reply

**Where:** `src/domain/communication/room/room.service.events.ts` → `processActivityPostComment` (~L292)

Only `post` and `room` are in scope here, so this one **does** need a load: `Post.contribution` (the inverse `OneToOne` at `post/post.entity.ts:22-24`) → `contribution.classification.tagsets`. One relation hop. This method already performs two async resolver lookups (`getCommunityFromPostRoomOrFail`, `getLevelZeroSpaceIdForCommunity`), so one more is proportionate — but load it in the same query as an existing lookup if you can rather than adding a third await.

Keep `name` as the post display name, as today.

---

## Decision required before merge

**`TASK_CREATED` replaces `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED` for tasks; it is not emitted in addition.**

That is what makes the post count clean, and it is the recommended behaviour — but it is a **deliberate semantic break** in the `contribution-events` series:

- Every existing dashboard counting `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED` will step down on deploy day by however many posts were actually tasks.
- **Historical data cannot be backfilled from Elasticsearch alone.** Documents already indexed carry no board marker; a backfill would need a join against Postgres (`callout_contribution.classificationId` → tagset named `task`). Not recommended.
- Recommended instead: record the deploy date and treat it as a documented series break in the affected Kibana dashboards.

If the analytics owner would rather keep `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED` as a stable superset, say so on this issue before implementation — emitting both is a one-line difference in the same branch, but it means the post count stays inflated and every consumer has to subtract.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Should add `TASK_BOARD_CREATED`, `TASK_CREATED` and `TASK_COMMENT_CREATED` to `CONTRIBUTION_TYPE` (`src/services/external/elasticsearch/types/contribution.type.ts`)
- [ ] Should add the three matching `ContributionReporterService` methods, following the existing single-actor `createDocument` shape (no new document fields — same `{id, name, space}` + author details)
- [x] Should emit `TASK_BOARD_CREATED` alongside `CALLOUT_CREATED` when a created callout is a Tasks board
- [x] Should emit `TASK_CREATED` **instead of** `CALLOUT_POST_CREATED` when the new contribution carries the reserved `task` classification
- [x] Should emit `TASK_COMMENT_CREATED` **instead of** `CALLOUT_POST_COMMENT_CREATED` when the commented post is a task
- [ ] Should leave an ordinary posts callout, post and post comment emitting exactly the events they emit today — no regression
- [ ] Should not change the activity feed, notifications, or any GraphQL contract
- [ ] Should not add a query to the task-creation path (the marker is already in memory)
- [ ] Should cover all three branches with unit tests, both sides of each (board/not-board, task/not-task)
- [ ] Should be verified on acceptance by finding the three new `type` values in `contribution-events-acc`

**Verification hook:** acceptance runs `SERVER_LOGGING_LEVEL: verbose`, so the reporter logs `Event 'TASK_CREATED' for object with id '(…)' ingested to (contribution-events-acc)` on success. Production runs at `warn` and will log nothing on the happy path — expected, not a fault.

---

## Notes for getting the data into analytics

The server change alone puts the new types into Elasticsearch, but they will render **without a human-readable label** until the reporting side is updated. That work lives in the private `alkem-io/reporting-orchestration` repo and is **not** part of this ticket — file it there, but it must land in the same window or the Kibana dashboards show blank type labels.

**1. Add the label rows.** `contributionstype-labels` is a plain lookup index (`.scripts/contribution-events/contributionstype-labels-index-content`). Add:

```
{ "type": "TASK_BOARD_CREATED",   "contributionType": "Task Board Created" }
{ "type": "TASK_CREATED",         "contributionType": "Task Created" }
{ "type": "TASK_COMMENT_CREATED", "contributionType": "Task Commented" }
```

**2. Re-execute the enrich policy — this is the step that gets forgotten.**

```
POST /_enrich/policy/contribution-type-enrich-policy/_execute
```

There is **no cronjob** for this policy. Only `space_name_enrich_policy_from_alkemio-data-spaces` is refreshed automatically (`execute-enrich-space-names`, `@daily`). An enrich policy serves from a frozen snapshot taken at execute time, so until it is re-run the new rows are invisible to the pipeline.

**3. Know how it fails.** It fails *silently*. The `contribution_events_spaceName` ingest pipeline's contribution-type `enrich` processor has no `on_failure` branch and the following `rename` is `ignore_missing: true` — so an unmatched `type` simply produces a document with **no `contributionType` field at all**. No error, no log line, just a blank column in Kibana. If the new types show up blank, this step is why.

**4. Fix the pre-existing drift while you are in there.** `contributionstype-labels` is already well out of date and this is a cheap moment to reconcile it:
- **Missing ~15 currently-emitted types:** `SUBSPACE_CONTENT_EDITED`, `CALLOUT_MEMO_CREATED`, `CALLOUT_WHITEBOARD_EDITED`, `CALENDAR_EVENT_CREATED`, `MEMO_CONTRIBUTION`, `OFFICE_DOCUMENT_CONTRIBUTION`, `OFFICE_DOCUMENT_VIEW`, `COLLABORA_DOCUMENT_CREATED` / `_UPLOADED` / `_REPLACED` / `_OPENED`, `MEDIA_GALLERY_CONTRIBUTION`, `CALLOUT_POLL_CREATED`, `POLL_VOTE_CONTRIBUTION`, `POLL_RESPONSE_ADDED_CONTRIBUTION` — all of these are already rendering blank today.
- **6 dead rows** for types the server no longer emits: `CHALLENGE_JOINED` / `_CREATED` / `_CONTENT_EDITED`, `OPPORTUNITY_JOINED` / `_CREATED` / `_CONTENT_EDITED`.

**5. Query the enriched index, not the raw one.** `contribution-events-with-names-v2` is where `spaceName` and `contributionType` exist; the transform is a `latest` transform with a 120s sync delay and needs no change for new types. Note that this enrichment chain is **production-only** — acceptance writes to `contribution-events-acc` with no enriched counterpart, so verify the *emission* on acceptance and the *labels* on production.

**6. Index template.** `contribution-events-space-name` (`.scripts/northstar/`, priority 500) maps its properties explicitly. Nothing to change for this ticket — but if the follow-ups below add a `column` field, add it to the template as `keyword` rather than letting dynamic mapping make it `text` + `.keyword`.

### Follow-ups this ticket deliberately leaves out

These complete the picture but are separate stories — please file rather than scope-creep:

- **`TASK_MOVED`** from `TaskBoardResolverMutations.moveTaskToColumn`, carrying the destination column. This is the single highest-value addition: it unlocks column throughput, time-to-Done, and cycle time. Today a move emits *nothing at all* — not a contribution event, not an activity row, not a notification — and the only trace it leaves anywhere is an APM transaction named `[mutation] MoveTaskToColumn` with no arguments (`ENABLE_GLOBAL_INSTRUMENTATION` is off, so no span carries the ids).
- **A `column` field on the task documents**, so a Kibana terms aggregation can render actual board state over time. Requires the index-template edit in note 6.
- **Column CRUD events** (`CreateTaskColumnOnCallout` / `Update` / `Delete` / `UpdateTaskColumnsSortOrder`) — lower value, currently also entirely unreported.

### Related known analytics defects

Both affect these new types the same way they affect the existing ones, and neither is in scope here:
- #5447 — subspace id instead of space id in the `contribution-events` index
- #5885 — guest users counted as Alkemio team users (the `alkemio` flag)

---

## Areas that will be affected

- `src/services/external/elasticsearch/types/contribution.type.ts`
- `src/services/external/elasticsearch/contribution-reporter/contribution.reporter.service.ts`
- `src/services/external/elasticsearch/events/` (new event types, mirroring `callout.post.created.ts`)
- `src/domain/collaboration/callouts-set/callouts.set.resolver.mutations.ts`
- `src/domain/collaboration/callout/callout.resolver.mutations.ts`
- `src/domain/communication/room/room.service.events.ts`
- Downstream, **not in this repo**: `alkem-io/reporting-orchestration` (label rows + enrich policy execute)

## Context

- Workspace spec: `agents-hq/specs/042-kanban-task-board/` — see "Out of Scope", which is why this gap exists
- Board delivery: epic alkem-io/alkemio#2007, server#6390, client-web#10169
- `LogContext.TASKS` (`context: "tasks"` in Kibana) is the **background job service** in `src/services/task/` and is unrelated to the Task board — do not reuse it for board logging. Board mutations log under `LogContext.COLLABORATION`.
t: Task board analytics: distinguish boards, tasks and task replies in contribution-events

**Summary:** text drawn inside a whiteboard is no longer found by search — global search or the new sidebar search widget. It was, until #6193.

**Since:** #6193 (`feat: collaboration persistence + collaborative content → per-document file storage (003+006)`, merged 2026-08-25). First tag containing it: `v0.163.0` (Release 73) — so this is already in production and is **not** a Release 74 regression. Noticed during the Release 74 acceptance walk of the sidebar search widget (client-web#10167, `workspace#055`), 2026-09-03.

**Before #6193** (`src/services/api/search/ingest/search.ingest.service.ts`):
- the ingest loaded `whiteboard.content`, extracted every Excalidraw text element via `extractTextFromWhiteboardContent` / `isExcalidrawTextElement`, and indexed that text for framing whiteboards **and** whiteboard contributions;
- whiteboards without any text were skipped ("only whiteboards with content are ingested").

**After #6193:**
- the scene lives only as a Yjs-V2 snapshot in the document's bucket; the ingest selects `contentPointer` instead of `content`, and the code comment states: *"the scene-text body is no longer indexed. Whiteboards are indexed by their profile (name/description/tags)"*;
- **memos** received a replacement in the same PR — searchable markdown derived from their snapshot, keyed by `contentPointer` (`markdownByPointer`) — whiteboards did not.

**Impact:** a user who remembers a word written on a whiteboard cannot find that whiteboard (or its callout) by searching; only its title, description and tags match. Applies to every search surface. No spec ruling or issue records the drop as intentional — the only trace is the code comment.

**Suggested fix shape:** mirror the memo path — derive the scene's text elements from the Yjs-V2 snapshot at ingest (keyed by `contentPointer`) and index them as before, so `extractTextFromWhiteboardContent`'s behaviour is restored on the new storage. Re-ingest after deploy so existing whiteboards catch up.

**Reproduce (any env ≥ 0.163.0):** create a whiteboard in a Space, draw the text `quasar055` inside it, wait for (or trigger) ingest, search `quasar055` → 0 results; search the whiteboard's title → found.

**Observed (production, 2026-09-04, after the Release 74 deploy):** the new sidebar search widget (`workspace#055`, client-web#10167) returns **no results inside Spaces whose visibility is `DEMO`** — every term answers "0 items", on every tab.

**Not a regression — an existing rule made visible.** Since #4972 (2025-02-24, "Only show active spaces in the search results") the search **ingest** reads only Spaces with `visibility = ACTIVE` — `fetchSpacesLevel0`/`fetchSpacesLevel0Count` and the sibling fetchers for subspaces, callouts, posts, whiteboards, memos and documents all filter on `SpaceVisibility.ACTIVE` (`src/services/api/search/ingest/search.ingest.service.ts`). Content of `DEMO` (and `INACTIVE`) Spaces is therefore **never indexed**; the exclusion happens at ingest time, not at query time. The old Knowledge-Base search made the same call and had the same result; with 055 a search field now sits on every tab of every Space, so a demo Space shows a working-looking field that can never find anything.

**Intent worth keeping:** demo Spaces should stay out of platform-wide discovery (global search). **Intent this breaks:** a member browsing *inside* a demo Space cannot search its own content.

**Suggested change (server-side):**
1. Ingest Spaces of all visibilities (drop the `ACTIVE` filter in the fetchers). Every document already carries `license.visibility` — the ingest stamps it — so nothing new needs to be indexed.
2. Enforce the "active only" rule in the **global** search query (filter `license.visibility = active` when no Space scope is given), and **skip** it when the request is scoped with `searchInSpaceFilter` — the user is already inside that Space, so its own visibility gate has been passed.
3. Re-ingest after deploy (`adminSearchIngestFromScratch`) so existing demo content appears.

Existing coverage to keep green: `test-suites` › `server-api/src/functional-api/search/search.it-spec.ts` › *Search Archived Space Data* (archived Spaces hidden from non-admins in global search; GA sees them). A new case should assert: global search excludes demo-Space content; Space-scoped search inside a demo Space returns it.

**Release 74 note:** recorded as a known limitation; the 055 acceptance walk used ACTIVE Spaces only, so this was not caught before production. Related: alkem-io/alkemio#2111.
t: Search inside a DEMO space returns nothing — ingest indexes ACTIVE spaces only; apply the active-only rule to global search at query time instead

## Summary

`ActorContext` cache invalidation can lose a race with an in-flight read: a request for an actor whose credentials just changed (role grant, revoke, authentication-ID clear) may already have fetched the actor from the DB and be about to write it to the cache. If that write lands after `ActorContextCacheService` deletes the entry, a stale `ActorContext` stays cached until the TTL expires.

## Observed symptom

Observed live on a local stack while verifying `workspace#061-organization-space-invitations` (branch `server-4100`):

1. Assign a user the ADMIN role on a Space role set (`assignRoleToUser`).
2. Immediately call `inviteForEntryRoleOnRoleSet` as that user.
3. Intermittently the call fails the `ROLESET_ENTRY_ROLE_INVITE` check with the cached actor still missing the just-granted credential. An identical retry moments later succeeds once the stale entry ages out.

## Where

- `ActorContextCacheService` (single `del` on invalidate)
- Call sites: `ActorService.grantCredentialOrFail`, `revokeCredential`, `deleteActorById`, `UserService` authentication-ID clear and settings/status update paths.

## Notes

A fix that deleted the entry twice (immediately and again after a short race-guard delay) was prototyped during the 061 verification run and deliberately **not** shipped with that feature: it is a pre-existing platform race and the delayed re-delete is a timing band-aid rather than a root-cause fix (e.g. versioning the cache entry, or invalidating after the read completes / not caching mid-mutation). Filed so it gets a proper owner and a discriminating test.

Refs: `agents-hq` spec `specs/061-organization-space-invitations/forge-run.md` (verification fix-round history).
t: ActorContext cache invalidation races with in-flight reads (stale credentials after role grant)

<!-- gh issue create -R alkem-io/server --title "Decide how the AI assistant's MCP whiteboard session counts against the multi-user whiteboard licence (and surface the room's read-only reason)" --label "user story",server,"Atlas Team" --body-file docs/issue-draft-mcp-assistant-multiuser-licence-story.md -->

## Description

As a space member using the web AI assistant on a space **without** the multi-user whiteboard licence
I want to keep a whiteboard open in my browser and ask the assistant to edit it
So that the primary assistant whiteboard flow ("I'm looking at this board — add/change X") works on every space, or I am told clearly why it doesn't

### Background (observed on acc, 2026-09-04)

The MCP `edit_whiteboard_elements` tool joins the whiteboard's collaboration room as a **second collaborator** (delegated on behalf of the user). The collaboration service's read-only calculation (`collaborative-document-service` › `authentication.factory.ts` › `calculateReadOnlyState`) has three read-only outcomes: `noUpdateAccess`, `multiUserNotAllowed` (a collaborator is already in the room and the space has no multi-user licence), `roomCapacityReached`. So on an unlicensed space:

1. user opens the board in the browser → occupies the single editor slot;
2. user asks the assistant to edit it → MCP session gets `read-only-state / session-mode` with `multiUserNotAllowed`;
3. the server's `edit_whiteboard_elements` maps `ReadOnlyRoomError` to **`Access denied: you do not have permission to edit this whiteboard.`** — the same string it uses for a genuinely missing `UPDATE_CONTENT` privilege — and drops the room's reason (`src/services/mcp-server/tools/edit-whiteboard-elements.tool.ts:219-222`).

Verified end-to-end: with the board open in the browser every MCP edit was refused; sibling boards on the same space (not open anywhere) accepted edits from the same user; after the space was given the multi-user whiteboard licence the same board accepted edits again with the tab still open.

Two questions fall out of this, and they need an explicit product decision rather than the current accidental behaviour:

- **Licence semantics:** should the assistant acting *on behalf of* a user count as a second human collaborator? Options: (a) yes — an unlicensed space gets an assistant that can only edit boards nobody has open (current behaviour, but then it must be explained to the user); (b) no — the delegated session is treated as the same user / an exempt system collaborator and does not consume a licence slot; (c) the assistant is a licensed feature and its edits are blocked (with a clear upsell message) unless the space has the licence.
- **Error surfacing:** regardless of (a)/(b)/(c), the MCP tool must not report a licence/room condition as a permissions failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A written decision (a / b / c above, or another) is recorded for how the delegated assistant session counts against `multiUserNotAllowed` and `roomCapacityReached`, and the collaboration service + server implement it.
- [ ] Should return a distinct, actionable MCP error for each room read-only reason, e.g. `This space's licence allows one editor at a time and the whiteboard is currently open elsewhere` for `multiUserNotAllowed`, `The whiteboard has reached its maximum number of simultaneous editors` for `roomCapacityReached`, keeping `Access denied…` only for `noUpdateAccess` / missing `UPDATE_CONTENT`.
- [ ] Should include the machine-readable reason code (`readOnlyCode`) in the MCP tool's error payload so the web assistant UI can render the right message / call to action.
- [ ] Should behave identically for `create_whiteboard` / `create_whiteboard_in_space` if they ever join a room, and for memo edits if/when an MCP memo edit tool exists.
- [ ] Should be covered by a spec that drives `ReadOnlyRoomError` with each `readOnlyCode` through `edit_whiteboard_elements` and asserts the distinct messages.
- [ ] QA: on acc, an unlicensed space with a board open in the browser → assistant edit yields the licence message (or succeeds, per decision); after assigning the licence → assistant edit succeeds with the tab open.

## Additional Context

- Reproduction space on acc: `zimbabve` (`8fb70b2d-9908-4f8b-b8e1-fb2b1d0de0b1`), board "New Whiteboard321" (`986c0b3e-3c04-4daa-88b6-7a8e286bffb2`).
- Server: `src/services/collaboration-client/collaboration-document.session.ts` (`read-only-state` / `session-mode` handling, `ReadOnlyRoomError` carries `readOnlyReason`), `src/services/collaboration-client/collaboration-document.service.ts:104` (throws on `isReadOnly()`), `src/services/mcp-server/tools/edit-whiteboard-elements.tool.ts:186-222`.
- Collaboration service: `src/hocuspocus/extensions/authentication/read.only.code.ts`, `authentication.factory.ts` (`calculateReadOnlyState`).
- Related bugs found in the same MCP QA pass: #6462, #6463, and the empty-text-element bug (filed alongside this story).

## Areas that will be affected

_To be added during the refinement_
t: Decide how the AI assistant's MCP whiteboard session counts against the multi-user whiteboard licence (and surface the room's read-only reason)

**Describe the bug**
`search_content` matches of type `space` and `subspace` come back without a `displayName`, while `callout`, `post`, `memo`, `whiteboard` and `collabora_document` matches have one. The same is true for `user` and `organization` matches. An MCP client that wants to show a space picker from search results has nothing to label the entries with except the last path segment of the `url`.

Reported by an external integrator building on the MCP server; confirmed on acc on 2026-09-04.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Connect any MCP client (Claude Code was used) to `https://acc-alkem.io/rest/mcp` with header `Authorization: Bearer mcp_…`.
2. Call `search_content` with `{ "query": "QA and Testing", "limit": 10 }` (any query that hits spaces).
3. See space/subspace matches shaped like `{"type":"subspace","id":"56d8293e-…","score":49.4,"spaceId":"56d8293e-…","url":"https://acc-alkem.io/un-sdgs/challenges/water/opportunities/water-sanit"}` and `{"type":"space","id":"e43554fa-…","score":32.1,"spaceId":"e43554fa-…","url":"https://acc-alkem.io/memosandwbs"}` — no `displayName`.
4. In the same response, callout/post/memo matches carry `"displayName":"Dev-QA Testing 101"` etc.
5. `user` (`{"type":"user","id":"b024c1f4-…","score":15.9,"url":"https://acc-alkem.io/user/qa-user-1700"}`) and `organization` matches also lack `displayName`.

**Expected behavior**
Every match carries `displayName` (space: `about.profile.displayName`; user/organization: `profile.displayName`), so a client can label results — in particular build a space picker for public spaces the user is not a member of, where search is the only discovery route (member spaces are already listed with names by `community_activity_summary`).

**Screenshots**
N/A — JSON above.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: N/A — server-side `/rest/mcp` endpoint
- Browser: N/A (MCP client: Claude Code)
- Version: acc on 2026-09-04; latest tag at time of writing `v0.163.5`

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**

- N/A

**Additional context**

*Root cause (code):* the MCP tool already tries to read the name — `src/services/mcp-server/tools/search-content.tool.ts` `toMatch()` (≈line 192):

```ts
const displayName =
  entity?.profile?.displayName ??
  r.callout?.framing?.profile?.displayName ??
  r.space?.about?.profile?.displayName;
```

but the entities it receives are hydrated by `src/services/api/search/result/search.result.service.ts` with bare lookups and **no relations**: spaces via `entityManager.findBy(Space, { id: In(spaceIds) })` / `findOneByOrFail(Space, { id })` (≈lines 212–222), users via `findBy(User, …)` (≈line 332), organizations via `findBy(Organization, …)` (≈line 376). So `space.about` / `user.profile` / `organization.profile` are undefined and the tool emits no name. The GraphQL `search` query does not notice because its field resolvers lazy-load `about`/`profile` per result; the MCP tool serialises the bare entity directly. Callouts/posts/memos/whiteboards are hydrated with their profile relations, which is why those matches have a name.

*Suggested fix:* load `about.profile` for spaces and `profile` for users/organizations in the search result hydration (or hydrate them in the MCP tool before mapping), and add a spec asserting `displayName` on every match type in `search-content.tool.spec.ts`.

*Impact:* MCP/assistant clients cannot label space, user or organization search results; the reporter is currently deriving labels from the URL slug.

## Description

`server#4100` (organization → Space invitations) implements the product instruction that accepting an invitation must not produce a double notification:

> Accepting an invite/application shouldn't trigger a double notification (one for X accepted, immediately followed by X joined). The "joined" notification should only fire when there was **no invitation or application step**.

For **invitations** this works: the generic `SPACE_ADMIN_COMMUNITY_NEW_MEMBER` ("a new member joined") is suppressed, and the dedicated invitation-response notification takes its place and reaches **every** admin of the Space.

For **applications** there is nothing to take its place. `NotificationEvent` carries:

- `SPACE_ADMIN_COMMUNITY_APPLICATION` — fired when an application is **submitted**
- `USER_SPACE_COMMUNITY_APPLICATION_DECLINED` — fired to the applicant on decline

…and **no application-approved event at all**.

So on `server-4100` as it stands:

> Space with admins A, B and C. A approves an application. B and C receive **nothing** — no email, no in-app, no push — where on `develop` they received all three.

This is a silent, platform-wide behaviour change to a flow `server#4100` does not otherwise touch, and it is the opposite of what the instruction asks for: "shouldn't trigger a *double* notification" presumes a replacement exists. Zero is not one.

## Why it shipped this way

This was decided twice, in opposite directions, and the second decision is the one on the branch:

| Ruling | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **R31** (2026-09-08) | Suppress invitations only; applications keep notifying | No application-approved event exists to replace the suppressed one, so suppressing leaves co-admins with nothing |
| **R35** (2026-09-09) | Suppress applications too — **supersedes R31** | R31 was defensible but overrode a binding product instruction, and recorded that override only in a code comment. The instruction wins; the consequence is accepted and tracked (this issue) |

R35 is correct against the source-of-truth order (product email → this epic's stories → spec). The gap it accepts is what this issue exists to close.

- [ ] New notification event `SPACE_ADMIN_COMMUNITY_APPLICATION_APPROVED` (name TBC), fired when an application is approved, to **every admin of the Space** — not only the admin who approved it, and not only the application's original recipient
- [ ] The admin who performed the approval is excluded on all three channels (they performed the action — same rule as R33 for invitation outcomes)
- [ ] Delivered on all three channels: email, in-app, push
- [ ] Governed by a user notification setting. **Product decision needed** — reuse `space.admin.communityInvitationResponse` ("someone responded to an invitation"), which is arguably wrong since an application approval is not a response to an invitation; or add a third row; or fold it back under `space.admin.communityNewMember`. - [ ] Live it-spec proving co-admins are notified on approval, and that the approver is not

Whichever is chosen, the migration must not silently re-enable an event a Space admin had deliberately muted — the `communityInvitationResponse` row already had to be backfilled from its predecessor `communityNewMember` for exactly this reason (ruling R27a).
2. **Should the applicant be told they were approved?** Out of scope for the regression itself, but the symmetric gap: `USER_SPACE_COMMUNITY_APPLICATION_DECLINED` exists and has no approved counterpart either.

**Describe the bug**

The `OWNER` role on an Organization declares `userPolicyData: { minimum: 1, maximum: 3 }` in `src/domain/community/organization/definitions/organization.role.definitions.ts`, but that minimum is never enforced. Organizations can be created with no owner and stay that way indefinitely. On production roughly **295 of ~702 organizations (~42%) currently have no owner**, in breach of the declared policy.

The same gap affects `maximum` — several organizations exceed the declared max of 3 for ADMIN and OWNER (one has 9 admins and 7 owners).

**To Reproduce**

1. Authenticate against `https://alkem.io/api/private/graphql` as a platform admin.
2. Run:

```graphql
query OrgRoleCoverage {
  organizations {
    id
    nameID
    profile { displayName url }
    roleSet {
      owners: usersInRole(role: OWNER) { id }
      admins: usersInRole(role: ADMIN) { id }
      associates: usersInRole(role: ASSOCIATE) { id }
    }
  }
}
```

3. Count organizations where `owners` is an empty array.
4. Observe that ~295 organizations return zero owners, despite `minimum: 1`.

Alternatively, create a new Organization through the normal flow and query its `roleSet` — no owner is assigned and no error is raised.

**Expected behavior**

An Organization should not be able to exist with fewer owners than its role definition declares. Either the creation flow assigns an owner (e.g. the creating user), or creation fails with a policy violation. Organizations already below the minimum should be reportable so they can be remediated.

**Screenshots**

N/A — server-side data integrity issue.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

N/A — reproduced via the GraphQL API, not browser-specific.

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**

N/A

**Additional context**

**Root cause.** The minimum is enforced only on *removal*, in `src/domain/access/role-set/role.set.service.ts:1219`:

```ts
if (userMembersCount === userPolicy.minimum) {
  // "Min limit of users reached for role ... cannot remove user from role"
}
```

Two consequences:

1. **No check at creation.** Nothing requires an owner when an Organization is created, so an org can enter the estate below its own declared minimum.
2. **The guard uses exact equality.** An org already at zero owners does not satisfy `0 === 1`, so the protection never engages for exactly the organizations already in breach. The rule only bites at exactly one owner.

No migration appears to have backfilled owners onto organizations created before the OWNER role existed, which likely explains the bulk of the 295.

**Current state on production** (platform-admin sweep; manual tally, approximate ±5):

| Bucket | Count | Share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owner + admin | ~407 | 58% |
| Admin, no owner | ~118 | 17% |
| Associates only — no owner, no admin | 8 | 1% |
| No roles at all | ~169 | 24% |
| **Total organizations** | **~702** | |

There is no organization with an owner but no admin — owners are a strict subset of admin-having orgs. That is incidental, not enforced.

**Impact.** `OWNER` and `ADMIN` both grant the implicit account-admin credential (`role.set.service.ts:747`), so a missing owner is invisible day to day — an admin can already do most of what an owner can. It surfaces at the point it is most expensive, offboarding. Two concrete cases:

- **8 organizations have members but neither an owner nor an admin.** Nobody can manage membership or edit the profile. The largest has 12 members. These users are blocked today.
- **A single user account is the sole owner of ~313 municipality (`gemeente-*`) organizations**, and a second single account is the sole or primary admin across roughly the same set. Because the removal guard *does* fire at one owner, offboarding that account would refuse each of those ~313 removals until a replacement owner is added per organization, and there is no bulk path for that in the API today.

**Suggested scope**

1. Enforce at creation — require or auto-assign an owner so no new org enters below minimum.
2. Change the removal guard from `===` to `<=` so orgs already below minimum are not silently unprotected.
3. Report and remediate the existing ~295 — a backfill where an unambiguous candidate exists (e.g. sole admin), or a platform-admin view listing orgs in breach. The 8 associates-only orgs should go first; they are the only ones where users are blocked right now.
4. Consider a bulk owner-reassignment path for offboarding, given the concentration above.

**Note on figures:** counts come from a manual pass over the query output and are approximate; the 8 associates-only organizations were read individually and are exact. Happy to re-run and attach precise numbers.

**Areas that will be affected as part of the fix**

_Optional, to be added by developer if relevant_
t: BUG: Organization OWNER minimum (1) is not enforced — ~295 organizations have no owner

## Problem

Existing memos can retain image references whose file-service metadata row still exists but whose backing bytes are missing. The memo remains editable, but preparing its signing PDF fails when the renderer reads the missing image.

Production example investigated read-only on 2026-09-11:
- Memo: https://alkem.io/qatesting/collaboration/memoe/memoa
- Memo ID: `8a802095-5ecb-40ac-95fe-52651050324d`.
- Referenced image document: `019ecbe0-887c-766f-9471-6b2a12325208` (`MEDIA_GALLERY_IMAGE (11).jpeg`). Its metadata row exists in the memo's storage bucket; its backing file was confirmed absent with a read-only filesystem check.
- File-service returned HTTP 404 `file not found on storage`; PDF preparation consequently failed with `File service HTTP error` before starting a gateway signing session.

This is separate from the production Kratos scope/context problem, which the user reports is now fixed and signing works. It is also separate from the serializer/layout fix in #6490.

## Requested change

Add an explicit memo sanitization/repair path for genuinely missing image references, following the Whiteboard media recovery/salvage precedent from the Yjs transition in #6420 (merge `029643064bc57c1fee26d082030d059db68c398f`). Reuse its failure taxonomy and established persistence/concurrency conventions where applicable; do not create a second migration framework.

Precedent: `CollaborationMigrationService.resolveWhiteboardAssetLocators` and `removeUnrecoverableLiveImages` recover available content, remove only unrecoverable live image references, preserve unrelated content, and report visual loss. Metadata existence alone is not proof that the backing image exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- A read-only dry run identifies affected memos and image references and reports proposed repairs without changing content or storage.
- Recover an image through an existing supported source when possible. When absence is confirmed and no supported recovery source exists, explicitly authorized repair removes only the affected image nodes/references and reports the visual loss.
- Missing metadata and metadata-with-missing-bytes are both covered. Authorization failures, timeouts, network errors, 5xx responses and malformed responses must not be classified as proof of missing content or cause image removal.
- Preserve all valid images and unrelated memo text, paragraph/list/table structure and formatting. Use the established Yjs persistence path; do not overwrite concurrent edits with a stale snapshot. Re-running a completed repair is harmless.
- Do not silently omit images only in the signing renderer: the repaired memo, preview and newly signed copy must agree. Existing signed PDFs remain untouched.
- Regression tests cover missing backing bytes with an existing metadata row, missing metadata, recoverable/valid images, repeated references, transient-error non-removal, preservation of unrelated structure and dry-run zero writes. Preparing the repaired memo's PDF succeeds without the stale image reference.

## Execution boundary

This ticket records follow-up work only. No production repair, memo edit, file removal or signing retry was performed during the investigation. Production application of any repair requires separate explicit authorization.
t: Sanitize memos with missing image content, following Whiteboard Yjs salvage

Table-containing Markdown with one or more images produces Yjs image nodes retaining `src`, `alt`, `title`, `width`, and `height` as applicable. Add a round-trip regression covering the combined table/image shape and audit the live creation/import callers before changing behavior.

Discovered while correcting the performance fixture in #6505. Exact test evidence is retained in that PR discussion/body; no production or acceptance data was used.
t: Markdown-to-Yjs projection drops image attributes in table-containing Markdown
